Theta0 = a sin th (1 - 2 cos^2 th) has simple zeros at pi/4, 3 pi/4; it fails transport; so the consequence of (e) and
3.30(vii) that every exact profile whose Theta0 has a zero in (0, pi) has a multiple or flat zero of Theta0 there uses
transport essentially. The checker confirmed this example by direct full-plane inversion at three resolutions (strain
c = -1 to 1.2e-13); along the far nodal ray th = pi/4 its residual tends to -6 sqrt(2)/7, while |R|/N_v tends to 1 and
|R|/N_f tends to 0 (N_v tends to 6 sqrt(2)/7, N_f grows like r^{1/2}), so a small value of |R|/N_f alone would not
detect this defect. Local transport models (fields with div W = 2 c_l and W . grad rho = rho near q, not satisfying
the curl relation or the canonical inversion; Appendix A.3.34) realize every resonance in (f) and a flat degenerate
zero; no exact profile with a multiple or flat interior zero of Theta0 is known, and such zeros are not excluded in
general; conditional exclusions are given in (i) and 3.39.
(i) Strain at a critical escaping node (from the hostile audit; confirmed algebraically by the checker). In the
setting of (f), DW(q) is symmetric because grad rho(q) = 0, so DU(q) = DW(q) - c_l I is symmetric and trace-free with
operator norm c_l - lambda_- = c_l + (2 c_l l - 1)/(k - l) >= c_l + A/(k - 1); a double zero (k = 2) needs
|DU(q)|_op = 3 c_l - 1, while |DU(0)|_op = c_l - 1. Hence, for an integer M >= 2 (unrelated to the M of (g)): if all
interior zeros of Theta0 have finite order at most M and
|DU|_op < c_l + A/(M - 1) at every nonzero zero of W where grad rho vanishes, then (H-dyn) holds.
Scope: (a)-(i) are implications and subclass exclusions; none of them proves (H-dyn) for every profile, constructs a
profile or excludes the full primary class.

3.35 Energy lower bound on gradients (the identity and the k = 3 bound from an external audit of the small c_l - 1
regime; the k = 2 bound, a direct instance of the same identity, from the main analysis; both confirmed by the checker,
who reconstructed the argument with outer cutoffs and the canonical multiplier on L^2 spaces of derivatives).
Put G_rho = sup |grad rho| and G_U = sup |DU| (Frobenius norms). By 3.23 both are finite and D^k rho, D^k U are in
L^2(R^2) for k >= 2; G_rho and G_U are invariant under the dilations rho_l(X) = l rho(X/l).
Differentiate transport k times and pair with D^k rho. Using div U = 0 and int (c_l X . grad f) f = -c_l int f^2 (the
cutoff error at infinity is bounded by the L^2 mass of D^k rho on an annulus and tends to zero), one gets
    ((k - 1) c_l - 1) ||D^k rho||_2^2 = - < D^k rho, [D^k, U . grad] rho >.
The canonical multipliers give ||D^k U||_2 <= ||D^k rho||_2, since the squared moduli of the symbols of U_1 and U_2
sum to xi1^2/|xi|^2 <= 1. One integration by parts gives ||D v||_4^2 <= (2 + sqrt 2) ||v||_inf ||D^2 v||_2, which
bounds the middle Leibniz terms. If D^k rho = 0, then rho is a polynomial; sublinear growth makes it constant and odd parity makes it zero, which
contradicts a0 != 0. So every exact profile satisfies
    c_l - 1 <= 2 G_U + G_rho   (k = 2),     2 c_l - 1 <= 3 G_U + G_rho + 3 (2 + sqrt 2) sqrt(G_U G_rho)   (k = 3),
and in particular G_rho + G_U >= (2 c_l - 1)/C_* with C_* = 6 + 3 sqrt(2)/2 (about 8.12). Comparison with the origin:
grad rho(0) = (0, a0) and DU(0) = diag(c_l - 1, 1 - c_l) (3.2) give G_rho >= |a0| and G_U >= sqrt(2) (c_l - 1), so the
k = 2 bound carries no information beyond the origin values. The coarsened sum bound G_rho + G_U >= (2 c_l - 1)/C_*
adds information beyond the origin values only when (2 c_l - 1)/C_* > |a0| + sqrt(2) (c_l - 1), which requires
c_l < 1 + 1/(6 sqrt 2 + 1) = 1.10542... and |a0| < (2 c_l - 1)/C_*. The full k = 3 inequality is stronger: for
example at c_l = 1.2, |a0| = 0.001 the origin pair (G_U, G_rho) = (0.2 sqrt 2, 0.001) satisfies the coarsened bound
(sum 0.28384 > 1.4/C_* = 0.17239) but gives 3 G_U + G_rho + 3 (2 + sqrt 2) sqrt(G_U G_rho) = 1.02179 < 1.4, so the
k = 3 inequality forces gradients larger than the origin values there. Consequences: no exact
profile has G_rho + G_U < 1/C_* (about 0.123), for any c_l > 1 and any a0. A family of exact profiles with
G_rho + G_U <= M (c_l - 1) does not exist for c_l - 1 < 1/(C_* M); this is the uniform form of the formal regime of
Section 7, item 6. By 3.44(ii), these consequences hold with C_* replaced by 3/sqrt 2. Scope: the bounds say nothing
about where the large gradients are, and the slope a0 itself may be small. No upper bound on G_rho or G_U for exact
profiles is known, so the bounds exclude only profiles with small gradients and give no contradiction for the class as
a whole.

3.36 Sharper energy constants and a conditional strain-cap exclusion (external analysis, hand-checked in the main
analysis; confirmed by the checker, who reconstructed the argument and ran exact and manufactured checks). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary
class, S = (DU + DU^T)/2 the symmetric part of DU, sigma = sup |S|_op (so sigma >= c_l - 1 = D by the origin values),
G_rho = sup |grad rho|, G_U = sup |DU| (Frobenius), E_k = ||D^k rho||_2^2.
(i) For smooth v with the decay of 3.23, ||D v||_4^2 <= 3 ||v||_inf ||D^2 v||_2.
(ii) In the identity of 3.35 the first-order commutator terms involve only S and are bounded by k sigma E_k. For k = 3,
    2 c_l - 1 <= 3 sigma + G_rho + 9 sqrt(G_U G_rho),
and, with sigma <= G_U/sqrt 2, G_rho + G_U >= (2 c_l - 1)/Lambda, where Lambda = 6.0954523... is the largest
eigenvalue of [[1, 9/2], [9/2, 3/sqrt 2]]; the sum bound is strengthened in 3.44(ii).
(iii) Strain cap. If sigma <= c_l - 1 (the symmetric strain is nowhere larger than at the origin), then
X . W >= |X|^2, every backward orbit tends to 0 (so (H-dyn) holds), |grad rho| is nonincreasing along forward
orbits, G_rho = |a0| and G_U <= sqrt(2 (c_l - 1)^2 + a0^2/2). Consequently no exact profile has 1 < c_l <= 3/2,
0 < |a0| <= 1/400 and sigma <= c_l - 1 (contained in 3.42(v); 3.47(iii) gives the stronger necessary condition a0 >= 4
c_l - 2 for every exact profile with sigma <= c_l - 1).
Remarks (not results): whether sigma <= c_l - 1 holds for any exact profile is not known; if the higher-order
commutator terms were o(k E_k) along a sequence of k the identity would give sigma >= c_l, which is not proved. Smooth
non-profiles can share with a smooth density of the class that has outward flow (X . W > 0 for X != 0) and c = 1 - c_l
the jet of rho at 0, the jet of U at 0 to any prescribed finite order, the far-field data Theta0 and outward flow, and
still have arbitrarily large G_rho and G_U; the base density may be an exact profile with outward flow, if one exists,
or an explicit density such as 4 (c_l - 1) y F0(r) with F0 radial, nonincreasing, F0 = 1 on [0, 1] and F0 = r^{p-1}
on [2, inf). So an upper bound on these quantities must use the equation.

3.37 The limit c_l -> 1 (external analysis, hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed by the checker with an
independent full-plane inversion of the family in (iii); (iii) and (iv) also checked by the external hostile audit).
For exact profiles of the primary class:
(i) sup |grad rho - a e_2| >= |a| for every a != 0 (because grad rho -> 0 at infinity, 3.23); so no exact profile is
within global C^1 distance less than |a| of the affine state a y, at any c_l > 1 and after any dilation.
(ii) With the k = 3 bound of 3.35 (constant C_* = 6 + 3 sqrt2/2): for finite M, K >= 0, profiles with
G_rho + G_U <= M |a0| and |a0| <= K (c_l - 1) satisfy (C_* M K - 2)(c_l - 1) >= 1; hence they do not exist when
C_* M K <= 2, and otherwise not for c_l - 1 < 1/(C_* M K - 2). By 3.44(ii), the same conclusions hold with C_*
replaced by 3/sqrt 2.
(iii) Interior false positives (non-profiles). Fix c_l > 1, D = c_l - 1, a != 0, a smooth radial cutoff chi with
chi = 1 on [0, 1] and chi = 0 on [2, inf), and eta >= 0 smooth, supported in (2, 3), with J = int eta(t) dt/t > 0.
Put q_L = a y chi(r/L) + ((a/4 - D)/J) r sin(3 th) eta(r/L) = L q_1(X/L). Its canonical velocity is
v_L = (D x, -D y) on the disk B_L (stream function -D x y there), so the transport residual
(c_l X + v_L) . grad q_L - q_L vanishes identically on B_L; the gradients of q_L and v_L are bounded independently of L
(dilation invariance); q_L is compactly supported and so is not a profile (3.7). A residual that is small, or zero, on
a bounded region does not by itself establish proximity to a profile.
(iv) Bounded-gradient limits. Let rho_n be exact profiles with c_{l,n} -> 1 and G_rho,n + G_U,n <= M. A subsequence
converges locally uniformly, with weak-* convergence of the gradients in L^inf, to a Lipschitz pair (rho, U) with the
parities of the class, rho(0) = 0, U(0) = 0 and |rho| + |U| <= M |X|, solving (X + U) . grad rho = rho almost
everywhere and div U = 0, curl U = -rho_x in the sense of distributions. The argument gives neither C^1 regularity, nor
a nonzero slope at 0, nor sublinear growth, nor a nonzero limit: dilating each rho_n by a suitably chosen factor
l_n -> 0 (which preserves c_{l,n} and the gradient bounds) gives the zero limit. The divergence and curl relations
determine U only up to a multiple of (x, -y): every field V of at most linear growth with the parities, div V = 0 and
curl V = -rho_x is U + b (x, -y) with b real, and at linear growth no canonical velocity of rho is defined in general.
The transport equation fixes b unless x rho_x = y rho_y almost everywhere; in particular, if rho = a y with a != 0,
then U = 0. That every such limit is affine is not proved.

3.38 Sharpness of the regularity ceiling for homogeneous source modes (external analysis; confirmed by the checker
with an independent upper-bound argument covering frequency-axis distributions, in the scope stated here). Fix A > 1, B = A - 1 and a0 > B. Consider nonzero
whole-plane tempered distributions h, even in x and odd in y, homogeneous of noninteger degree d > 1, solving
(A x d_x + y d_y - 1) h + a0 psi_x = 0 with -Lap psi = h_x, psi the unique homogeneous distributional inverse of degree
d + 1 (frequency-axis distributions included). For noninteger s > 0, every such mode of class C^s (on both axes and at
the origin) satisfies s <= min(d, (a0 - d + 1)/B), and the supremum of the attained s over this class is
s_sup = (a0 + 1)/A (= min(a0/B, (a0 + 1)/A) for a0 > B); attainment at s_sup is not claimed. In particular, if m >= 0,
0 < alpha < 1 and s = m + alpha < s_sup, a mode of degree d of class C^{m, alpha} (stream of class C^{m+1, alpha})
exists for every noninteger d in (max(1, s), a0 + 1 - B s) for which (A d - 1)/B and (a0 - d + 1)/B are not integers
(finitely many d are excluded); no nonzero mode is C^inf at 0, and modes with d < m + 1 are not C^{m+1} at 0 (m = 1:
3.25(ii)).
Integer degrees, logarithmic modes, non-homogeneous solutions and the case a0 <= B are outside this statement. Its use
for the nonlinear problem is conditional on a locally finite polyhomogeneous expansion of the profile at the source
with coefficients extracted in angular C^s and a justified termwise local inverse; it proves no smoothness, constructs
no profile and decides neither existence nor nonexistence.

3.39 Critical escaping nodes: conditional exclusions (external analysis, hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed by
the checker with an independent proof and exact symbolic checks of the kernels, moments, transport and resonance
formulas). For an exact profile of the primary class, in the notation of 3.30 and 3.34, let q be a zero of W with
rho(q) = 0 and grad rho(q) = 0.
(a) Kernel formula: DU(q) = (1/pi) int rho(q - z) |z|^{-6} M(z) dz, absolutely convergent, where M(z) is the
symmetric trace-free matrix with entries M_11 = -M_22 = z_2 (3 z_1^2 - z_2^2), M_12 = z_1 (3 z_2^2 - z_1^2); so
|DU(q)|_op is the modulus of a cubic-angle moment of rho about q. Combined with transport (W(q) = 0, z . grad of the
kernel is -3 times the kernel) it gives the scale-invariant moment identity
D m(q) = -int rho(q - z) [(U(q - z) - U(q)) . grad] Q(z) dz, with m(q) the vector of the two strain entries and
Q(z) = (sin 3 arg z, -cos 3 arg z)/(pi |z|^3), and hence
|DU(q)|_op <= (3/(pi D)) int |rho(q - z)| |U(q - z) - U(q)| |z|^{-4} dz.
A strict bound, the right side < 3 c_l - 1 or |DU(q) - DU(0)|_op < 2 c_l, at every nonzero zero q of W with
grad rho(q) = 0 (it suffices at the maximizer of 3.34(b)), would exclude a double node (k = 2 in 3.34(f)), since there
|DU(q)|_op = 3 c_l - 1 and |DU(q) - DU(0)|_op >= 2 c_l, with equality only if DU(q) = diag(3 c_l - 1, 1 - 3 c_l) (a
horizontal fast direction, not excluded off the x-axis; at a double node on the x-axis the value is 4 c_l - 2). Compactly supported non-profiles with prescribed a0 and rho = a0 y (x - 2)^2 near
q = (2, 0) have unbounded |DU(q)|, so no bound follows from the kernel alone.
(b) Sign subclass: if (H-dyn) fails and the maximizer q of Pi on K (3.34(b)) is off the x-axis and one of its fast
branches escapes at a zero of Theta0 of finite order k, with l as in 3.34(f), then both fast unstable branches of q are
nodal and escape with the same (k, l) (for a general zero of W with grad rho = 0 the second branch is not known to
escape); if q lies in y > 0 and rho/a0 >= 0 on y > 0, then k and l are both even; in particular
there is no off-axis double node with rho/a0 >= 0 on y > 0.
(c) Counting: the y-axis carries no zero of W other than 0; if all zeros of W are nondegenerate and (H-dyn) fails,
there are at least five zeros, and at least nine if one of them is an off-axis saddle. Hence an exact profile whose
zeros of W are all nondegenerate and at most four in number satisfies (H-dyn).
(d) At an angular double zero th* of Theta0 the second far-field term satisfies Theta1(th*) = 0 and
Theta1'(th*) = u_{0,th}(th*) Theta0''(th*)/D; it displaces the nodal line by O(r^{p - 1}) and gives no contradiction.
(e) The periodic non-profile of 3.34(c) realizes the double order (k, l) = (2, 1) at its axis saddle x = pi/kappa
(kappa the wave number k of 3.34(c)), where DW = diag(-A, 4 c_l - 1), with rho >= 0 on y > 0; so for the local
identities the restriction of (b) to off-axis nodes cannot be dropped. That example violates both sublinear growth and
U = o(r).
Scope: (a) uses exact transport at a critical saddle (an arbitrary angular zero of an arbitrary field does not have
this structure); the non-profiles in (a) satisfy neither transport nor the origin strain; (b) needs the global sign
rho/a0 >= 0 on y > 0 and an off-axis node, and double nodes on the x-axis remain allowed; (c) counts only nondegenerate
zeros (degenerate and flat zeros are outside it); (d) uses only the first two far-field terms; 3.68 gives the further
terms, the third of which fixes its angular coefficient at th* (A.3.39(d)); further consequences for (d) are not
analyzed here. None of (a)-(e) proves (H-dyn) or excludes the double node in general.

3.40 Scale-invariant derivative residual (external audit; checked in the main analysis; confirmed by the checker with an
independent proof of the residual cutoff identity and exact Gaussian full-plane integrations). For a smooth
candidate rho with its canonical velocity, symbol bounds of degree q < 1, D^3 rho != 0 and D^3 R in L^2, where
R = (c_l X + U) . grad rho - rho, the quantity eta_3 = ||D^3 R||_2/||D^3 rho||_2 is invariant under dilations and
    eta_3 >= [2 c_l - 1 - 3 G_U - G_rho - 3 (2 + sqrt 2) sqrt(G_U G_rho)]_+ .
It is the identity of 3.35 with R kept: (2 c_l - 1) ||D^3 rho||_2^2 + < D^3 rho, [D^3, U . grad] rho >
= < D^3 rho, D^3 R >. So a candidate with small gradients has eta_3 >= 2 c_l - 1 - C_* (G_rho + G_U),
C_* = 6 + 3 sqrt(2)/2, so eta_3 is at least about 2 c_l - 1 (it can be arbitrarily large), even if its pointwise
relative residuals are small: for the vanishing family of 3.41, whose relative
residuals are O(D), eta_3 stays of order 1 as D -> 0 (3.41(v)). The inequality is a diagnostic for candidates;
it is not an existence or distance theorem and gives no bound for sampled norms.

3.41 Vanishing approximate family (constructed by the checker; hand-checked in the main analysis; proved item by item
in an external audit, whose sharper constants are used here). For 0 < D <= 1 put c_l = 1 + D, eta = D/(1 + D),
a = 4D, f(r) = (1 + r^2)^{-eta/2}, H(r) = int_0^1 t^3 f(r t) dt, and
    rho_D = a y f(r),     psi_D = -a x y H(r).
(i) psi_D is the canonical stream function of rho_D: r H' = f - 4H gives -Lap psi_D = d_x rho_D, U_D = O(r^{1 - eta})
= o(r), and uniqueness is that of 3.1. rho_D is smooth, even in x, odd in y, and |rho_D| = O(r^p) with
p = 1/c_l = 1 - eta < 1.
(ii) a0 = a = 4D and c = -a/4 = -D, so the origin condition c_l + c = 1 holds exactly.
(iii) With q = r^2/(1 + r^2), tau = H/f in [1/4, 1/(4 - eta)] and J = r H'/f = 1 - 4 tau in [-eta/(4 - eta), 0],
    R/rho_D = D [ (1 - q) - 4 f (tau + cos^2(th) J + eta q tau cos(2 th)) ],
so |R| <= (23/7) D |rho_D| everywhere; since N_f >= |rho_D| and N_v >= |rho_D|, also |R| <= 4D N_f and |R| <= 4D N_v
(on the x-axis R = N_f = N_v = 0 and the ratios are undefined).
(iv) No member is a profile. On the positive y-axis R(0, y) ~ -a^2 p y^{1 - 2 eta}/(4 - eta), with negative
coefficient; the unnormalized residual R(0, y) is unbounded for 0 < D < 1 and tends to -16/7 at D = 1. The cubic
relations of 3.3 fail as well: b = e = -a eta/2, the sin 4th coefficient of the quartic part of psi_D is 0, and the
defects (a0 - 2A) b - 6e = 16 D^2/(1 + D) and (a0 - 4A) b - 3 a0 (q1 - q2) = 8 D^2 (A = 2 c_l - 1) are nonzero.
(v) sup |grad rho_D| = 4D and sup |DU_D|_F <= D (sqrt 2 + 4 eta + eta^2/2), so for small D the family violates the
lower bounds of 3.35 and 3.36, as it must; by the triangle inequality every exact profile with the same c_l is at
distance at least (1 + 2D)/C_* - 4D - D (sqrt 2 + 4 eta + eta^2/2) from rho_D in sup |grad .| + sup |D U[.]|, which stays
positive as D -> 0. The derivative residual of 3.40 stays of order 1: the checker computes eta_3 = 1.3093 at
D = 1e-4 (three quadrature levels); and eta_3 -> sqrt(12/7) as D -> 0 (checker's proof, confirmed in a second external audit with a uniform majorant
C (1 + r)^{-2}): D^3 rho_D/D^2 and D^3 R/D^2 converge in L^2 to the third derivatives of -2 y log(1 + r^2) and
-4 y r^2/(1 + r^2), whose squared norms are 512 pi/5 and 6144 pi/35 (also recomputed in the main analysis).
(vi) Strain and weighted residual (checker's proof; confirmed in a second external audit, exactly, not by sampling).
sigma = sup |sym DU_D|_op = D and M = sup(-X . U_D/|X|^2) = D (the supremum of M approached along the y-axis as
r -> 0), so X . W >= |X|^2: the family satisfies the strain cap of 3.36(iii) with a0 = 4D < 2 (2 c_l - 1) and a
nonzero cubic jet, which 3.45 and 3.46 exclude for exact profiles; the transport equation is essential there
(d_xxy R(0) = -8 D^2 != 0). Since c_l + c = 1, the weighted residual ratio ||R||_m/||h_D||_m (h_D = rho_D - a y) is
finite for 2 < m < 4, and h_D/D^2 -> -2 y log(1 + r^2), R/D^2 -> -4 y r^2/(1 + r^2) in L^2(r^{-2m} dX); at m = 3 the
limit of the ratio is 2 sqrt(3)/pi = 1.1027, above the lower bound 1 - O(D) that 3.44(vi) gives for this family.
Meaning and scope: arbitrarily small uniform relative residuals coexist with smoothness, the exact elliptic relation,
the canonical velocity, the parities, sublinear growth and the exact origin condition, without an exact profile; so
small relative residuals alone cannot certify a profile. The family degenerates as D -> 0 (c_l -> 1, a0 -> 0,
p -> 1); it does not show the same phenomenon at fixed c_l > 1, at fixed a0 != 0 or with one growth exponent below 1
for the whole family; it gives no small absolute residual; and it says nothing about existence of profiles near
c_l = 1.

3.42 Weighted lower bound for h = rho - a0 y (from an external audit of 3.41; proved independently by the checker,
with exact Mellin algebra, complex matrix singular values and manufactured Gaussian energy integrations; audited in a
second external analysis). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary class, c = 1 - c_l, h = rho - a0 y,
phi = psi - c x y, v = (-phi_y, phi_x) = U - (-c x, c y), ||g||_m^2 = int |g|^2 r^{-2m} dX, and sigma as in 3.36.
(i) By c_l + c = 1, (c_l X + U) . grad h - h = -a0 v_2.
(ii) For 2 < m < 4, h and v are O(r^3) at 0 and O(r) at infinity, 0 < ||h||_m < inf (rho = a0 y does not have
sublinear growth), and pairing (i) with h r^{-2m} gives, with vanishing boundary terms,
    ((m - 1) c_l - 1) ||h||_m^2 + m int (X . U/r^2) h^2 r^{-2m} dX = -a0 int v_2 h r^{-2m} dX.
(iii) ||v||_m <= N_m ||h||_m with N_m = max((m^2 + 4)/(m^2 - 4), (m^2 + 16)/(16 - m^2)). In s = log r, the Poisson
equation for G = r^{-m} phi with source F = r^{1-m} h is diagonal in the frequency xi and the even angular modes n of
phi, and the map from F to v is bounded there by (xi^2 + m^2 + n^2)/((xi^2 + (n - m)^2)(xi^2 + (n + m)^2))^{1/2},
largest at xi = 0 and n = 2 or n = 4 (an upper bound for the norm of h -> v; 3.44 gives the sharp constants for the
form int v_2 h r^{-2m}); N_3 = 25/7 and N_{sqrt 8} = 3. Here v_2 is normalized at the origin; the canonical
inverse of the same source is U_2 = v_2 - D y.
(iv) Since X . U(X) = int_0^1 X^T S(tX) X dt >= -sigma |X|^2, every exact profile satisfies, for 2 < m < 4,
    (m - 1) c_l - 1 <= m sigma + N_m |a0|,   in particular   2 c_l - 1 <= 3 sigma + (25/7) |a0|,
and, as sigma <= G_U/sqrt 2 and |a0| <= G_rho, G_rho + G_U >= 7 (2 c_l - 1)/25. This improves the constant
1/Lambda = 0.164 of 3.36(ii) to 0.28.
(v) Under the strain cap sigma <= c_l - 1 of 3.36(iii) (an extra hypothesis, not known to hold for any exact
profile), 2 - c_l <= (25/7) |a0|; so no exact profile has sigma <= c_l - 1, 1 < c_l < 2 and |a0| < 7 (2 - c_l)/25.
This contains the exclusion stated in 3.36(iii).
Scope: (iv) is a lower bound on the strain. No upper bound on sigma is known for exact profiles, so no parameter region
is excluded without the extra hypothesis of (v).

3.43 Angular contrast, a positivity test and non-profiles with the integral identities (external analysis; proved
independently by the checker, with exact symbolic identities, reflected-bump sign checks and full-plane Gaussian
inverse samples; the formula in (i) audited in a second external analysis). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary
class, q = rho/(a0 y) (smooth, even in x and in y, q(0) = 1, q = O(r^{p-1}) at infinity by 3.23) and
k(th) = sin^2 th (4 sin^2 th - 3).
(i) The strain identity of 3.2 in the form c/a0 = (4/pi) int_Q x y^2 r^{-4} q_x dX (Q the open first quadrant) becomes,
after integration by parts in r and in th,
    D/a0 = 1/4 + (4/pi) int_0^inf [ int_0^{pi/2} k(th) q(r, th) dth ] dr/r,
with the angular integral taken first: it is O(r^2) at 0 because k has mean zero, while the double integral of
k q/r is not absolutely convergent near 0.
(ii) Put A(q) = int_0^inf osc_{0 <= th <= pi/2} q(r, th) dr/r (finite and dilation invariant). Since k has mean zero
on [0, pi/2] and its positive part has mass 3 sqrt(3)/16, |D/a0 - 1/4| <= (3 sqrt(3)/(4 pi)) A(q), with strict
inequality if A(q) > 0. With z = 3 sqrt(3) A(q)/pi: z = 0 gives a0 = 4D, and 0 < z < 1 gives
4/(1 + z) < a0/D < 4/(1 - z). Hence A(q) <= pi/(3 sqrt 3) implies a0 > 2D; a0 < 0 requires
A(q) > (pi/(3 sqrt 3))(1 + 4D/|a0|); and 0 < a0 <= 2D requires A(q) > (pi/(3 sqrt 3))(4D/a0 - 1). No bound on A(q)
is known for exact profiles, and a sampled value of A(q) for an approximate state is not a global bound (4.7).
(iii) Positivity test. The multiplier T with symbol xi_1^2/|xi|^2 is nonnegative on L^2, but positively weighted forms
need not be: for g = y e^{-r^2} (positive for y > 0), Tg(2, 1) = -11/250 + (133/125) e^{-5} < 0, and there is a
smooth positive weight w, even in x and in y, with int w g Tg dX < 0. This refutes only the inference from multiplier
positivity to positivity of every positively weighted form; no profile-specific weighted identity is refuted.
(iv) Non-profiles with the integral identities. For fixed s < 0 or s >= 1/2 there are D > 0, a0 = D/s and smooth
densities rho_n, n = 1, 2, ..., with canonical velocity, the parities of the class, Theta0 = a0 sin th,
DW(0) = diag(2 c_l - 1, 1), X . W >= |X|^2/2 and F_p/2 <= q_n <= C F_p with F_p = (1 + r^2)^{(p-1)/2} and C
independent of n, which satisfy the strain
identity, the identity 1 = S + T of 3.24(ii) and the weighted identity 3.4, while sup |grad rho_n| and sup |DU_n| are
unbounded. They are not profiles: their second far-field coefficient is 0, whereas 3.32 requires
Theta1 = -a0^2 sin th (cos^2 th + p sin^2 th)/(D (p + 3)) != 0. So these scalar identities together, with positivity
and outward flow, give no gradient upper bound and do not fix the sign of a0.

3.44 Sharp weighted constants (external analysis; hand-checked in part in the main analysis; confirmed by the checker,
who derived the angular operator independently and gave separate exact rational certificates for the infinite
matrices). Notation of 3.42, and M = sup_{X != 0} (-X . U(X)/|X|^2), so that D <= M <= sigma (the lower bound from the
origin values along the y-axis).
(i) For 2 < m < 4, -Q_m^- ||h||_m^2 <= int v_2 h r^{-2m} dX <= Q_m^+ ||h||_m^2, where Q_m^- (resp. Q_m^+) is the top
of the spectrum of the symmetric Jacobi matrix on l^2(j >= 1) with diagonal (1/4, 1/2, 1/2, ...) (resp. its negative)
and off-diagonal entries b_j(m) = (m^2 + 4 j^2)/(4 |4 j^2 - m^2|). Reason: in the variables of 3.42(iii) the map
h -> v_2 is tridiagonal in the odd sine modes, with diagonal -(1/4, 1/2, 1/2, ...) and off-diagonal entries
(2j - z)/(4(2j + z)) and (2j + z)/(4(2j - z)), z = m + i xi; the off-diagonal entries of its Hermitian part have
modulus at most b_j(m), with equality at xi = 0, and Plancherel in s = log r gives the bounds. The constants are sharp
for the weighted class with the parities of the profile (not asserted for profiles). Certified enclosures:
1.6327 < Q_3^- < 1.633 and 0.704 < Q_3^+ < 0.710.
(ii) Every exact profile satisfies, for 2 < m < 4, (m - 1) c_l - 1 <= m M + Q_m^- a0 if a0 > 0 and
(m - 1) c_l - 1 <= m M + Q_m^+ |a0| if a0 < 0; in particular 2 c_l - 1 <= 3 sigma + 1.633 a0 (a0 > 0) and
2 c_l - 1 <= 3 sigma + 0.710 |a0| (a0 < 0). With sigma <= G_U/sqrt 2 and |a0| <= G_rho this gives
G_rho + G_U >= (sqrt 2/3)(2 c_l - 1), improving the constant 0.28 of 3.42(iv) to 0.47.
(iii) For fixed c_l, every sequence of exact profiles with a0 -> 0 has liminf sigma >= max(c_l - 1, (3 c_l - 1)/4)
(let a0 -> 0 in (ii) at fixed m, then m -> 4).
(iv) Higher vanishing. If h = O(r^{2k+1}) at 0 with k >= 1, then phi = O(r^{2k+2}) by the transport equation, the
identity of 3.42(ii) holds for 2 < m < 2k + 2 (no harmonic polynomial can be added to the weighted inverse, by L^2
uniqueness), and for such m that are not even integers (i)-(ii) hold with the same matrices. If h is flat at 0 (all
Taylor
coefficients vanish; analyticity is not assumed), letting m -> inf through odd integers gives sigma >= c_l - |a0|/2.
(v) Derivative form. For 1 < mu < 3, mu c_l - 1 <= (mu + 1) sigma + N'_mu |a0| with
N'_mu = max((mu^2 + 1)/(mu^2 - 1), (mu^2 + 9)/(9 - mu^2)) (N'_2 = 13/5), from the differentiated equation paired
with grad h r^{-2 mu}; the potentials of the derivatives have odd angular frequencies only.
(vi) Residual form for candidates (checker's proof; confirmed in a second external audit). Let rho be smooth, even in
x, odd in y, a0 = rho_y(0) != 0, with its canonical velocity (normalized by parity, U(0) = 0) and symbol bounds
|D^k rho| + |D^k U| <= C_k r^{p - k} (r >= 1, k <= 2, some p < 1), and let c_l > 1 be arbitrary. Put c = psi_xy(0)
(the actual strain), delta = c_l + c - 1 (the centre defect), R = W . grad rho - rho and F = R - a0 delta y. Then for
2 < m < 4, ||F||_m/||h||_m >= (m - 1) c_l - 1 - m M - Q_m^-+ |a0| (sign by a0), and for 1 < mu < 3,
mu c_l - 1 <= (mu + 1) sigma + N'_mu |a0| + ||grad F||_mu/||grad h||_mu; here M >= |c| (not necessarily D). If
delta != 0 then ||R||_m = inf for every m >= 2 and ||grad R||_mu = inf for every mu >= 1, so the centre defect must be
reported separately; subtracting it does not make a candidate closer to a profile. All ratios are dilation invariant.
For exact profiles F = 0 and (vi) reduces to (ii) and (v).
Scope: (i)-(v) are necessary conditions (lower bounds on sigma or M in terms of c_l and a0), and (vi) is a diagnostic
for candidates, not a distance or existence statement. No upper bound on sigma or M is known for exact profiles, so
none of them excludes a parameter region by itself.

3.45 Strain cap: the cubic jet and the weight m = 5 (main analysis and external analysis, by two independent routes;
confirmed by the checker with exact jet algebra and separate infinite-tail certificates). Let rho be an exact profile
of the primary class that satisfies in addition the strain cap sigma <= c_l - 1 of 3.36(iii) (an extra hypothesis,
not known to hold for any exact profile). Notation of 3.3: rho = a0 y + b x^2 y + e y^3 + O(r^5) and
psi = -D x y + q1 x^3 y + q2 x y^3 + O(r^6), with q1 = -2Ab/(3 a0), q2 = -2e/a0, 6e = (a0 - 2A) b, A = 2 c_l - 1.
(i) Either a0 >= 2A = 4 c_l - 2, or b = e = q1 = q2 = 0; if a0 < 0 the second alternative holds. Strain route:
|S(X)|_op^2 = D^2 - 6D (q1 x^2 + q2 y^2) + O(r^4) has its global maximum D^2 at 0, so q1 >= 0 and q2 >= 0. Gradient
route: |grad rho|^2 = a0^2 + 2 a0 (b x^2 + 3 e y^2) + O(r^4) and |grad rho| <= |a0| (3.36(iii)) give a0 b <= 0 and
a0 e <= 0. Either pair with the relations above gives the alternative: if b != 0 then a0 b < 0 and
a0 e = (a0 - 2A) a0 b/6 <= 0 force a0 >= 2A; if b = 0 then e = q1 = q2 = 0.
(ii) In the second alternative h = O(r^5), so m = 5 is admissible in 3.44(iv). Certified: 2.3629 < Q_5^- < 2.363
and Q_5^+ < 1.367 (upper bounds by two independent exact rational certificates for the infinite matrices, lower bounds
by exact Rayleigh quotients and an exact truncated elimination test; 1.3661 < Q_5^+ < 1.3662). With sigma <= D,
3.44(ii) at m = 5 reads 4 - c_l <= Q_5^- a0 if a0 > 0 and
4 - c_l <= Q_5^+ |a0| if a0 < 0. Hence, for 1 < c_l < 4: a0 > 0 implies a0 >= min(4 c_l - 2, (4 - c_l)/2.363), and
a0 < 0 implies |a0| >= (4 - c_l)/1.367; as c_l -> 1 these thresholds tend to 3/2.363 > 1.2695 and 3/1.367 > 2.1945.
(iii) Scope. The radial cap M <= D alone gives only q2 >= 0 by this argument (along the y-axis
-X . U/r^2 = D - q2 y^2 + O(y^4)), and this argument does not give (i). Whether any exact profile satisfies sigma <=
c_l - 1 is
open; (i)-(ii) restrict the parameters of such profiles and say nothing about their existence. A sampled strain
maximum of an approximate state is a lower estimate of its own sigma and cannot be used to verify the cap.

3.46 Strain cap at every order (external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed by the checker, who
reconstructed the jet recursion and its solution space independently, with a different choice of the auxiliary index
in the lemma, and certified lambda by a separate rational bound on both infinite tails). Let rho be an exact profile of
the primary class with sigma <= c_l - 1 (the extra hypothesis of 3.45). Put h = rho - a0 y, phi = psi + D x y,
B = A - 1 = 2 D.
(i) Jet threshold. If h has a nonzero Taylor coefficient at 0, let h_n be its first nonzero homogeneous part
(n = 2K + 1 >= 3, odd by parity; analyticity is not assumed). Then a0 >= (n - 1)(2 c_l - 1) >= 2 (2 c_l - 1).
Proof outline: phi = O(r^{n+1}), and the leading pair (h_n, phi_{n+1}) satisfies a two-term recursion in its
coefficients whose solution space is one-dimensional for every real a0, the resonant values included. Write
(phi_{n+1})_xy = y^{n-1} P(x^2/y^2). Since phi_xy = psi_xy + D >= D - |S|_op >= 0 everywhere, P >= 0 on [0, inf).
With eta = 1 + K/B and chi = eta - a0/(2B), P is a nonzero multiple of
F_chi(t) = sum_{k=0}^K (-1)^k C(2K, 2k) (eta)_k (chi + k)_{K-k} t^k ((x)_k the rising factorial). If
a0 < (n - 1) A then chi > 1 - K, and E F_chi(T S) = 0 for independent random variables T, beta-prime with parameters
(chi + K - 1, K + 1/2), and S, beta with parameters (1/2, eta - 1/2), both with full support (the expectation is a
K-th finite difference of a polynomial of degree K - 1 in the summation index, so no value of chi is exceptional).
Since T S has
full support on (0, inf) and the top coefficient of F_chi is nonzero, no nonzero multiple of F_chi is nonnegative on
[0, inf), a contradiction. For a0 >= (n - 1) A compatible jets with P >= 0 exist, so the threshold is sharp for the
jet conditions; this says nothing about exact profiles. The gradient condition |grad rho| <= |a0| of 3.36(iii) is
implied by P >= 0 at the level of the leading jet, but does not suffice by itself: compatible degree-5 jets with
a0 (h_5)_y < 0 in every direction and P(1) < 0 exist (for example at c_l = 19, a0 = -2; these are polynomial jets
satisfying only the leading equations, and by (i) no capped profile has such a leading jet).
(ii) Flat case. If h is flat at 0 (all Taylor coefficients vanish), then M >= c_l - lambda |a0|, hence
sigma >= c_l - lambda |a0|, where lambda is the top of the spectrum of (L u)_k = l_{k-1} u_{k-1} + l_k u_{k+1} on
l^2(Z), l_k = 1/(4 |2k - 1|). Certified: 0.363427798 < lambda < 0.363427799 (checker, exact rational elimination with
bounds on both infinite tails); 0.36342 < lambda < 4/11 by a different certificate (a positive supersolution and a
Rayleigh quotient). Reason:
by 3.44(iv) the bound 3.44(ii) holds for every odd m >= 3; the identity b_j(m)/m - 1/(4 |2j - m|) =
sgn(2j - m) 2j/(4m(2j + m)) gives |Q_m^-+/m - lambda| <= 1/m, and dividing 3.44(ii) by m and letting m -> inf gives
c_l <= M + lambda |a0|. This improves the flat bound of 3.44(iv).
(iii) Conclusion. An exact profile of the primary class with sigma <= c_l - 1 has either a0 >= 2 (2 c_l - 1) (h not
flat) or h flat at 0 and |a0| >= 1/lambda > 2.7515. In particular |a0| > 2, and a0 < 0 forces h to be flat. This
supersedes 3.45(i)-(ii). Under the radial cap M <= c_l - 1 alone, (ii) still holds but (i) is not available
(3.45(iii)).
Scope: a conditional theorem. Whether any exact profile satisfies sigma <= c_l - 1 is open; nothing is claimed about
the existence or nonexistence of capped profiles. By 3.47 the flat alternative of (ii)-(iii) does not occur.

3.47 Strain cap or one-sided sign: no flat remainder (external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed
by the checker by an independent reconstruction; for (iv) see there). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary class
with sigma <= c_l - 1 (the extra hypothesis of 3.45, 3.46). Put a = a0, H = y - rho/a = -h/a, V = U_2 + D y = phi_x
and B = X . W/r^2. (i) Consequences of the cap (3.36(iii) and its proof). X . U = int_0^1 X^T S(tX) X dt gives
r^2 <= X . W <= A r^2, so every backward orbit of W tends to 0. Along W, (1/2) W . grad |grad rho|^2 = -D |grad
rho|^2 - grad rho^T S grad rho <= 0, so |grad rho| <= |a| and, integrating vertically from rho(x, 0) = 0, |rho| <= |a|
|y|; hence y H >= 0. Parity gives U_1(0, y) = U_2(x, 0) = 0, and the diagonal entries of DU lie in [-D, D], so
1 <= W_1/x <= A, 1 <= W_2/y <= A and 0 <= V/y <= 2D; since q = rho/(a y) satisfies W . grad q = -q V/y and q -> 1
along backward orbits, 0 < q <= 1. (ii) h is not flat at 0. Exact transport and the Poisson equation give W . grad
H - H = V and Lap V = a H_xx. If h were flat, then V would be flat, and for every m > 2 the moments I_m = int H y
r^{-2m} dX and J_m = int V y r^{-2m} dX would converge (H, V = O(r) at infinity), with I_m > 0 (y H >= 0 and h != 0,
since rho = a y is not sublinear). Testing Lap V = a H_xx with y r^{2-2m} (Lap(y r^{2-2m}) = 4 (m - 1)(m - 2) y
r^{-2m} and d_xx(y r^{2-2m}) = 2 (m - 1) y r^{-2m} (2m x^2/r^2 - 1)) gives
    J_m = (a/(2 (m - 2))) int H y r^{-2m} (2m x^2/r^2 - 1) dX,
so J_m/I_m <= a (2m - 1)/(2 (m - 2)) if a > 0 and J_m/I_m <= |a|/(2 (m - 2)) if a < 0. Testing the transport identity
with y r^{-2m} (div W = 2 c_l) gives
    J_m = 2m int H y B r^{-2m} dX - (2 c_l + 1) I_m - int H W_2 r^{-2m} dX >= (2m - 4 c_l) I_m,
using B >= 1 and W_2/y <= A. At m = 3 + 2 c_l + 2 |a| the two bounds are incompatible (the upper bound is below 5|a|/2
for a > 0 and below 1/4 for a < 0, the lower bound is 6 + 4 |a|). The boundary terms are O(R^{4-2m}) on |X| = R by the
symbol bounds of 3.23 and vanish on small circles by flatness. (iii) Conclusion with 3.46(i). Every exact profile of
the primary class with sigma <= c_l - 1 has a nonzero first homogeneous part h_n of h, of odd degree n >= 3, and
a0 >= (n - 1)(2 c_l - 1) >= 4 c_l - 2 > 0; if 2A <= a0 < 4A the first part is cubic. In particular no capped profile
has a0 < 0 or a0 < 4 c_l - 2. (iv) The one-sided sign instead of the cap (the checker's proof; hand-checked in the
main analysis; the external audit found it correct). The conclusion of (ii) holds for every exact profile of the
primary class with y H >= 0, that is rho/(a0 y) <= 1 off y = 0, with no cap and no positivity of rho/(a0 y): h is not
flat at 0. Proof: the identities of (ii) hold without the cap, and the elliptic one still gives J_m/I_m <= a (2m -
1)/(2 (m - 2)) (a > 0) or J_m/I_m <= |a|/(2 (m - 2)) (a < 0). For transport let r_* = inf{|X| : H(X) y > 0}. If
r_* > 0 then H = V = 0 on the disc of radius r_*, so phi = 0 there (phi_x = V, phi odd in x) and W = (A x, y); if
r_* = 0 then W = (A x, y) + O(r^3). In both cases B >= 1/2 on 0 < |X| < R for some R > r_*. Choose r_* < r0 < R with
c0 = int_{|X| < r0} H y dX > 0; then I_m >= c0 r0^{-2m}, while the contributions of |X| >= R to the B-term and the
W_2-term of the transport identity are O(R^{4 - 2m}/(2m - 4)), negligible relative to I_m even after multiplication by
2m. With C_R = sup_{|X| < R} |W_2/y| this gives J_m/I_m >= m - (2 c_l + 1) - C_R - o(1) -> inf, a contradiction. In
particular, an exact profile with flat h has rho/(a0 y) > 1 somewhere. Scope: a conditional theorem; whether any exact
profile satisfies the cap, or the one-sided sign of (iv), is open. The cap and the pointwise inequalities of (i)
(|grad rho| <= |a|, 0 < rho/(a y) <= 1 and the bounds on X . W, W_1/x, W_2/y and V/y), imposed as properties of a
capped density without exact transport, do not bound a0 from above at c_l = 2 (capped non-profiles with arbitrarily
large a0, 3.50(a)); so, at least at c_l = 2, excluding the remaining capped subclass a0 >= 4 c_l - 2 needs exact
transport beyond these inequalities. By (iv) the flat alternative is also excluded under the one-sided sign
alone; its consequences for the jets of h are in 3.51.

3.48 Low-slope regime (elementary; external audit found it correct; confirmed by the checker with a standalone proof).
For an exact profile put rho_3(r) = (1/pi) int_0^{2 pi} rho(r, th) sin(3 th) dth. The strain identity of 3.2 with
c = 1 - c_l = -D reads int_0^inf rho_3 r^{-2} dr = a0/4 - D; the radial integral converges absolutely because
rho_3 = O(r^3) at 0 and O(r^gamma) at infinity (the two-dimensional integral (1/pi) int rho sin(3 th) r^{-3} dX of 3.2
never converges absolutely, since a0 != 0).
Write f_- = max(-f, 0). Hence (a) if 0 < a0 <= A - 1 = 2D, then int_0^inf (rho_3)_- r^{-2} dr >= (A - 1)/4; (b) if
a0 > 0 and |int rho_3 r^{-2} dr| <= eps0 a0/4 with 0 <= eps0 < 1, then a0 >= 2 (A - 1)/(1 + eps0); (c) if
|int rho_3 r^{-2} dr| <= kappa |a0| with 0 <= kappa < 1/4, then a0 > 0 and 4D/(1 + 4 kappa) <= a0 <= 4D/(1 - 4 kappa).
Proof: (a) the integral equals a0/4 - D <= -D/2; (b) a0/4 - D >= -eps0 a0/4; (c) for a0 < 0 the modulus of the
integral is |a0|/4 + D > kappa |a0|, and for a0 > 0 the two-sided bound rearranges to the stated interval. Scope: no
bound on the third mode of this kind is known to hold for exact profiles; these are conditional statements.

3.49 Endpoint regimes c_l -> 1 and c_l -> inf (external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed by the
checker by an independent reconstruction, which gives the exact value 18342/4669 for the Gershgorin bound at m = 11/3
used in (a)). (a) Near c_l = 1 with bounded strain: by 3.44(ii) at one fixed m in (2, 4), for every K > 0 and
0 <= s < 1/2 there is an explicit eps(K, s) > 0 such that no exact profile has 0 < c_l - 1 < eps, |a0| <= K (c_l - 1)
and sigma <= s; with the Gershgorin bound Q_m^-+ <= 1/2 + b_2(m) + max(b_1(m), b_3(m)), m = 11/3 gives eps(1,
2/5) = 14007/88370 > 0.158. This is a form of 3.44(iii) uniform in c_l; it says nothing when sigma >= 1/2. (b) Large
c_l: after division of rho and U by c_l, a uniform bound on the suprema of both normalized gradients (of rho/c_l and
of U/c_l) gives locally uniform subsequential limits with linear growth solving (X + u) . grad q = 0, div u = 0, curl
u = -q_x. This limit system has the nonzero solutions q = f(y), u = (x, -y) for every smooth odd f with bounded
derivative, so no Liouville theorem holds in the class the limit inherits (the growth law U = o(r) is not inherited by
locally uniform limits, and the limit velocity is determined by q only up to b (x, -y)). Explicit smooth non-profiles
with the exact origin condition, a nonzero r^{1/c_l} far field and fixed a0/c_l have unbounded normalized gradient
suprema, so the structural hypotheses alone do not supply the uniform bound. (c) The c_l = 1 limit system (X + U) .
grad rho = rho, div U = 0, curl U = -rho_x has the nonzero solutions (a y, 0); a smooth solution with bounded first
derivatives, zero first jets at 0 (U(0) = 0, grad rho(0) = 0 and DU(0) = 0, so that rho(0) = 0; U(0) = 0 holds under
the parities) and global strain at most s < 1 vanishes (rho is flat at 0 by the jet equations, and backward orbits
contract at rate at least 1 - s). Applying this to a family needs smooth compactness and retention of a nonzero
derivative, which are not proved. (d) If a family with c_l -> 1 had a slowly varying all-radius representation rho = r
(D h(s) sin th + D^2 sum_{j >= 3 odd} H_j(s) sin(j th)), s = D log(r/l), valid for all real s, with
||h||_{C^3_b} + ||H_3||_{L^1} + sum_{j >= 3 odd} (1 + j)^4 ||H_j||_{C^3_b} <= M for a constant M independent of c_l,
then G_rho + G_U = O(c_l - 1), contradicting 3.44(ii) (G_rho + G_U >= (sqrt 2/3)(2 c_l - 1)). So no exact family has
this form, and the formal slow hierarchy cannot describe an exact family uniformly; the representation is an
additional hypothesis and does not locate or exclude inner layers at arbitrary radii. Scope: conditional statements;
none of (a)-(d) excludes a parameter interval without an extra hypothesis.

3.50 Capped non-profiles and capped local solutions (external analysis; hand-checked in the main
analysis; confirmed by the checker by independent reconstructions, with exact symbolic checks). Notation of 3.47. (a)
Unbounded slope under the cap. At c_l = 2 (D = 1), with C = 1179936, B >= 9, L = C B and delta = B/(L + 1)^2, the
density rho_B = 4 (1 - delta) y (1 + r^2)^{-1/4} + B y exp(-x^2/L^2 - y^2) with its canonical velocity has
psi_xy(0) = -1, sigma = M = 1 = D (|S(X)|_op <= 1 - min(r^2, 1)/294984), a0 = B + 4 (1 - delta), 0 < q <= 1 and |grad
rho| <= a0, and is not a profile (transport fails, for example at (0, 1)). So the cap and the pointwise inequalities
of 3.47(i) (|grad rho| <= |a0|, 0 < q <= 1 and the bounds on X . W, W_1/x, W_2/y and V/y), which 3.47(i) derives with
exact transport, can all hold for capped densities with arbitrarily large a0 when exact transport fails. The
monotonicity of |grad rho| along W stated in 3.47(i)
fails for this family (rho_y(0, 0) > 0 > rho_y(0, 1), so rho_y^2 increases along the y-axis beyond its zero, where
W_2 > 0). (b) Flat remainder under the cap. rho = 4 D y (1 - exp(-1/r^2))^beta, beta = D/(2 (1 + D)), is a capped
canonical non-profile whose remainder h is flat and nonzero, so 3.47(ii) uses exact transport essentially. (c) Local
exact solutions. For c_l > 1 and k > 0, rho = A y (1 + cos(k x)), psi = y (c_l x - (A/k) sin(k x)) satisfy -Lap
psi = rho_x and (c_l X + U) . grad rho = rho identically (W = ((A/k) sin(k x), y (2 c_l - A cos(k x))), and 2 c_l =
A + 1), with U(0) = 0, a0 = 2A and h = -(A k^2/2) x^2 y + O(r^5), so n = 3 and a0 = (n - 1) A. With w = 1 - cos(k x),
|S|_op^2 - D^2 = A w [-2D + A w + (A k^2 y^2/4)(1 + cos(k x))], so the cap holds on r <= (2/k) (D/A)^{1/2}. The pair
is not sublinear (rho(0, y) = 2 A y), so it is not in the class. It shows that the bound a0 >= (n - 1) A of 3.47 is
attained by local solutions, and that the equations together with the cap on a neighbourhood of 0, to every order, do
not exclude a0 = 2A. (d) Exact transport on a ball. For every c_l > 1, a0 > 4D and R > 0 there is a smooth canonical
pair with the parities, the far-field class with exponent 1/c_l, the global cap and F = W . grad rho - rho = 0 on
|X| < R: a radial base 4 D y f(r) equal to 4 D y near 0, plus a compactly supported remote pair (stream function (b/L)
f_*(x/L) g(y), b = a0 - 4D, L large) whose velocity vanishes on |x| < L and whose density equals b y on |x| < L,
|y| < 1; then rho = a0 y and W = (A x, y) on the unit disc, and a dilation rho -> l rho(X/l) enlarges the disc without
changing a0, sigma or the cap. By 3.47(ii) transport fails somewhere outside the disc; for large b the sign condition
rho/(a0 y) > 0 also fails. (e) The capped Gaussian family of (a) satisfies ||F_B||_3/||h_B||_3 >= (B/(B + 4))
(32/(15625 pi))^{1/2} > 1/100 for all B >= 9 (on the upper rectangle |x| <= 1, 1 <= y <= 6/5 one has x rho_x <= 0,
rho_y < 0 and |F_B| > rho_B > B/5, and by reflection |F_B| > |rho_B| > B/5 on the lower one; and |h_B| <= (B + 4) |y|
min(r^2, 1)). Here ||f||_m^2 = int f^2 |X|^{-2m} dX. So that family is not an approximate profile in this norm. Limits
(external analysis; confirmed by the checker by an independent proof): for each fixed 2 < m < 4, ||F_B||_m/||h_B||_m
tends as B -> inf to a positive limit R_m, with R_3 >= (e log 2)^{-1/2}; for the pairs of (d), the remote scale L ->
inf with b fixed, or with b proportional to L, also gives positive limits at every fixed m > 2. For each fixed member
of either family the ratio tends to 0 as m decreases to 2, since ||h||_m^2 = pi a0^2/(2 (m - 2)) + O(1) while ||F||_m
stays bounded; that statement changes the norm and is not a small defect in a fixed norm. Scope:
none of (a)-(e) bounds a0 for exact capped profiles or decides the capped subclass.

3.51 One-sided sign: local version, a trajectory criterion and jets without the cap (external analysis; hand-checked
in the main analysis, with 44 symbolic and numerical checks of the jet algebra; confirmed by the checker by
independent reconstructions, with exact checks of the recurrence, of the moments of the positive law and of the
leading equations). Notation of 3.47; rho is an exact profile of the primary class, and no strain cap is assumed; y
H >= 0 means rho/(a0 y) <= 1 off y = 0. (a) Local version of 3.47(iv): if h is
flat at 0 and r_d = inf{|X| : H(X) != 0}, then H y takes both signs in every disc |X| < R with R > r_d (on such a disc
the outer contributions are exponentially small in m relative to the inner mass). (b) Trajectory criterion:
q = rho/(a0 y) extends smoothly with q(0) = 1 and W . grad q = -q G, G = V/y = W_2/y - 1. If every backward orbit of W
tends to 0, then q(X) = exp(-int_{-inf}^0 G(X(t; X)) dt) > 0, so y H >= 0 holds exactly when all these backward
integrals are nonnegative; in particular, under the same hypothesis on backward orbits, W_2/y >= 1 everywhere
(equivalently U_2/y >= -D) gives 0 < q <= 1. (c) Jets without the cap: let h_n (n = 2K + 1 >= 3) be the first nonzero
homogeneous part of h, H_n = -h_n/a0 = sum_j c_j x^{2j} y^{n-2j} and e_j = n - 1 + 2j (A - 1). The leading equations
are equivalent to (n - 2j)(n - 2j - 1) e_j c_j + (2j + 2)(2j + 1)(e_{j+1} - a0) c_{j+1} = 0 (0 <= j < K), whose
solutions form a line, and y H >= 0 near 0 gives P(t) = sum_j c_j t^j >= 0 for t >= 0. Consequences: c_K > 0 and
prod_{j=1}^K (a0 - e_j) >= 0, so a0 >= e_1 = n - 1 + 2 (A - 1) when K is odd; if A <= n then a0 >= (n - 1) A, sharp
for jets (for a0 < (n - 1) A the solution has zero integral against a law on (0, inf) with positive density, a product
of a beta-prime and a beta variable, the beta factor being absent when A = n); for n = 5, a0 >= 4A when A <= 9, and
a0 >= 4A or a0 <= 2 (A^2 - 18 A + 1)/(A - 9) when A > 9. With 3.47(iv), every exact profile with y H >= 0 has
a0 >= (n - 1) A for its first degree n if 1 < c_l <= 3, and a0 >= 2A > 0 if 1 < c_l <= 5, with no cap. (d) Negative
slopes for jets: at c_l = 6 (A = 11), H_5 = y (y^2 - x^2/5)^2 with a0 = -76 solves the leading equations and y
H_5 >= 0, and every a0 <= -76 admits such a jet; so for c_l > 5 the sign-compatible leading equations do not give
a0 > 0. Scope: conditional statements, under the one-sided sign or under the dynamical hypothesis of (b); neither is
proved for the primary class.

3.52 Composition of 3.27 and 3.28 (external audit; the common domain and the repaired equal-weight step of A.3.27
confirmed by the checker). The space E of 3.27 can be taken to be the weighted Sobolev space E of 3.28, with the same
graph domain X0 = {h in E : P0 h in E} (both results use these spaces). Hence for an exact profile of the primary
class with (H-dyn), 3.28 supplies the Fredholm and index part of the hypothesis of 3.27 at every even order s >= 4
above the threshold,
and local uniqueness modulo scaling, in the Holder neighbourhood of 3.27, follows from the kernel hypothesis of 3.27
alone. Scope: kernel simplicity, (H-dyn) and existence remain open.

3.53 Angular monotonicity under the one-sided sign (proposed in an external audit; hand-checked in the main analysis;
confirmed by the checker by an independent proof and by exact checks: 2 angular identities, 210 recurrence identities
and 300 sign tests). No exact profile of the primary class has q = rho/(a0 y) <= 1 everywhere and q_th >= 0 on the
open first quadrant (th the polar angle). No positivity of q, strain cap, analyticity or coordinate monotonicity is
assumed. Since |grad rho| <= |a0| gives |rho| <= |a0| |y| (integrate vertically from rho(x, 0) = 0), and hence q <= 1,
this also excludes profiles with q_th >= 0 that attain their gradient maximum at the origin. Proof. Since q <= 1 is y
H >= 0, by 3.47(iv) h is not flat at 0, so q - 1 (smooth, even in x and in y) has a first nonzero homogeneous Taylor
part Q_{2k} = sum_{j=0}^k t_j x^{2j} y^{2k-2j}, k >= 1. Integration by parts in th in 3.43(i) (its angular weight is
-d/dth (cos th sin^3 th)) gives D/a0 = 1/4 + (4/pi) int_0^inf [ int_0^{pi/2} cos th sin^3 th q_th dth ] dr/r, and the
inner integral is nonnegative, so D/a0 >= 1/4 and 0 < a0 <= 4D. From q <= 1, Q_{2k} <= 0 and t_0 = Q_{2k}(0, 1) <= 0.
The leading part of q_th = (x d_y - y d_x) q is (x d_y - y d_x) Q_{2k} = 2 (k t_0 - t_1) x y^{2k-1} + O(x^3) near the
positive y-axis, so q_th >= 0 gives t_1 <= k t_0 <= 0. The recursion of 3.24(iii), which uses only the leading
transport and Poisson equations, gives at j = 1: 2 (a0 - d_1) t_1 = 2k (2k + 1) d_0 t_0 with d_0 = 2k > 0 and
d_1 = 4D + 2k > a0. The left side is nonnegative and the right side nonpositive, so t_0 = t_1 = 0; since d_j = 2j
(A - 1) + 2k increases in j, a0 - d_j < 0 for all j >= 1 and the recursion gives t_j = 0 for every j, a contradiction.
Scope: a subclass theorem. It does not exclude profiles with q <= 1 and q_th < 0 somewhere, nor profiles attaining
their gradient maximum at the origin without angular monotonicity; neither condition is known to hold for exact
profiles.

3.54 Angular variation under the one-sided sign (external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis with 18 symbolic
and numerical checks; confirmed part by part by the checker by an independent reconstruction, which also proves the
strict inequalities of (a); the main statement of (a), with the endpoint case, rederived independently in a second
external audit; the checker's supporting checks passed: 19 symbolic identities, 1625 recurrence cases, and Gaussian
and small-variation quadrature at 70 digits; the local gradient maximum of the cubic jet in (e) confirmed by the
checker). Put w(th) = cos th sin^3 th, q = rho/(a0 y), P(q) = int_0^inf int_0^{pi/2} w (q_th)_+ dth dr/r and
N(q) = int_0^inf int_0^{pi/2} w (-q_th)_+ dth dr/r; both are finite for every density of the primary class
(q = 1 + O(r^2) at 0, w |q_th| = O(r^{gamma - 1}) at infinity). The form of 3.43(i) used in 3.53 reads
-psi_xy(0)/a0 = 1/4 + (4/pi)(P - N) for every density of the primary class, hence D/a0 = 1/4 + (4/pi)(P - N) when
psi_xy(0) = -D, in particular for exact profiles. (a) If 1 < c_l <= 5, no exact profile of the primary class with
q <= 1 has N(q) <= pi/(16
A). Proof: by 3.51(c) a0 >= 2A, so N - P = (pi/4)(1/4 - D/a0) >= (pi/4)(1/4 - D/(2A)) = pi/(16 A), since A - 2D = 1;
if a0 = 2A then, by 3.51(c), the first part of h is h_3 = -a0 c x^2 y with c > 0, so q_th = 2 c r^2 sin th cos
th + O(r^4) > 0 on an open sector near 0 and P > 0. More generally, if a0 >= (n - 1) A for the first degree n of h
(for example 1 < c_l <= 3, or A <= n), then N(q) > pi ((n - 3) A + 2)/(16 (n - 1) A); and for 1 < c_l <= 5 under
q <= 1 the angular contrast of 3.43 satisfies A(q) > pi/(3 sqrt3 A). (b) For an exact profile (the identity uses
psi_xy(0) = -D, which comes from transport) with a0 > 0 and N(q) < pi/16 the identity gives a0 <= 4D/(1 - 16 N(q)/pi).
(c) On the range 1 < c_l <= 5 of (a), its angular hypothesis N(q) <= pi/(16 A) is strictly weaker than the angular
monotonicity of 3.53: q_eps = exp(-r^2) (1 - eps y^2/(1 + r^2)), eps = 1/(2A), has 0 < q_eps <= 1, (q_eps)_th < 0 on
the open quadrant and N(q_eps) < pi/(64 A) (with a_eps = D/(1/4 - 4 N(q_eps)/pi) < 2A the density a_eps y q_eps with
its canonical velocity has psi_xy(0) = -D and is not a profile: its cubic jet violates (T1) of 3.3). (d) Without
transport, the one-sided sign and the gradient maximum at 0 do not bound a0: for beta >= 1, rho_beta = D (1 + sqrt
beta)^2 y exp(-x^2 - beta y^2) with its canonical velocity has psi_xy(0) = -D, 0 < q <= 1 and |grad rho| <= a0, and is
not a profile (grad rho = 0 but rho > 0 on the y-axis at y^2 = 1/(2 beta), so transport fails there for any velocity).
(e) Jet level: at c_l = 2 and a0 = 13 the cubic part h_3 = -13 (x^2 y + (7/6) y^3) solves the leading equations with y
H >= 0 and the cubic density rho = 13 (y - H_3), H_3 = -h_3/13, has |grad rho| < a0 for 0 < r < 2 sqrt2/7 (since
(H_3)_y >= r^2 and |grad H_3|^2 <= (49/4) r^4), but q_th = -(1/3) r^2 sin th cos th < 0; at c_l = 19 and a0 = 2 a
quintic part with y H >= 0 and |grad rho| < a0 near 0 (punctured) solves them and has S_22 < -D on the diagonal near
0. So the leading equations with the one-sided sign and a local gradient maximum imply neither angular monotonicity
nor the cap. Scope: (a) is a subclass theorem; whether exact profiles with q <= 1 exist for c_l <= 5 remains open, and
no upper bound on a0 under q <= 1 alone is known.

3.55 Compactness and the strain cap (analysis of the checker, with supporting quadrature checks; reviewed in the main
analysis; confirmed in an external audit with 17 exact symbolic checks). Let rho_n, rho be smooth densities with the
symmetries, rho_n -> rho in C^1 on compact sets, with common constants C and 0 < gamma < 1 in |rho_n| + (1 + r) |grad
rho_n| <= C (1 + r)^gamma (the bound passes to rho). (a) The canonical velocities converge locally uniformly, and the
limit velocity satisfies |U| <= C' (1 + r)^gamma; if the gradients have a common Dini modulus on each compact set,
DU_n converges locally uniformly too. (b) If c_{l,n} -> c_l and sup |S_n|_op <= c_{l,n} - 1 + eps_n with eps_n -> 0,
then the limit has sigma <= c_l - 1 (no convergence of DU_n is needed: v^T S_n v, tested against a nonnegative test
function, is an integral of U_n after one integration by parts); if moreover the transport residuals R_n tend to 0
locally uniformly, the limit pair solves the profile equation, and rho_{n,y}(0) -> rho_y(0), which (b) alone does not
make nonzero. (c) C^1 convergence does not give strain convergence: for each c_l > 1 the canonical non-profiles
rho_n = 4D y exp(-r^2) + F_n - d_n J, where F_n consists of four reflected patches r sin(3 th) f(log r) of amplitude
1/n and logarithmic width n^2 near (+-3, +-3) and the fixed annular density J with coefficient d_n = O(1/n) keeps
psi_xy(0) = -D, converge in global C^1 at rate O(1/n) and agree with 4D y exp(-r^2) on a fixed neighbourhood of 0,
while |S_n(3, 3)|_op -> infinity; they are not profiles ((T1) of 3.3 fails: 6e - (a0 - 2A) b = -32D). (d)
Consequently, fix C, gamma, constants c_min > 1, c_max, a_min > 0 and eta > 0, and bounds on every C^k norm on every
ball B_j; among smooth canonical pairs obeying these bounds, with c_l in [c_min, c_max], |a0| >= a_min and
a0 <= 2A - eta, the sum of the local residual metric sum_j 2^{-j} min(1, sup_{B_j} |R|) and the strain excess max(0,
sigma - D) is bounded below by a positive constant depending on all the fixed bounds (compactness in C^inf_loc, then
(a)-(b), and 3.46-3.47: a capped exact profile has a0 >= 2A); no value of the constant is given. Scope: (d) applies to
the states of 4.7 (a0 < 2A, small sampled sigma - D) only under common local bounds that the computations do not
supply, and it does not exclude their approximating a profile without the cap; (c) concerns non-profiles.

3.56 First moment at the first degree under the one-sided sign (external analysis; confirmed by the checker by an
independent reconstruction, with exact checks of the test function, of the endpoint algebra and of 576 rational
leading cases; hand-checked in the main analysis; the written proof audited in a second external audit, which also
gave the identity without the sign stated in the Scope, hand-checked in the main analysis and exactly on all monomials
of degrees 3 to 9, and confirmed by the checker by an independent derivation). Notation of 3.47 and 3.51(c). Let rho
be an exact profile of the primary class with y H >= 0, let n >= 3 be the first degree of h (finite by 3.47(iv)) and
put C_n = int_0^{2 pi} H_n(om) sin th dth and T_n = C_n^{-1} int_0^{2 pi} cos^2 th H_n(om) sin th dth, om = (cos th,
sin th). Then C_n > 0, 0 < T_n < 1 and [a0 - (n - 1)(A - 1)] ((n + 3) T_n - 1) = (n - 1)^2; hence a0 < (n - 1)(A - n)
or a0 > (n - 1)(A - 1) + (n - 1)^2/(n + 2), both strict (with z = (n + 3) T_n - 1 in (-1, n + 2) the product
[a0 - (n - 1)(A - 1)] z = (n - 1)^2 is positive). Proof outline: for 2 < m < (n + 3)/2 the moments I_m and J_m of
3.47(ii) converge absolutely (H, V = O(r^n) at 0 and O(r) at infinity) and I_m > 0; the two tests of 3.47(ii) (the
Poisson relation Lap V = a0 H_xx against y r^{2-2m}, and transport against y r^{-2m}), with cutoffs at radii eps and R
whose errors are O(eps^{n+3-2m} + R^{4-2m}), give two expressions for J_m; after multiplication by n + 3 - 2m, letting
m increase to (n + 3)/2 leaves only H_n and gives lim J_m/I_m = a0 ((n + 3) T_n - 1)/(n - 1) and lim
J_m/I_m = n - A + (n + 3)(A - 1) T_n. The sign gives H_n sin th >= 0, not identically 0, so C_n > 0 and 0 < T_n < 1.
Scope: the identity does not need the sign. For every homogeneous solution (H_n, V_n) of degree n of the leading
equations V_n = (A x d_x + y d_y - 1) H_n, Lap V_n = a0 (H_n)_xx of 3.51(c) (any a0 and A, resonant values included),
with M_n = int_0^{2 pi} cos^2 th H_n(om) sin th dth, one has [a0 - (n - 1)(A - 1)]((n + 3) M_n - C_n) = (n - 1)^2 C_n:
integrating the first equation against sin th on the unit circle (by parts, using (cos th sin^2 th)' = 3 cos^2 th sin
th - sin th) gives int V_n sin th = (n - A) C_n + (n + 3)(A - 1) M_n, and integrating the second (on the unit circle
Lap V_n = n^2 V_n + V_n'', so its left side gives (n^2 - 1) int V_n sin th, and two integrations by parts give int
(H_n)_xx sin th = (n + 1)((n + 3) M_n - C_n)) gives (n - 1) int V_n sin th = a0 ((n + 3) M_n - C_n). For n = 3 it is
equivalent to (T1) of 3.3. The sign enters only through C_n > 0 and 0 < T_n < 1, so the dichotomy is a consequence of
the leading equations together with the full sign condition P >= 0 of 3.51(c); the moment argument of the proof
outline is a second proof of the identity. For A <= n the bound a0 >= (n - 1) A of 3.51(c) already implies the second
alternative, since (n - 1) A exceeds (n - 1)(A - 1) + (n - 1)^2/(n + 2) by 3 (n - 1)/(n + 2). For A > n the dichotomy
can sharpen the inequalities listed in 3.51(c), but need not (for n = 3 and A = 4 the jet bound a0 >= 8 already
implies a0 > 34/5); an example of a strict improvement: for n = 7 and A = 10 the inequalities a0 >= e_1 and prod_j
(a0 - e_j) >= 0 leave 24 <= a0 <= 42 or a0 >= 60, and the dichotomy (a0 < 18 or a0 > 58) removes [24, 42]. This is a
necessary condition on the subclass y H >= 0 and gives no upper bound on a0.

3.57 The first sine projection of transport (external analysis; confirmed by the checker by independent derivations,
with 19 exact checks; (c) obtained independently by the external analysis and by the checker, with 35 exact checks;
hand-checked in the main analysis, including the integral in (d)). Notation of 3.47 and 3.56: H = y - rho/a0,
phi = psi + D x y, v = (-phi_y, phi_x), V = v_2, mu = y H, G = V/y, om = X/r, B = X . W/r^2, beta = X . v/r^2,
R = W . grad rho - rho and R_1(r) = int_0^{2 pi} R(r, th) sin th dth. Let rho be a smooth density with the parities
and growth of the primary class and its canonical velocity, with a0 = rho_y(0) != 0 and psi_xy(0) = -D; transport is
not assumed. Let n >= 3 be an integer with H, V = O(r^n) at 0 (n = 3 always qualifies). (a) For 2 < m < (n + 3)/2, int
mu r^{-2m} Phi_m dX = (1/a0) int R y r^{-2m} dX = (1/a0) int_0^inf R_1(r) r^{2-2m} dr with Phi_m = a0 (2m
om_x^2 - 1)/(2(m - 2)) + A + 3 + G - 2m B, all integrals absolutely convergent. Hence the identities int mu r^{-2m}
Phi_m dX = 0 for all m in this interval (satisfied by every exact profile; they are the combination of the two tests
of 3.47(ii) used in 3.47 and 3.56) hold if and only if R_1(r) = 0 for every r > 0. (b) If 0 < a0 < (n - 1)(A - 1),
then m_* = 2 + a0/(2(A - 1)) lies in this interval, the om_x^2 coefficient of Phi_{m_*} vanishes, and for an exact
profile int mu r^{-2m_*}(G - 2m_* beta) dX = (a0/(A - 1)) int mu r^{-2m_*} dX. (c) Radial rigidity: if rho = y f(r),
the canonical stream is psi = -(1/2) r^2 J sin 2th with J = r^{-4} int_0^r t^3 f dt, the normalization psi_xy(0) = -D
forces a0 = 4D, and R_1/(pi r) = (c_l - J/2) r f' + D f - f^2/4; R_1 is not identically 0, so no such density
satisfies the identities of (a), and none is a profile. (d) At c_l = 2 let eta = 1/sqrt6 and a0 = 12 + 4 sqrt6. The
density rho = a0 y (1 + r^2)^{-1/4}(1 - eta y^2/(1 + r^2)) has 0 < q <= 1, psi_xy(0) = -D and (T1) of 3.3, but
R_1(r) -> pi a0^2 (3344 sqrt6 - 8231)/29568 < 0 as r -> inf. Proof outline: H, V = O(r^n) at 0 and O(r) at infinity,
and |R| <= C r^gamma, give absolute convergence. The two tests of 3.47(ii), with the transport identity W . grad
H - H - V = 0 replaced by W . grad H - H - V = -R/a0 and the same cutoffs, add to the identity of (a). The Mellin
transform of R_1 is holomorphic on -n < Re z < -gamma; if it vanishes at the points z = 3 - 2m, which fill (-n, -1),
it vanishes identically, and Fourier uniqueness on a vertical line gives R_1 = 0. (b) is the substitution m = m_*. In
(c), the sin 2th mode of -Lap psi = rho_x is a radial ODE solved by the stated psi, which is o(r) in velocity and
hence canonical; if R_1 = 0, then in t = log r the function k = 4D - f satisfies k' = lambda k with
lambda -> 2D/(c_l + 1) < 2 as t -> -inf, which is incompatible with k = O(r^2) unless k = 0 near 0, and then f = 4D
everywhere by uniqueness for the ODE system, which is not sublinear. In (d) the leading far-field terms of rho and psi
are computed in closed form, and the limit is an exact trigonometric integral. Scope: (a) is an identity for canonical
pairs and (b) holds whenever R_1 = 0, in particular for exact profiles; (c) excludes only the radial subclass; (d)
shows that the one-sided sign, the centre normalization and (T1) do not imply R_1 = 0, so adding the vanishing of the
family of (a) to these three conditions strictly restricts the class they define. None of these statements bounds a0
for the primary class.

3.58 Radial densities of finite regularity (obtained by the checker; rederived in the main analysis with 62 exact
symbolic checks and high-precision solutions of the radial equations for c_l = 1.1, 2, 3, 5 and 50; external audit:
(i) and (ii) correct; the moment identity used in (ii) is proved in Step 8 of A.3.58). Let rho = y f(r), J = r^{-4}
int_0^r t^3 f dt, and let dot denote r d/dr. (i) Suppose rho is C^1 on the plane, f is C^1 on r > 0 with
f(0) = a0 != 0, the growth bound of the primary class holds, U is the canonical velocity and (c_l X + U) . grad
rho = rho holds everywhere. These hypotheses are inconsistent: there is no radial profile even of class C^1, with no
sign or monotonicity assumption on f. (ii) For every c_l > 1 and lambda = 2D/(c_l + 1) (so 0 < lambda < 2, and
lambda < 1 if and only if c_l < 3) there is a one-parameter scale orbit of radial densities rho = y f(r) with
f = 4D - C r^lambda + O(r^{2 lambda}) at 0 (C > 0), f = K r^{p-1}(1 + O(r^{p-1})) at infinity (K > 0), 0 < f < 4D and
f' < 0 for r > 0, smooth off 0, with canonical stream psi = -x y J and psi_xy(0) = -D, such that R_1 = 0 at every
radius and R = r C3(r) sin 3th with C3(r) < 0 at every radius. At 0, rho and U are C^{1,lambda} and not C^2 if
lambda < 1, C^{1,1} and not C^2 if lambda = 1, and C^{2,lambda-1} and not C^3 if 1 < lambda < 2. Moreover
|grad rho| < a0 = 4D and ||sym DU||_op < D for X != 0 (with equality at 0), W is strongly monotone,
(W(X) - W(Y)) . (X - Y) >= |X - Y|^2, 0 < q < 1 for r > 0, and the identities of 3.57(a) hold for
2 < m < 2 + lambda/2. Consequences: in 3.57(c) the condition f - a0 = O(r^sigma) with sigma > 2D/(c_l + 1) cannot be
weakened to sigma = lambda; and R_1 = 0 together with the one-sided sign, the strain cap, the gradient bound and
strong monotonicity does not imply transport outside the smooth class. Proof outline: the residual of a radial density
is exactly r (C1 sin th + C3 sin 3th) with C1 = (c_l - J/2) f-dot + D f - f^2/4 = R_1/(pi r) and C3 = J f + (J/2)
f-dot - f^2/4, and the C^1 hypothesis suffices to identify psi = -x y J as the canonical stream and to obtain a0 = 4D.
In (i), C1 = C3 = 0 near 0 gives f = 2J + 2J/(c_l - J) and then (1 - v)(v^2 - v + 2 c_l) = 0 with v = c_l - J, so (f,
J) = (4D, D) near 0 and, by uniqueness for the equation C1 = 0, everywhere; rho = 4D y is not sublinear. In (ii) the
unstable branch of C1 = 0, J-dot = f - 4J at (4D, D), with eigenvalue lambda, is constructed by a contraction in
t = log r, stays in the invariant triangle 0 < f < 4D, f/4 < J < f/3, J < D, and decays like r^{p-1}; a
variation-of-constants argument gives J/f < 1/(4 - k) with k = -f-dot/f in (0, 1), hence C3 < -k f^2/(4(4 - k)) < 0.
Scope: (i) needs full transport; (ii) consists of non-profiles; neither concerns nonradial densities.

3.59 One-sided projected equations (external analysis; confirmed by the checker by an independent derivation with 1139
exact algebra checks). Let rho be smooth with the parities, a0 = rho_y(0) != 0 and the growth bound of the primary
class, let U be its canonical velocity, assume psi_xy(0) = -D and the one-sided sign mu = y H >= 0 (that is q <= 1;
q >= 0 is not assumed), and put B = X . W/r^2 and R_k(r) = int_0^{2 pi} R(r, th) sin k th dth. Transport is not
assumed; only the stated projections are. (i) If 1 < c_l <= 5, a0 > 0, R_1 = 0 at every radius and h = rho - a0 y is
not flat at 0, then a0 >= 2A, with equality only if the first nonzero Taylor term of H is alpha x^2 y, alpha > 0. (ii)
If R_1 = 0 at every radius and h is flat at 0, then r_* = inf{|X| : mu(X) > 0} is positive and finite, rho = a0 y on
the disc r < r_*, min over |X| = r_* of B is <= 0, and sup over X != 0 of -X . U/r^2 is >= c_l; in particular sup
||sym DU||_op <= D fails. (iii) If rho has only the sine modes 1, 3, ..., 2N + 1 (N >= 1) and
R_1 = R_3 = ... = R_{2N-1} = 0 at every radius, then h is not flat. (iv) If rho has only the modes 1 and 3 and
R_1 = R_3 = 0 at every radius, then 0 < a0 < 4(3 c_l + 1)(c_l + 3), for every c_l > 1. Consequences: for 1 < c_l <= 5,
every density of the class with the one-sided sign, the strain cap, a0 > 0 and R_1 = 0 has a0 >= 2A (by (i), and (ii)
excludes the flat case); for h not flat, the moment identity of 3.56 and its two alternatives hold with exact
transport replaced by R_1 = 0 (A.3.59, Steps 2 and 3). Proof outline: the identity of 3.57(a) and the endpoint
m -> (n + 3)/2 of 3.56 use only R_1 = 0, giving [a0 - (n - 1)(A - 1)]((n + 3) T_n - 1) = (n - 1)^2 at the first degree
n; (i) follows for n = 3 from H_3 = y (alpha x^2 + beta' y^2) with alpha > 0 and beta' >= 0, which gives
T_3 = (alpha + beta')/(2 (alpha + 3 beta')) and 0 < 6 T_3 - 1 <= 2 (A.3.59, Step 4), for n >= 9 from 0 < T_n < 1, and
for n = 5, 7 from T_n >= (2 - sqrt3)/4 (an exact six-point quadrature for the angular polynomials). In (ii) flatness
makes the two moment tests valid for every m > 2, and as m -> inf a positive lower bound on B near the support of mu
contradicts an upper bound on J_m/I_m that is uniform in m. In (iii) an affine disc carries only finitely many
interior harmonic stream modes, which the projections remove, so W = (A x, y) on the disc, contradicting (ii). In (iv)
the two leading projection coefficients give a 2 x 2 linear system for the leading coefficients of b_1, b_3;
eliminating the angular shape parameter gives the bound. Scope: necessary conditions on projected equations under the
one-sided sign; the theorem makes no existence assertion (the densities of 3.61 satisfy the hypotheses of (i) when
1 < c_l <= 5, and of (iii) with N = 1), (iv) is restricted to densities with the modes 1 and 3 on the whole plane
(with a fifth mode outside a disc and the projections imposed on the disc, the slope is unbounded, 3.63) and is not
uniform in c_l, and no statement bounds a0 from above for densities with unrestricted angular content or excludes the
full primary class.

3.60 No elliptical profiles (external analysis under the extra condition F <= 1; extended to every smooth F by the
checker, with an independent derivation and 1089 exact supporting checks; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed
in an external audit). No exact profile of the primary class has the form rho = a0 y F(alpha x^2 + beta y^2) with
alpha, beta > 0 and F smooth on [0, inf) (all right derivatives at 0 exist) with F(0) = 1. No sign, monotonicity or
analyticity of F is assumed, and such densities have in general infinitely many angular modes; alpha = beta is the
radial case of 3.57(c). Proof outline: the growth bounds on the y-axis give |F(s)| + s |F'(s)| <= C (1 + s)^{-delta}
with delta = (1 - gamma)/2, so F(s) -> 0 as s -> inf. The canonical stream is psi = -k x y int_0^inf F(s_t) omega(t)
dt, with k = a0 alpha/2, s_t = alpha x^2/(1 + alpha t) + beta y^2/(1 + beta t) and omega = (1 + alpha t)^{-3/2}
(1 + beta t)^{-3/2}, by the identity omega Lap[x y F(s_t)] = -4 x y d_t[F'(s_t) omega], the bound U = O(r^gamma) and
3.1. With I_K = int_0^inf (1 + alpha t)^{-K} omega dt, the centre normalization is k I_0 = D, and 0 < I_K < I_0 for
K >= 1. If F - 1 has a first nonzero Taylor term f_K s^K (K >= 1), the coefficient of x^{2K} y in the degree-(2K + 1)
part of transport gives 2KA = D (2K + 1) I_K/I_0 < D (2K + 1), contradicting 2KA - D (2K + 1) = (2K - 1) D + 2K > 0,
whatever the sign of f_K. If F - 1 is flat at 0, the y-derivative of transport on the x-axis is, in z = alpha x^2, the
equation 2z (A + k J_g) g' = k (1 + g)(J_g + 2z J_g') for g = F - 1, with J_g(z) = int_0^1 g(z u) w(u) du and a smooth
weight w >= 0 with int_0^1 w du = I_0; after an integration by parts in u the right side is bounded by the running
maximum of |g|, and a weighted uniqueness estimate near 0 followed by a Gronwall argument gives g = 0, so F = 1,
contradicting F(s) -> 0. Scope: a restricted shape class, excluded without any sign condition; this does not exclude
the full primary class.

3.61 The first projection and the one-sided sign do not bound the slope (external analysis; confirmed by the checker
by an independent reconstruction, with 790 exact supporting checks; the projection identity, the stream, the first
variation, the departure and trapping estimates and the cubic coefficient checked in the main analysis, the identity
also symbolically; confirmed in an external audit; the seventh projection, Step 7 of A.3.61, confirmed by the checker,
checked symbolically in the main analysis and confirmed in an external audit). Let c_l > 1, let n >= 0 be an integer
and put a0 = (8n + 6)(c_l + 1). There is eps_* > 0, depending on c_l and n, such that for every 0 < eps < eps_* there
is a density rho = r f(r) sin th + r g(r) sin 3th, smooth on the plane, with the parities of the primary class,
rho_y(0) = a0, growth |rho| + (1 + r) |grad rho| <= C (1 + r)^{1 - 2 eps}, canonical velocity U = O(r^{1 - 2 eps})
with psi_xy(0) = -D, the one-sided sign q = rho/(a0 y) <= 1, and R_1 = 0 at every radius. For n >= 1, R_3 is not
identically 0, and for every n >= 0, R_7 < 0 at every r > 0. Hence the vanishing of the first projection, together
with the one-sided sign, the centre normalization and the growth bound, does not bound a0 from above, even for
densities with the modes 1 and 3 only; by 3.59(iv), R_3 = 0 in addition does bound a0 for these two modes. Proof
outline: with M = a0/4 - D, T = M (1 + r^2)^{-eps} and g = -r T' = 2 eps M r^2 (1 + r^2)^{-eps - 1}, the canonical
stream is psi = (1/2) r^2 (T - J) sin 2th - (1/2) r^2 K sin 4th with J = r^{-4} int_0^r s^3 f ds and K = r^{-6}
int_0^r s^5 g ds, and R_1/(pi r) = L r f' - N with L = c_l + (T - J)/2 and N an explicit quadratic expression in f, g,
r g', T, J and K. So R_1 = 0 is an ODE system for (f, J) in t = log r. At eps = 0 it has the constant solution f = a0,
J = a0/4; for small eps a branch analytic in r^2 with f(0) = a0 follows from a contraction (the linearization in r^2
has the eigenvalues nu = 2n + 3/2 and -2, neither a positive integer). The first variation of f + 3g in eps is
explicit and negative, by the sign of a hypergeometric-type series at the half-integers nu, so f + 3g <= a0 on compact
sets. Differential inequalities show that f leaves a0 and reaches 2D before L can degenerate (eps log(1/eps) -> 0
controls the drift of T), after which a box 0 <= f <= 2D, 0 <= J <= a0/4, J - T <= D + (c_l + 1)/4 is invariant and
f = O(r^{-2 eps}). Since q extends smoothly to y = 0 and its maximum over th is (f + 3g)/a0, q <= 1. At the origin the
cubic Taylor coefficients give lim R_3/(pi r^3) = g2 [a0^2 - (4 c_l + 20) a0 + 64 A]/[4 (4 (c_l + 1) - a0)] with
g2 = 2 eps M, which is negative for a0 >= 14 (c_l + 1); the seventh projection is R_7 = pi r [K (r g' + 4 g) - 3
g^2/4], which is negative at every r > 0 because r g'/g decreases in r. Scope: these densities are not profiles (for
n >= 1 because R_3 is not identically 0, and for every n because R_7 < 0 and by 3.10, since they have two angular
modes); only R_1 = 0 is imposed, q >= 0 is not asserted, and the growth exponent depends on the member. For n = 0 the
displayed limit vanishes at one value of c_l, and no statement about R_3 is made there.

3.62 No profile of finite Cartesian separation rank (external analysis; proved independently by the checker, with 608
exact supporting checks; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed in an external audit). Let rho be an exact
profile of the primary class, p = 1/c_l, and rho_inf(X) = |X|^p Theta0(arg X) its far field (3.7). (i) rho_inf does
not have finite separation rank on the upper half-plane: there are no N and functions F_j on R and G_j on (0, inf)
with rho_inf(x, y) = sum_{j <= N} F_j(x) G_j(y) for all x in R and y > 0. (ii) Let Omega be a subset of {y > 0} that
contains, for each X with y > 0, the points R X for all large R (for example {y > 0, |X| > R0} or {y > y0}). There are
no N and functions F_j on R and G_j on (0, inf) such that E(X) = rho(X) - sum_{j <= N} F_j(x) G_j(y), defined for X in
Omega, satisfies R^{-p} E(R X) -> 0 as R -> inf for every X with y > 0; in particular rho is not a finite sum
sum_{j <= N} F_j(x) G_j(y) on Omega, and rho - sum_{j <= N} F_j(x) G_j(y) is not o(|X|^p) on Omega. No regularity,
sign or growth of the factors is assumed. Proof outline: the (N + 1) x (N + 1) matrices [R^{-p} (rho - E)(R x_i, R
y_k)] have rank at most N and tend entrywise to [rho_inf(x_i, y_k)], so V = span{rho_inf(., y) : y > 0} has dimension
at most N; by homogeneity, rho_inf(s x, y) = s^p rho_inf(x, y/s), V is invariant under the dilations T_s f = f(s .),
s > 0; on the finite-dimensional space W = {f - f(0) : f in V}, normed by finitely many point evaluations, the Holder
continuity of order alpha in (p, 1) at x = 0 (3.7) gives ||T_s|| <= C s^alpha and the growth bound |rho_inf(X)| <= C
|X|^p gives ||T_{1/s}|| <= C s^{-p} for small s, which is incompatible with T_s T_{1/s} = 1 unless W = 0; so
rho_inf(x, y) = rho_inf(0, y) = K y^p for y > 0, with K != 0 (3.6, 3.7), and then rho_inf(1, y) = K y^p for y > 0
contradicts the Holder continuity of order alpha > p at the point (1, 0). Scope: a restricted shape class (finite sums
of Cartesian separated functions, also outside a disk or on a half-plane y > y0, and up to errors o(R^p) along each
ray; hence also densities whose quotient rho/(a0 y) is a finite sum of separated functions), excluded without any sign
condition; exact transport enters only through the convergence of R^{-p} rho(R X) to the homogeneous far field rho_inf
of degree p in (0, 1), its axis coefficient K != 0 and the Holder continuity of Theta0 of some order above p (3.6,
3.7). The same argument excludes finite separation rank in linear coordinates (u, v) = M^{-1} X, M a fixed invertible
real 2 x 2 matrix, on {v > 0} outside a disc and up to errors o(R^p) along each ray (A.3.62, Remark (linear
coordinates)). Profiles of infinite separation rank are not excluded, nor is finite rank in nonlinear coordinates: in
u = x/y, v = y the far field rho_inf(u v, v) = v^p rho_inf(u, 1) has rank one.

3.63 Two projections with the one-sided sign on a disc do not bound the slope (external analysis; hand-checked in the
main analysis, with an independent symbolic check of all jet identities in Cartesian coordinates; confirmed by the
checker, by an independent reconstruction with exact checks, for every c_l > 1; confirmed in an external audit). Fix
c_l > 1, put D = c_l - 1 and I(a, lam) = a^2 - 4 ((c_l + 2) lam - D) a + 4 (c_l^2 + 4 c_l - 1) lam^2 - 8 D (c_l - 3)
lam, and let E_c be the set of real a with I(a, 2j) = 0 for some integer j >= 1; E_c is finite on every bounded
interval. For every a0 >= 100 (c_l + 1) not in E_c and every R > 0 there is a smooth compactly supported density rho
with the parities of Section 2 and only the sine modes 1, 3 and 5 such that rho_y(0) = a0, its canonical velocity has
psi_xy(0) = -D, the quotient q = rho/(a0 y), extended smoothly to y = 0, satisfies q(0) = 1 and q < 1 elsewhere,
R_1(r) = R_3(r) = 0 for 0 < r <= R, and R_5(r) = pi C5 r^5 + O(r^7) as r -> 0 with C5 < 0, so rho is not a profile. On
the disc r <= R the density has only the modes 1 and 3; the fifth mode is supported outside it and enters the disc
only through the harmonic stream term (H/2) r^4 sin 4th, H = int_0^inf k(s) s^{-3} ds > 0, where r k(r) is the fifth
sine coefficient. For c_l = 2 and 3 every a0 = 1000 + m + sqrt 2 with m >= 0 an integer is admissible. Proof outline:
on a small disc, f, g in rho = r (f sin th + g sin 3th) solve the regular singular radial system of R_1 = R_3 = 0 with
the canonical stream plus the term (H/2) r^4 sin 4th; a0 not in E_c is the nonresonance condition (16 times the
determinant of the order-j coefficient matrix is I(a0, 2j)), which gives an analytic solution; its cubic coefficients
rho = a0 y + b x^2 y + e y^3 + ... are b = -192 H a0/F(a0) < 0 and e = -32 H a0 (a0 - 4 c_l + 2)/F(a0) < 0 with
F(a) = I(a, 2) = a^2 - (4 c_l + 20) a + 128 c_l - 64 > 0, so q < 1 near 0; C5 is an explicit negative rational
