function of a0 and H; a cutoff, exterior bumps in the modes 3 and 5 that fix the upper integrals int_0^inf g/s
ds = a0/4 - D and int_0^inf k s^{-3} ds = H, and a negative first-mode bump under them keep q < 1 and leave the
density and the stream on the inner disc unchanged; a dilation rho -> l rho(X/l) enlarges the disc. Scope: the
projections are imposed only on the disc. Without the harmonic datum (H = 0, as for densities with the modes 1 and 3
on the whole plane) the cubic part of h = rho - a0 y vanishes unless F(a0) = 0, so the upper bound of 3.59(iv) depends
on the absence of the higher modes on the whole plane. With exterior higher modes permitted, imposing R_1 = R_3 = 0 on
a prescribed disc gives no upper bound on a0, even with q < 1 off 0, and for fixed R none depending only on c_l and R;
this does not decide whether imposing both projections at every radius gives such a bound. This construction does not
impose exact transport on the disc; 3.65(b) gives a different construction that does, with a nonzero cubic jet and the
strict one-sided sign (compare 3.50(d)). No existence or nonexistence conclusion is obtained for exact profiles of
the primary class.

3.64 No profile satisfies an exterior linear equation with constant coefficients (proposed in an external audit;
proved in the main analysis; confirmed by the checker by an independent proof with exact supporting checks; confirmed
in an external audit). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary class and p = 1/c_l. Let P(d) = sum_{j = m}^{d0}
P_j(d) be a linear differential operator on R^2 with constant complex coefficients, P_j homogeneous of order j and
P_m != 0 (P_m is the part of lowest order). There is no measurable, locally integrable function sigma, defined outside
a compact set B, with P(d) sigma = 0 in the sense of distributions on R^2 \ B and either (a) sup_{|X| = r}
|rho - sigma| = o(r^p) as r -> inf, or (b) |rho - sigma| <= C (1 + |X|)^p outside B and, for almost every X, R^{-p}
(rho - sigma)(R X) -> 0 as R -> inf. In particular (sigma = rho) no nonzero linear differential operator with constant
coefficients annihilates rho outside a compact set (for example rho is not harmonic or polyharmonic outside a disc),
and sup_{|X| = r} |rho - sum_{j <= N} h_j(l_j . X + b_j)| is not o(r^p) for any finite sum of ridge functions with h_j
locally integrable on R, l_j in R^2 \ {0} and arbitrary directions (such a sum is annihilated by prod_j (v_j . grad)
with v_j != 0, v_j . l_j = 0). Proof outline: the rescalings sigma_R(X) = R^{-p} sigma(R X) converge to the far field
rho_inf = |X|^p Theta0(arg X) in distributions on R^2 \ {0}, and the rescaled equation sum_j R^{m - j} P_j(d)
sigma_R = 0 gives P_m(d) rho_inf = 0 there (the large-scale limit selects the part of lowest order); P_m(d) rho_inf is
then supported at 0 and homogeneous of the noninteger degree p - m, hence 0; the Fourier transform of rho_inf is
smooth off 0 (rho_inf is smooth off 0, 3.23, and homogeneous) and vanishes off the zero set of P_m(i xi), which has
empty interior, so it is supported at 0, rho_inf is a polynomial, and a polynomial homogeneous of degree p in (0, 1)
is 0, contradicting K != 0 (3.6). Scope: a restricted class (exterior solutions of one fixed linear equation with
constant coefficients, and approximations by them in the sense (a) or (b)), excluded without any sign condition; exact
transport enters only through 3.6, 3.7 and 3.23 (convergence to a nonzero homogeneous far field of degree p in (0, 1),
smooth off 0). The smoothness off 0 is essential: K sign(y) |y|^p is homogeneous of degree p, nonzero on the y-axis
and annihilated by d_x, but not smooth across y = 0. The result does not subsume the exclusions of finite Cartesian
separation rank (3.62) and of finite angular support (3.10), and its class is not contained in theirs (a test density,
not a profile, whose far field has three square-root cusp lines; A.3.64, Scope); it says nothing about operators with
variable coefficients or about general profiles.

3.65 Finitely many projections, or exact transport, on a disc with the one-sided sign do not bound the slope (external
analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis, with independent symbolic checks of the stream formula, the matrices, the
determinant recursion, the norm estimates and the jets through degree 11; confirmed by the checker, by an independent
reconstruction with exact checks, for N >= 2; confirmed in an external audit, with local repairs). Fix c_l > 1 and put
D = c_l - 1. For lam > 0 let P_0 = 1, P_1(lam, a) = (c_l + 1) lam/2 - a/4 and P_d = (c_l lam + D - a/2)
P_{d-1} - Q_{d-2} P_{d-2} (d >= 2), Q_k = ([2D (lam + 2) - a]^2 - 16 D^2 (k + 1)^2)/16. For an integer N >= 2 let E^N
be the set of real a with P_{min(N, j+1)}(2j, a) = 0 for some integer j >= 1, and let E^inf be the set of real a with
P_{j+1}(2j, a) = 0 for some j >= 1. These sets are finite on every bounded interval, and E^2 = E_c of 3.63 (16
P_2(lam, a) = I(a, lam)). (a) For every integer N >= 2, every a0 >= 4 c_l + 20 not in E^N and every R0 > 0 there is a
smooth compactly supported density rho with the parities of Section 2 and only the sine modes 1, 3, ..., max(2N - 1,
5) such that rho_y(0) = a0, its canonical velocity has psi_xy(0) = -D, the quotient q = rho/(a0 y), extended smoothly
to y = 0, satisfies q(0) = 1 and q < 1 elsewhere, the cubic part of rho - a0 y is b x^2 y + e y^3 with b < 0 and
e < 0, and R_1(r) = R_3(r) = ... = R_{2N-1}(r) = 0 for 0 < r <= R0. (b) For every a0 >= 4 c_l + 20 not in E^inf and
every R0 > 0 there is a density with the same properties, with no restriction on its sine modes, such that R = 0 on
the disc r <= R0 (exact transport there). If c_l is an integer >= 2, every rational element of E^N and of E^inf is an
integer (4^d P_d(2j, a) is a polynomial in a with integer coefficients and leading coefficient (-1)^d, so its rational
roots are integers), and every a0 >= 4 c_l + 20 that is rational and not an integer is admissible in (a) for every N
and in (b). None of these densities is a profile: at a positive maximum of rho, R = -rho < 0. Proof outline: on a
disc, if the upper moments of the density are fixed as M_1 = a0/4 - D, M_2 = H > 0 and M_m = 0 for m >= 3, the
canonical stream of rho = a0 y + h, h a convergent sum of homogeneous parts of odd degree, is psi = -D x y + (H/2) r^4
sin 4th + P h with an explicit local inverse P on each degree; the part of degree 2j + 1 of the residual is L h_{2j+1}
plus terms of lower degree in h, and the matrix of L on the sine modes of that degree is tridiagonal, with determinant
P_{j+1}(2j, a0) (its compression to the first d modes has determinant P_d(2j, a0)); a binomial weighting W gives
||W^{-1} L W x||_inf >= (2j - |a0|) ||x||_inf for the matrix L of that degree, so the weighted matrix is strictly
diagonally dominant when 2j > |a0| (not in general for small j) and only finitely many degrees can be resonant, and a0
outside E^N (or E^inf) excludes them; a contraction in a binomial coefficient norm gives a convergent series whose
cubic part, forced by the harmonic term, has b = -192 H a0/F(a0) < 0 and e = -32 H a0 (a0 - 4 c_l + 2)/F(a0) < 0 with
F as in 3.63, so q < 1 near 0 off 0; a cutoff, exterior bumps in the modes 3, 5, ... that restore the moments, and a
negative first-mode bump under them keep q < 1 and leave the density and the stream on the inner disc unchanged; a
dilation rho -> l rho(X/l) enlarges the disc. Scope: the projections, or the full equation, are imposed only on a
disc. For N = 2 the threshold 4 c_l + 20 is lower than the threshold 100 (c_l + 1) of 3.63, but the statement of 3.63
on R_5 is not obtained; for N = 1 the construction gives no cubic jet, and 3.61 gives R_1 = 0 at every radius with
unbounded a0. Compared with 3.50(d), which has exact transport on a disc with rho = a0 y there, (b) has the strict
sign q < 1 off 0 on the whole plane and a nonzero cubic jet. Thus no finite number of projections, and not exact
transport, imposed on a prescribed disc together with the one-sided sign and the centre normalization, gives an upper
bound on a0, and for fixed R0 none depending only on c_l and R0. The excluded slopes are not decided, the
constructions are not uniform in a0, and no existence or nonexistence conclusion is obtained for exact profiles of the
primary class.

3.66 No exact profile has finite angular support outside a disc (proved by the checker, with exact supporting checks,
and independently in an external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed in an external audit, with
local repairs). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary class. There are no R0 > 0 and odd N >= 1 such that rho(r,
th) = sum_{j odd, j <= N} f_j(r) sin j th for all r > R0. For R0 = 0 this is 3.10 (which A.3.10 proves by a different
argument). Given the symbol bounds of 3.23 and Theta0 != 0 (3.7), the proof uses c_l > 1, the canonical velocity and
its parities, the smoothness needed for the interior moments of the Green formula 3.1(iv), and the equation only for
large r; this does not assert that 3.7 and 3.23 themselves need only exterior information. Proof outline: with B = U .
grad rho and T f(X) = (1/c_l) int_1^inf t^{-p-1} f(t X) dt, the equation gives rho = r^p Theta0 + T B for large r, T
preserves the classes of functions whose derivatives of order k are O(r^{b-k}) for b < p, and Theta0 is a
trigonometric polynomial; an exterior inverse lemma gives the canonical velocity of a density with finite exterior
angular support that is a finite sum of terms r^s (log r)^d G(th) up to a remainder of order r^b, as a finite sum of
terms of the same degrees, harmonic terms r^{-2m} sin 2m th in the stream and a remainder of order r^b (the infinitely
many stream modes produced by the interior are harmonic outside a disc and their sum converges geometrically);
iterating, rho and U have unique finite expansions of this kind to every depth. A density term of degree p - t has t
in {k delta + 2 l : k, l >= 0} (delta = 1 - p) and angular frequency at most n + (n + 1) t/delta, n the highest
frequency of Theta0; the harmonic terms stay strictly below this bound, and equality occurs only at t = k delta and
the frequency n_k = (k + 1)(n + 1) - 1, whose coefficient A_k in front of r^{(k + 1) p - k} sin n_k th is a constant
with k D A_k = sum_{i + j = k - 1} c_ij A_i A_j, c_ij = (1/4) [1 - 2 (j + 1)(n + 1)/((i + 1)(n + p) + 2)],
D = c_l - 1. Since c_ij + c_ji < 0 and c_ii < 0, A_k = (-1)^k a^{k + 1} b_k with b_k > 0, a the coefficient of sin n
th in Theta0, which contradicts the support assumption once n_k > N. Scope: excluded is finite angular support with
one N on a whole exterior region; this result alone does not cover densities whose angular frequencies have no uniform
bound outside every disc. Result 3.67 shows that in every exact profile the number of nonzero modes on the circle of
radius r tends to infinity, and gives asymptotic lower bounds for finite-mode approximations; finitely many modes on
each circle, with a number growing with r, are not excluded by what is proved here, and general profiles of the
primary class are not excluded.

3.67 A finite leading trace forces infinitely many angular modes, and the number of modes tends to infinity (proved by
the checker, with exact supporting checks; hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed in external audits, with local
repairs). Let rho be an exact profile of the primary class and rho_j(r) = (1/pi) int_0^{2 pi} rho(r, th) sin j th dth.
(a) Suppose that the trace Theta0 (3.23) is a trigonometric polynomial, let n be its highest frequency and a != 0 its
coefficient of sin n th, and let n_k = (k + 1)(n + 1) - 1, s_k = (k + 1) p - k and A_k = (-1)^k a^{k + 1} b_k
(b_k > 0) be as in 3.66 and A.3.66. Then for every k >= 0 there is eps_k > 0 with rho_{n_k}(r) = A_k
r^{s_k} + O(r^{s_k - eps_k}) as r -> inf, and d_r^j rho_{n_k}(r) = d_r^j (A_k r^{s_k}) + O(r^{s_k - eps_k - j}) for
every j >= 1. (b) Consequently, if N >= n is odd, k is the first index with n_k > N and P(r, th) is any function whose
angular modes are sin j th with j <= N (for instance Pi_N rho, the projection of rho on these modes), then
liminf_{r -> inf} r^{-s_k} sup_th |rho - P| >= (pi/4) |A_k| and liminf_{r -> inf} r^{-s_k} (int_0^{2 pi} |rho - P|^2
dth)^{1/2} >= sqrt(pi) |A_k|: rho has nonzero modes of arbitrarily high frequency at large radii, and the part of rho
above any fixed frequency is not O(r^b) for any b < s_k. (c) With no assumption on Theta0, let C(r) be the number of
odd j with rho_j(r) != 0 (possibly infinite). Then C(r) -> inf as r -> inf: for every M there is R_M with C(r) > M for
r > R_M, so the number of modes is not bounded on any sequence of radii tending to infinity, even if the frequencies
may vary with the radius. More precisely, let E_M(r) be the infimum of sup_th |rho(r, th) - P(th)| (respectively of
the L^2(0, 2 pi) norm of rho(r, .) - P) over all sums P of at most M sine modes, with frequencies and coefficients
chosen freely for each r. Then liminf_{r -> inf} r^{-p} E_M(r) >= (pi/4) min_{j in J} |theta_j| (respectively sqrt(pi)
min_{j in J} |theta_j|) for every set J of M + 1 frequencies at which the coefficients theta_j of Theta0 are nonzero;
in fact r^{-p} E_M(r) converges to the corresponding distance from Theta0 to the set of sums of at most M sine modes.
Under the hypothesis of (a), if Theta0 has N_0 nonzero coefficients and M >= N_0, then liminf_{r -> inf} r^{-s_{M_1}}
E_M(r) >= (pi/4) |A_{M_1}| (respectively sqrt(pi) |A_{M_1}|) with M_1 = M + 1 - N_0 >= 1. Nothing is assumed about the
angular content of rho - r^p Theta0. The proof (A.3.67) is that of A.3.66 with its exterior inverse lemma replaced by
a lemma without any assumption on angular support: if f is smooth with the parities and lies in S^b outside a disc
(b < 1, b != -2m - 1 for every integer m >= 1), its canonical stream is a finite sum of harmonic terms (J_m/(4m))
r^{-2m} sin 2m th with -2m - 1 > b, J_m = int_0^inf s^{2m+1} g_m ds (g_m the sin 2m th coefficient of f_x), plus a
remainder whose derivatives of order k are O(r^{b + 1 - k}); (c) then follows by a counting argument. 3.66 is the
special case of finite angular support outside a disc, where Theta0 is a trigonometric polynomial and rho_{n_k}
vanishes for large r once n_k > N. Scope: these are necessary conditions; profiles whose trace is a trigonometric
polynomial are not excluded (they must carry the infinite tail described). The radius beyond which rho_{n_k} != 0 may
depend on k, and (a)-(c) do not give infinitely many nonzero modes on any one circle; the asymptotic statements alone
cannot give that, since a smooth function with the parities, finitely many modes on every circle, the symbol bounds
and every coefficient asymptotic of (a) exists, also with a nonzero slope at the origin (A.3.67; it is not a profile).
When Theta0 has infinitely many modes, (a) and (b) say nothing, since the argument needs a highest frequency of the
trace, and only the coefficients at the top frequencies n_k are controlled. The lower bounds concern r -> inf and do
not restrict approximations on bounded regions.

3.68 Far-field expansions for an arbitrary smooth trace (proved by the checker, with exact supporting checks;
hand-checked in the main analysis; confirmed in an external audit, with a local repair). Let rho be an exact profile
of the primary class or, more generally, a smooth function with the parities of Section 2 whose canonical velocity U
satisfies the profile equation outside a disc, with rho and U in S^p (S^b as in Section 2 and A.3.66) and r^{-p}
rho(r, .) -> Theta0 uniformly; nothing is assumed on the angular content of Theta0 or of rho, and Theta0 = 0 is
allowed. Put delta = 1 - p, Sigma_rho = {p - k delta - 2l : k, l >= 0 integers} and
Sigma_H = {-2m - 1 : m >= 1 an integer}. (a) Theta0 is smooth and r^{-p} rho(r, .) -> Theta0 in C^j(S^1) for every j.
(b) For every b < p outside Sigma_rho and Sigma_H there are finite sums rho = sum_{s in Sigma_rho, s > b} r^s
P_s(log r, th) + E_b and U = sum_{s in Sigma_rho or Sigma_H, s > b} r^s V_s(log r, th) + F_b, with E_b and F_b in S^b,
where each P_s and each polar component of V_s is a polynomial in log r whose coefficients are smooth 2 pi-periodic
functions of th, and P_p = Theta0; the velocity terms of degree p carry no logarithm; the coefficients are unique
after collecting equal degrees and powers of log r, and the expansions for different b agree on their common degrees.
(c) If delta = 1 - 1/c_l is irrational, no logarithm occurs, each degree in Sigma_rho has a unique label (k, l), and
Sigma_rho and Sigma_H are disjoint. If delta = u/v in lowest terms, a logarithm is created only by the inversion of a
density term of degree p - k delta - 2l = -2m - 1 with m >= 1, in the stream mode sin 2m th, which requires (k + 1)
u = 2 v J for an integer J >= 1 and m = J + l - 1 >= 1; this lists possible resonances only (the projection of the
source on the resonant mode can vanish); once created, a logarithm propagates through products, the transport
inversion and nonresonant inversions to lower degrees of rho and U, which need not be of this form (for c_l = 3, 3.69
gives density logarithms of degree -11/3). Proof outline (A.3.68): the construction of A.3.66 and A.3.67 with
trigonometric polynomials replaced by smooth periodic functions. A term r^s (log r)^d G(th) is inverted mode by mode,
the Fourier coefficients of its source being divided by 4m^2 - (s + 1)^2, which vanishes only in the single mode with
s = -2m - 1 (at most one more power of log r there); comparison with the canonical stream of a compactly supported
source gives the global harmonic terms, with geometrically convergent tails; Theta0 is smooth because the functions
r^{-p} rho(r, .) are bounded in every C^j. Scope: necessary conditions on the far field of every exact profile; for
arbitrary angular content no coefficient below the leading one is shown to be nonzero (unlike 3.67(a)), while the
leading coefficient P_p = Theta0 is nonzero for an exact profile of the primary class (3.7; the more general exterior
class allows Theta0 = 0); the harmonic coefficients are global data of rho and are not determined by Theta0; no
convergence of the infinite expansion and no control of the constants as the depth grows is asserted; existence is not
decided.

3.69 A pure first-mode trace forces far-field logarithms for c_l = 3 and c_l = 5/2 (proved by the checker, with exact
supporting checks; hand-checked in the main analysis, with an independent exact recomputation of the resonant
coefficients; confirmed in an external audit, with local wording repairs). Let rho satisfy the hypotheses of 3.68 with
Theta0 = A sin th, A != 0. (a) Every density degree of the expansion in 3.68(b) is p - k delta - 2l with l = 0 or
l >= 2: a harmonic velocity term, of degree -2m - 1, lowers the density degree by 2m + 2 >= 4. (b) Let (c_l, k_*,
m) = (3, 5, 1) or (5/2, 9, 2), so that p - k_* delta = -2m - 1. For k <= k_* the coefficient of r^{p - k delta} in rho
is a sine polynomial P_k(th) determined by A and c_l alone through a finite recurrence (A.3.69), and the coefficient
g_* of r^{-2m-2} sin 2m th in the x derivative of r^{-2m-1} P_{k_*} is g_* = -(177047/301056000000) A^6 for c_l = 3
and g_* = (26243642326438735772269905591088207/4898218301752285282303033607434666157015040) A^10 for c_l = 5/2. (c)
Consequently the canonical stream contains the term (g_*/(4m)) r^{-2m} log r sin 2m th and the density contains the
term -(A g_*/(8 c_l (m + 1))) r^{p - 2m - 2} log r [delta sin (2m - 1) th + (1 + p) sin (2m + 1) th], both nonzero;
these are the first logarithmic terms of the stream and of the density. For c_l = 3 the density term is r^{-11/3} log
r (-(A g_*/72) sin th - (A g_*/36) sin 3 th), and for c_l = 5/2 it is r^{-28/5} log r (-(A g_*/100) sin 3 th - (7 A
g_*/300) sin 5 th). Proof outline (A.3.69): by (a), no harmonic term reaches the pure degrees p - k delta with
k <= k_*, so the coefficients there are those of the recurrence started at A sin th; the resonant inversion of A.3.68
Step 2'' turns the source g_* into the logarithmic stream, and its velocity acting on A r^p sin th forces the density
logarithm; harmonic terms carry no logarithm and cannot cancel either term. Scope: this shows that the logarithms
admitted by 3.68(c) actually occur for these traces and values of c_l; a logarithm at infinity is compatible with
smoothness on R^2, so no profile is excluded; traces with other angular content are treated in 3.71.

3.70 Transport identities with weights depending on (r, rho) (external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis;
proved independently by the checker, with exact supporting checks; confirmed in an external audit, whose local repairs
are applied). Let rho be smooth on R^2, even in x and odd in y, with a0 = rho_y(0) != 0 and the growth bound of the
class, let U be its canonical velocity, c_l > 1, p = 1/c_l, W = c_l X + U, U_r = U . X/r, and E = W . grad rho - rho;
no profile equation is assumed. (i) For every Phi in C_c^inf((0, inf) x R), with Phi and its partial derivatives
evaluated at (r, rho(X)),
    int_{R^2} [2 c_l Phi + (c_l r + U_r) Phi_r + rho Phi_s] dX = -int_{R^2} E Phi_s dX.   (1)
Hence the identities obtained for an exact profile by integrating div(W Phi(r, rho)) = 2 c_l Phi + (c_l r + U_r)
Phi_r + rho Phi_s over the plane hold for every such Phi if and only if the image of the measure E dX under X -> (r,
rho(X)) is zero; at a regular value s of rho(r, .) this is the vanishing of the sum of E/|rho_th| over the points of
the circle of radius r at which rho = s. (ii) Near 0, rho_th = x (a0 + O(r^2)). For r small and s strictly between the
minimum and the maximum of rho(r, .), the points of that circle where rho = s are two mirror images under x -> -x, at
which E takes the same value; so the condition of (i) forces E = 0 on a disc around 0. At other radii the condition is
that, for every r, the image of E(r, th) dth under th -> rho(r, th) vanishes; at regular levels this is the sum in
(i), and any part carried by critical levels must vanish as well. No pointwise conclusion away from the disc is proved
here. (iii) For an exact profile and the weights r^alpha |rho|^beta with beta > 0 and -2 - beta < alpha < -2 - beta p,
the integrals M(alpha, beta) = int r^alpha |rho|^beta dX and V(alpha, beta) = int r^{alpha - 2} (U . X) |rho|^beta dX
converge absolutely and V = ((2 + alpha) c_l + beta) M/(-alpha) < 0; at alpha = -2 - beta p, M diverges, V converges
and alpha V = c_l int_0^{2 pi} |Theta0|^beta dth. These signs do not follow from the canonical coupling and the data
at 0 and at infinity: put a = 4 (c_l - 1) and rho_t = A_t(r) sin th with A_t(r) = a r (1 + r^2)^{(p - 1)/2} + t f(r),
f >= 0 smooth, not identically zero, supported in 1 < r < 2. Each rho_t has the parities and the growth of the class,
a0 = a, Theta0 = a sin th, canonical stream -(2 r^2)^{-1} (int_0^r s^2 A_t(s) ds) sin 2 th and
psi_xy(0) = -a/4 = 1 - c_l; for fixed admissible (alpha, beta), V(alpha, beta) of rho_t has the sign of -t for |t|
large, and for each single such (alpha, beta), and for the endpoint identity at a single beta, some rho_t satisfies
the identity (the parameter t depends on the identity, and simultaneous satisfaction of several identities is not
claimed). No rho_t is a profile: independently of t, its residual near 0 is E = r^3 [a (p - 1) sin th + (a^2
(p - 1)/12) sin 3 th] + O(r^5), with a nonzero coefficient of r^3 sin 3 th. So these identities, one at a time, are
satisfied by smooth canonical non-profiles sharing the data c_l, a0 = 4 (c_l - 1), psi_xy(0) = 1 - c_l and Theta0 = a
sin th, and the whole family of (i) is the vanishing of the image of E dX, at regular levels a statement about
conditional means of the residual on level sets, which near 0 is the profile equation itself. Whether a smooth
canonical density with the parities of the class and E != 0 satisfies the condition of (i) for every Phi is not
decided here.

3.71 The resonant coefficient for traces with other angular content (the parts proved by the checker, with exact
supporting checks; the combined statement and proof checked by the checker and in an external audit, both with the
same local repairs, the audit recomputing the numbers in (a), (b) and (c) independently in exact arithmetic; (b) and
(d) hand-checked in the main analysis, with an independent recomputation of the radii in (b); (c), including the
leading coefficients, computed independently in the main analysis). Let (c_l, k_*, m) be as in 3.69(b), K = k_*, and
let X_t (t >= 0 an integer) be the space of traces with the inherited parities, Theta = sum over odd n >= 1 of a_n sin
n th, with ||Theta||_t = sum_n (1 + n)^t |a_n| finite. For Theta in X_K let P_k[Theta] (k <= K) be given by the
recurrence of A.3.69 started at P_0 = Theta in place of A sin th (so P_k[Theta] lies in X_{K-k}), and let g[Theta] be
-2m times the coefficient of sin (2m - 1) th in P_K[Theta]; for smooth Theta this is the coefficient of r^{-2m-2} sin
2m th in the x derivative of r^{-2m-1} P_K[Theta]. If rho satisfies the hypotheses of 3.68 with Theta0 = Theta, then
the coefficient of r^{p - k delta} in rho is P_k[Theta] for k <= K, and g[Theta] is the resonant source coefficient of
3.69(b): 3.69(a) and the radial arithmetic of A.3.69 do not depend on the angular content. (a) Dependence on high
modes. For Theta = sin th + eps sin N th with N odd and N > 4K + 4, g is a polynomial in eps whose coefficient of eps
vanishes and whose coefficient of eps^2 is a rational function of N, nonzero at N = 101 for both values of c_l; hence
for every N0 there are odd N > N0 with g[sin th + eps sin N th] != g[sin th] for all small eps != 0, and no finite set
of Fourier coefficients of Theta determines g. This holds even among traces positive on 0 < th < pi: since |sin N
th| <= N sin th there, sin th + eps sin N th > 0 on 0 < th < pi for |eps| < 1/N. (b) Continuity. g is locally
Lipschitz for ||.||_K, with explicit rational constants (A.3.71), and if ||Theta - A sin th||_K <= eps0 |A| with
A != 0, then g[Theta] has the sign of g[A sin th] and |g[Theta]| >= |g[A sin th]|/2; here eps0 is an explicit
rational, about 2.18e-21 for c_l = 3 and 3.04e-53 for c_l = 5/2. These radii are sufficient conditions, not tolerances
for a computed state. (c) Cancellation. For Theta_eps = sin th + eps sin 3 th, which is positive on 0 < th < pi for
0 <= eps < 1, g[Theta_eps] is a polynomial of degree K + 1 in eps, with leading coefficient -336578601/34112798720 for
c_l = 3 and a positive rational, about 0.015266, for c_l = 5/2. For c_l = 3 a positive multiple of it is
    -176703765525000 eps^6 + 222533688701250 eps^5 - 96180432855375 eps^4 + 20675598499400 eps^3
        - 2783057141280 eps^2 + 243275209320 eps - 10532171936,
with exactly two real zeros in (0, 1), near 0.28066 and 0.64635; for c_l = 5/2 it has exactly four real zeros in (0,
1), near 0.06595, 0.10934, 0.35056 and 0.59420; all these zeros are simple. (d) If rho satisfies the hypotheses of
3.68 with Theta0 = Theta, Theta is not identically zero and g[Theta] != 0, then the stream contains (g[Theta]/(4m))
r^{-2m} log r sin 2m th and the density contains the nonzero term -(g[Theta]/(4 c_l (m + 1))) r^{p - 2m - 2} log r [p
cos 2m th Theta + sin 2m th Theta'], and these are the first logarithmic terms. Scope: by (c), positive smooth traces
can have g = 0, and then the logarithmic terms displayed in (d) are absent; later logarithms are not ruled out. By
(b), nonvanishing of g is stable under perturbations small in ||.||_K, with explicit sufficient radii around A sin th;
by (a), the value of g is not determined by any finite set of Fourier coefficients of the trace. All conclusions
concern the exterior expansion of a profile assumed to exist; none of (a)-(d) constructs or excludes a profile.

3.72 Exact anisotropic rescaling by the slope, and the large-slope limit of the canonical inverse ((a) and (b)
proposed in the main analysis; (a)-(d) proved by the checker, with numerical checks; (a), (b), the phenomenon of (c)
with a second example, and versions of (d) and (e) under bounds on all derivatives derived independently in an
external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis, with a numerical check of the strain formulas of (c); confirmed
in an external audit, whose local repairs are applied, and the repaired text, including (e), confirmed by the
checker). Let a0 != 0, s = sgn a0, h = |a0|^{1/2} and eps = 1/|a0|. (a) Put x = h xi, rho(x, y) = a0 g(xi, y), psi(x,
y) = h Phi(xi, y) and V = (-Phi_y, Phi_xi) = (U_1/h, U_2). Then rho is a profile of the class with slope a0 and
exponent c_l if and only if g is smooth, even in xi and odd in y, satisfies the growth bounds of the class in the
variables (xi, y), and
    (c_l xi + V_1) g_xi + (c_l y + V_2) g_y = g,   -Phi_yy - eps Phi_xixi = s g_xi,   g_y(0) = 1,   (1)
with Phi odd in both variables and V = o(|(xi, y)|); for each eps > 0 this velocity is unique. The centre strain is
unchanged, psi_xy(0) = Phi_xiy(0), so the origin condition reads Phi_xiy(0) = 1 - c_l. If rho = a0 y + b x^2 y + e
y^3 + O(r^5), then g = y + B xi^2 y + E y^3 + O(|(xi, y)|^5) with B = s b and E = e/a0, and (T1) of 3.3 becomes
6E = (s - 2 A eps) B. On the y-axis g(0, y) ~ (K/a0) y^p with K/a0 > 0 (3.6), and the representative with L_K = 1
(that is K = a0) has g(0, y) ~ y^p. So the slope is an anisotropy parameter: a profile with slope a0 is a solution
with unit slope of the problem whose elliptic operator is -d_y^2 - eps d_xi^2, and |a0| -> inf is formally the
hydrostatic limit -Phi_yy = s g_xi. For fixed a0 the map is a change of coordinates, not a symmetry of the profile
equation. (b) For c_l > 1 and K != 0, rho = K sgn(y) |y|^p with U = 0 solves the profile equation in the sense of
distributions on R^2. It is Holder continuous of order p, not C^1 on the x-axis, violates the gradient bound of the
class as x -> inf at fixed y != 0, and is outside the class (its trace K sgn(sin th) |sin th|^p is excluded as a far
field by 3.7). It is a candidate singular outer state at fixed K: identifying it as a limit of smooth profiles would
need matching and convergence arguments, and no such approximation is proved here (3.7 excludes this trace for each
profile, but not convergence of smooth traces to it without uniform angular regularity). (c) For inputs with only the
density and gradient bounds of the class, the canonical centre strain of (1) need not stay bounded as eps -> 0, and a
sublinear hydrostatic inverse need not exist. For 0 < gamma < 1, g = exp(-xi^2) y (1 + y^2)^{(gamma - 2)/2} is smooth,
has the parities, g_y(0) = 1 and the density and gradient bounds with exponent gamma, but for s = 1 its canonical
centre strain satisfies eps^{gamma/2} Phi_xiy(0) -> -2 Gamma(2 - gamma) Gamma(gamma)/Gamma(1 - gamma/2) < 0, and no
velocity of sublinear growth with the parities solves -Phi_yy = g_xi. The external analysis finds the same rate, with
the limit constant -2 B(gamma, 3 - gamma) (B the Beta function), for y (1 + y^2)^{(gamma - 2)/2}/(1 + xi^2). These
functions are not profiles. (d) One more bound gives the limit. Let 0 < gamma < 1 and let g be smooth with the
parities, |g| <= C (1 + r)^gamma, |grad g| <= C (1 + r)^{gamma - 1} and |g_xixi| <= C (1 + r)^{gamma - 2}, r = |(xi,
y)|, and let V_eps be the canonical velocity of -Phi_yy - eps Phi_xixi = g_xi. Then |V_eps| <= C' (1 + r)^gamma with
C' depending only on C and gamma, and as eps -> 0, V_eps converges locally uniformly to the velocity V_0 given for
y >= 0 by
    V_0,1 = -int_y^inf g_xi(xi, t) dt,   V_0,2 = int_0^y t g_xixi(xi, t) dt + y int_y^inf g_xixi(xi, t) dt,   (2)
which is the unique velocity with the parities and sublinear growth solving -Phi_yy = g_xi; moreover
Phi_eps,xiy(0) = int_0^inf (P_{sqrt(eps) t} * g_xixi(., t))(0) dt -> int_0^inf g_xixi(0, t) dt, where P_a(z) = a/(pi
(a^2 + z^2)) and * is the convolution in xi. The limiting stream Phi_0(xi, y) = int_0^inf min(y, t) g_xi(xi, t) dt is
C^1, Phi_0,yy exists and is continuous and -Phi_0,yy = g_xi holds classically; no regularity of the full velocity
gradient is asserted. The same convergence holds for inputs g_eps that converge in C^2 on compact sets and obey the
three bounds with common C and gamma. (e) Conditional consequence. Let rho_n be exact profiles with a0,n -> +inf and
c_l,n -> c_lim, and suppose that representatives g_n (in the sense of (a)) satisfy the three bounds of (d) with one C
and one gamma in (0, 1) and converge in C^2 on compact sets to g_lim. By 3.6 and the density bound, c_l,n >= 1/gamma,
so c_lim >= 1/gamma > 1. Then g_lim is a C^2 density which, with the velocity V given by (2), solves the hydrostatic
profile problem
    (c_lim xi + V_1) g_xi + (c_lim y + V_2) g_y = g,   -Phi_yy = g_xi,   g_y(0) = 1,   (3)
pointwise, with the three bounds, |V| <= C' (1 + r)^gamma and the stream regularity stated in (d), and int_0^inf
g_xixi(0, t) dt = 1 - c_lim. Hence: fix C > 0, 0 < gamma < 1, a compact interval J and finite constants C_R (R > 0),
and suppose that for no c_lim in J does (3), with the velocity (2), have a C^2 density satisfying the three bounds
with these C and gamma. Then there is M = M(J, C, gamma, (C_R)) such that no exact profile with c_l in J and a0 >= M
has a representative satisfying the three bounds with C and gamma and |D^3 g| <= C_R on each disc of radius R. A
conclusion for every C and gamma needs the nonexistence premise for every C and gamma. The report establishes neither
nonexistence for (3) nor the uniform estimates needed to apply this argument to all large-slope profiles, and by (c)
the bounds of the class alone do not give the limit of the inverse. For a0,n -> -inf (s = -1) the limiting velocity is
minus the velocity (2), the stream equation is -Phi_yy = -g_xi, the centre condition is int_0^inf g_xixi(0, t)
dt = c_lim - 1, and the same argument applies to this signed problem. Scope: (a) and (b) are exact statements; (c)-(e)
concern the inverse operator and conditional limits; these results neither construct a profile of the class nor give
an unconditional nonexistence theorem for it. For the computed states of 4.7(c), 2 A eps = 10/a0 lies between 0.451
and 0.507, so the correction in the exact cubic identity 6E = (s - 2A eps) B is not small.

3.73 The hydrostatic problem on the axis, the evolution in xi, and three excluded forms ((a)-(d) derived in an
external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; independently proved by the checker with symbolic and
high-precision checks; confirmed in an external audit, whose local repairs are applied, and the repaired text
confirmed by the checker). Let c > 1, p = 1/c and D = c - 1, and let g be a C^2 density, even in xi and odd in y, with
g_y(0) = 1 and the three bounds of 3.72(d) for some C and 0 < gamma < 1, which with the velocity V of (2) of 3.72
solves (3) of 3.72 with c_lim = c. For y >= 0 put G(y) = g(0, y) and v(y) = c y + V_2(0, y). (a) Axis reduction. On
the axis V_1 = 0, and
    v G' = G,   v'(y) = c + int_y^inf g_xixi(0, t) dt,   v'' = -g_xixi(0, .),   v'(0) = 1,   v(y)/y -> c;   (1)
v, G and G' are positive on (0, inf), and for every R > 0
    int_0^R (1 - t/R) g_xixi(0, t) dt = 1 - v(R)/R,  which tends to 1 - c as R -> inf.   (2)
So the centre condition int_0^inf g_xixi(0, t) dt = 1 - c of 3.72(e) is the relation v'(0) = 1, which the axis
equation forces, and g_xixi(0, y) >= 0 for all y > 0 is impossible. Since v(y) - c y = V_2(0, y) = O(y^gamma),
integrating G'/G = 1/v gives G(y) = K y^p (1 + O(y^{gamma - 1})) as y -> inf with 0 < K < inf; the density bound then
requires p <= gamma, that is c >= 1/gamma. If g is C^3 near 0 and g = y + B xi^2 y + E y^3 + o(r^3), then (1) gives
B = 6E, the case eps = 0 of 3.72(a). (b) The axis conditions select neither G nor c. For every c > 1 the odd
real-analytic functions v(y) = c y - D arctan y and G(y) = y exp(int_0^y (1/v(t) - 1/t) dt) satisfy v G' = G,
v'(0) = 1, v(y)/y -> c, v'' > 0 on (0, inf), G' > 0 and 0 < G(y) <= y on (0, inf), G(y) ~ K y^p with 0 < K < inf, and
G = y - (D/6) y^3 + O(y^5). If phi is odd and smooth with support in [-y2, -y1] u [y1, y2], 0 < y1 < y2, and its C^2
norm is below a constant depending on c, y1 and y2, then v + phi and the function G defined from it by the same
formula are smooth and odd and have all these properties except real analyticity (with a constant K that may change),
so for each c the axis data compatible with (1), (2) and these signs form an infinite-dimensional family. They are
axis data, not solutions of (3); for a prescribed gamma they satisfy the growth bound of G only when c >= 1/gamma. (c)
Formal expansion and evolution in xi. Write h = V_1, a = c xi + h and b = c y + V_2; then h_y = g_xi, b_y = c - h_xi
and a g_xi + b g_y = g. For a formal calculation take smooth odd axis data G with G' > 0 and seek formal series
g = G + xi^2 g_2 + xi^4 g_4 + ..., h = xi h_1 + xi^3 h_3 + ..., b = v + xi^2 b_2 + ... with smooth coefficient
functions solving these three identities. They are determined by G: h_1 = c - v', g_2 = -v''/2, b_2 = ((4c - 1 - 2v')
v'' + v v''')/(2 G'), and for k >= 1 each b_{2k} is obtained by dividing by G', h_{2k+1} = -b_{2k}'/(2k + 1) and
g_{2k+2} = -b_{2k}''/((2k + 1)(2k + 2)). So at fixed c the formal data are one odd function G, subject to the
conditions of (a). This is not an assertion that a C^2 solution has an expansion of all orders in xi; convergence of
the series (by 3.75(b) it fails at a given axis point for generic analytic axis data near the function G of 3.73(b)),
compatibility with the formula (2) of 3.72 and the global bounds are further requirements, and the calculation gives
neither existence nor uniqueness of a solution. Where q = g_y > 0, the equations give the evolution system g_xi = h_y,
h_xi = c - d_y((g - a h_y)/q) in xi. Its linearization at a solution, (u, z) for (g, h) at fixed c, is u_xi = z_y,
z_xi = -d_y((u - h_y z - a z_y - b u_y)/q); with coefficients frozen at an axis point (0, y0), y0 > 0, the
characteristic roots lambda at vertical frequency eta satisfy lambda^2 = -i (v(y0)/G'(y0)) eta^3 + O(eta^2), so Re
lambda = +-(v(y0)/(2 G'(y0)))^{1/2} |eta|^{3/2} + O(|eta|^{1/2}), and the frozen Cauchy problem with data on the axis
satisfies no Sobolev estimate with any fixed finite loss of derivatives, also for data with z = 0. This is a statement
about the frozen system: it does not establish ill-posedness or nonexistence for the variable-coefficient nonlinear
problem (3), and a construction by continuation from the axis would need estimates that this calculation does not
supply. (d) Excluded forms. No g as above has any of the forms (i) g = y F(alpha xi^2 + beta y^2) with alpha, beta > 0
and F a function on (0, inf); (ii) g = f(xi) G_0(y); (iii) g(X) = l g(X/l) for all X and one l in (0, 1) or (1, inf).
Under the scalings (xi, y, g) -> (lambda xi, mu y, (lambda^2/mu) g) with lambda, mu > 0, which map solutions of (3)
without the normalization g_y(0) = 1 to solutions, the normalization forces lambda = mu, so (iii) contains invariance
under any nontrivial scaling of this kind. Scope: these results give necessary conditions and exclude the three stated
forms; they establish neither existence nor nonexistence for the full hydrostatic problem (3) and provide no uniform
estimates for sequences of exact profiles of the kind required in 3.72(e).

3.74 The hydrostatic problem: isopycnal form, leading far field, no regular expansion at c = 1, and formal far-field
terms ((a)-(c), the conditional moment identity in (d) and the compactness statement of (e) proved under their stated
hypotheses, the far-field expansion of (d) and the linearization and selection statements of (e) formal; derived in an
external analysis; hand-checked in the main analysis; independently proved by the checker with symbolic and
manufactured checks; confirmed in an external audit, whose local repairs are applied, and the repaired text confirmed
by the checker). Let c, p, D, g, G, v and K be as in 3.73, A = 2c - 1, and h = V_1, a = c xi + h and b = c y + V_2 as
in 3.73(c), so that h_y = g_xi, b_y = c - h_xi and a g_xi + b g_y = g; let k(xi) = g_y(xi, 0), let r, th be polar
coordinates of X = (xi, y), and write V[u] = (V_1[u], V_2[u]) for the formulas (2) of 3.72 applied to a function u.
(a) Boundary law and isopycnal form. If k(xi) > 0 for all xi, then, with a_0(xi) = a(xi, 0),
    a_0 k' = (a_0' - A) k,   a_0(xi) = A k(xi) int_0^xi dt/k(t),   k(xi) = L |xi|^{p - 1} (1 + O(|xi|^{gamma - 1}))  (|xi| -> inf)   (1)
with a constant 0 < L < inf. If g_y > 0 on {y >= 0}, then for each xi the map y -> g(xi, y) is an increasing bijection
of [0, inf) onto itself; with y = Y(xi, sigma) its inverse, Z = Y_sigma and H(xi, sigma) = h(xi, Y(xi, sigma)),
    d_xi((c xi + H) Z) + sigma Z_sigma = A Z,   H_sigma = -Y_xi,   H(xi, sigma) = int_sigma^inf Y_xi(xi, s) ds,   (2)
with Y(xi, 0) = 0, Z(xi, 0) = 1/k(xi), Z(0, 0) = 1 and H_sigma(xi, 0) = Z_sigma(xi, 0) = 0, and at fixed xi, as
sigma -> inf, Y ~ (sigma/K)^c, Z ~ c K^{-c} sigma^{c - 1} and H -> 0. Moreover, for sigma_1 > 0,
    int_0^inf Y_xixi(0, sigma) dsigma = D,   d_xi int_0^{sigma_1} (c xi + H) Z dsigma + sigma_1 Z(xi, sigma_1) = 2c Y(xi, sigma_1),   (3)
and, without a sign condition on g_y, M(xi) = int_0^inf (G(y) - g(xi, y)) dy converges and is C^2, with M' = h(xi, 0)
and M''(0) = D. These identities give no sign estimate for Z_xi and establish no maximum-principle argument excluding
g_y > 0: by (2), (c xi + H) Z_xi + sigma Z_sigma = (D - H_xi) Z, where H_xi is taken at fixed sigma and has no known
sign. No restriction on c beyond 3.73(a) is obtained here. (b) Leading far field. There is a continuous function Theta
of the angle, with Theta(pi - th) = Theta(th) = -Theta(-th), Theta(pi/2) = K and |Theta(th)| <= C'' |sin th|, such
that
    g = r^p Theta(th) + o(r^p)   as r -> inf, uniformly in th;   (4)
in particular |g| <= C' (1 + r)^p. If g_y > 0 on {y >= 0}, then Theta > 0 on (0, pi) and Theta(th) = L th + o(th) as
th -> 0+, with L of (1). The proof gives no convergence of derivatives of r^{-p} g and no asymptotics of V; on a fixed
annulus the second xi-derivatives of R^{-p} g(R X) are only O(R^{gamma - p}). Since p < 1, the bound
|Theta(th)| <= C'' |sin th| excludes K sgn(sin th) |sin th|^p as the entire trace; it does not exclude agreement with
that function near th = pi/2. (c) No regular expansion at c = 1. If a family of solutions g_D of (3) of 3.72 with
c = 1 + D satisfied g_D = y + D u + O(D^2) in C^1 on compact sets and V[g_D] = D V[u] + O(D^2) uniformly on compact
sets, with V[u] defined and u satisfying the conditions of the following theorem, then u would solve (5) below.
Theorem: there is no C^2 function u on R^2, even in xi and odd in y, with |u(X)| <= C (1 + r)^q for some 1 < q < 2,
such that int_y^inf u_xixi(xi, t) dt converges for all xi and all y >= 0 and
    (X . grad - 1) u + V_2[u] = -y   on {y >= 0}.   (5)
In particular no such first-order coefficient of size O(r log r) exists. This is not a nonexistence statement for
small D > 0: it excludes only an expansion of this regular form. By 3.73(a), a family of solutions with c -> 1+ also
needs gamma >= 1/c, so gamma -> 1. For comparison, the functions K_D y^{1/(1 + D)} on y > 0, with K_D = 1 + kappa_1
D + O(D^2), do not depend on xi, have zero velocity and solve the transport equation of (3) of 3.72 on y > 0; their
first-order coefficient y (kappa_1 - log y) is not C^1 at y = 0. (d) Formal far-field terms (formal, except the moment
identity below, which is proved under its hypothesis: they assume an expansion g = f_p + f_{2p-1} + ..., f_p = r^p
Theta(th) with Theta smooth, that may be differentiated and inserted in the formulas (2) of 3.72 term by term, the
velocity formulas being used termwise only where the integrals converge). The terms of degree 2p - 1 in (3) of 3.72
give
    f_{2p-1} = (V[f_p] . grad f_p)/D,   f_{2p-1}(0, y) = K Q y^{2p - 1}/((1 - p) D),   Q = p K + Theta''(pi/2),   (6)
since (f_p)_xixi(0, y) = Q y^{p - 2} and V_2[f_p](0, y) = Q y^p/(p (1 - p)). The degrees d_n = n p - (n - 1) generated
by the nonlinearity have c d_n - 1 = -(n - 1) D != 0 for n >= 2, so no transport resonance occurs among them. For a
homogeneous term of degree d <= 0 with nonzero axis curvature Q_d y^{d - 2} the axis integral int_0^y Q_d t^{d - 1} dt
diverges, so its velocity requires matching to a regular core; at d = 0 a nonzero axis curvature Q_0 y^{-2} gives Q_0
log y in V_2 after this matching. Hence the values c = n/(n - 1), where d_n = 0, are possible logarithmic cases;
whether a logarithm occurs is not determined here (at c = 2, under the hypotheses of 3.77(d), the axis curvature of
the term of degree 0 vanishes and V_2(0, y) has no logarithm). If int_0^inf t |g_xixi(0, t) - Q t^{p - 2}| dt < inf
for some constant Q, then V_2(0, y) = Q y^p/(p (1 - p)) + m_0 + o(1) as y -> inf (a proved statement), with
m_0 = int_0^inf t (g_xixi(0, t) - Q t^{p - 2}) dt, and formally m_0 contributes K m_0 c^{-2} y^{p - 1} to G (under the
hypotheses of 3.77(c) and (d), m_0 = 0 for c > 2 and m_0 = C_0(f_0) for c = 2; by 3.78(d) the moment hypothesis fails,
formally, in the presence of the nonzero leading layer of 3.78). Near the vertical axis, with F(s) = f_p(1, s),
q(s) = p (p - 1) F(s) - 2 (p - 1) s F'(s) + s^2 F''(s) and the finite number C_p(Theta) = int_0^inf s (q(s) - Q
s^{p - 2}) ds, V_2[f_p](xi, y) = Q y^p/(p (1 - p)) + C_p(Theta) |xi|^p + O(xi^2 y^{p - 2}) as xi/y -> 0, so f_{2p-1}
contains p K C_p(Theta) |xi|^p y^{p - 1}/D, which is not differentiable in xi at xi = 0; an expansion of this kind
with coefficients that are C^1 in xi near the vertical axis therefore requires C_p(Theta) = 0 (3.77(b)-(d) give this
condition for solutions under explicit far-field hypotheses; for C_p(Theta) != 0, 3.78 treats formally a near-axis
layer that is smooth at the axis). (e) Selection of c and compactness. At fixed c the dilations g -> l g(X/l) map
solutions to solutions (3.73(d)), so the function g - X . grad g, which is not zero by 3.73(d)(iii), lies formally in
the kernel of the linearization L_g u = (c X + V[g]) . grad u - u + V[u] . grad g (for a C^2 solution, g - X . grad g
is only C^1 and its velocity is not automatically defined classically); a variation c_1 of c enters as L_g u + c_1
X . grad g = 0 and, at fixed Theta, changes the leading term of (4) by -c_1 p^2 r^p Theta(th) log r, so for c_1 != 0
this formal leading variation is not O(r^p). The results of 3.73 and (a)-(d) do not determine existence or the number
of solution classes modulo dilation, and give no rule selecting c: the axis-data families of 3.73(b) and the trace
Theta are function-valued data whose compatibility with a global solution has not been established, and the frozen
estimate of 3.73(c) concerns a Cauchy problem, not a boundary problem. Compactness (proved): let c_n -> c > 1 and let
g_n be C^3 functions, even in xi and odd in y, with d_y g_n(0) = 1, the three bounds of 3.72(d) with one C and one
gamma, |D^3 g_n| <= C_R on each disc of radius R, and (c_n xi + V_1[g_n]) d_xi g_n + (c_n y + V_2[g_n]) d_y
g_n - g_n -> 0 uniformly on compact subsets of {y >= 0}; then a subsequence converges in C^2 on compact sets to a
solution of (3) of 3.72 with c_lim = c in the class of 3.73. Scope: (a)-(c), the conditional moment identity in (d)
and the compactness statement in (e) are proved under their stated hypotheses, for solutions of (3) of 3.72 in the
class of 3.73 (and (c) for the stated functions u); they establish neither existence nor nonexistence for (3), select
no c and give no uniform estimates for the exact profiles of 3.72(e); the far-field expansion of (d) and the
linearization and selection statements of (e) are formal.

3.75 The hydrostatic problem: local analytic solutions from the bottom, divergence of the horizontal series from the
axis, a representation at the source, and no sign of the cusp coefficient ((a)-(c) and (e) proved, (d) formal; (a)-(d)
derived in an external analysis and (e) obtained by the checker; hand-checked in the main analysis; (a)-(c)
independently proved and (d) independently checked by the checker with symbolic and numerical checks; confirmed in an
external audit, whose local
repairs are applied, and the repaired text confirmed by the checker). Let c > 1, p = 1/c, D = c - 1 and A = 2c - 1. By
the local system we mean the equations
    h_y = g_xi,   b_y = c - h_xi,   (c xi + h) g_xi + b g_y = g   (1)
for a triple (g, h, b) of functions with g even in xi and odd in y, h odd in xi and even in y, and b even in xi and
odd in y. (a) Data on the bottom. (i) Let g be C^2 on {y >= 0} with these parities, g_y(0) = 1 and the three bounds of
3.72(d), and let h be C^1 on {y >= 0} and b continuous there with a continuous partial derivative b_y, such that (1)
holds, b(xi, 0) = 0 and h(xi, y) -> 0 as y -> inf for every xi. Then h = V_1 and b = c y + V_2 with V given by (2) of
3.72, so g solves (3) of 3.72 with c_lim = c; conversely every solution of (3) of 3.72 in the class of 3.73 gives such
a triple, with h = V_1 and b = c y + V_2. (ii) Let k be an even real-analytic function on R with k > 0 and k(0) = 1,
and put zeta(xi) = int_0^xi dt/k(t), a_0 = A k zeta and h_0 = a_0 - c xi, so that a_0 k' = (a_0' - A) k as in (1) of
3.74. For every R > 0 there is a real-analytic triple (g, h, b) solving (1) on a neighbourhood of [-R, R] x {0} with
g(xi, 0) = 0, g_y(xi, 0) = k(xi), h(xi, 0) = h_0(xi) and b(xi, 0) = 0, and any two real-analytic triples solving (1)
with g(xi, 0) = 0, g_y(xi, 0) = k(xi) and b(xi, 0) = 0 on connected neighbourhoods of [-R, R] x {0} agree on the
component of their common domain that contains [-R, R] x {0}. The height of the neighbourhood is bounded below in
terms of the complex extension of k (A.3.75); no common positive height on the whole line is claimed. In g = sum_n
g_{2n+1}(xi) y^{2n+1} the coefficients are determined by k: g_1 = k and, for n >= 1, a_0 g_{2n+1}' + ((2n + 1)
b_1 - 1) g_{2n+1} = F_n with b_1 = 1 - a_0 k'/k and F_n a polynomial in g_1, ..., g_{2n-1} and their derivatives
(F_1 = -k'^2/2 + k k''/6), and each of these equations has exactly one solution that is bounded near xi = 0. So a
solution of (3) of 3.72 in the class of 3.73 with g_y(xi, 0) = k(xi) has these coefficients in its Taylor expansion in
y at the bottom if it is C^inf near the bottom, and coincides with the triple of (ii) near [-R, R] x {0} if it is real
analytic there; for such solutions the remaining requirements are global: continuation to {y >= 0}, the three bounds
and h(xi, y) -> 0 as y -> inf. Whether a C^inf or C^2 solution is determined by k is not known. (b) Divergence of the
horizontal series from the axis. For odd smooth axis data G with G' > 0, put v = G/G' and Q_G = G/G'^2; then the
coefficients of 3.73(c) satisfy g_{2n} = Q_G^n G^{(3n)}/(2n)! + R_n for n >= 1, where R_n depends only on G, G', ...,
G^{(3n - 1)}. Fix y_0 > 0, let G_* be the axis function of 3.73(b) for this c, and for delta > 0 and alpha > 0 let B
be the real Banach space of odd holomorphic functions phi on the strip |Im z| < delta, real on the real axis, with
phi'(0) = 0 and finite norm sup |exp(alpha z^2) phi(z)| over the strip. For delta small and an open ball N about 0 in
B small enough, every G = G_* + phi with phi in N has G'(0) = 1 and G' > 0 on R, and v = G/G' has v'' > 0 on (0, inf)
and v(y) - c y = O(1), so that G(y) ~ K_G y^p with 0 < K_G < inf; and the set of such G for which limsup_n
|g_{2n}(y_0)|^{1/(2n)} = inf contains a countable intersection of dense open subsets of G_* + N. For such G the series
sum_n g_{2n}(y_0) xi^{2n} has radius of convergence zero, so no triple solving (1) that is real analytic near (0, y_0)
has g(0, y) = G(y) near y_0. Whether the series for G_* itself diverges is not decided, and divergence excludes only
real analyticity near the axis point, not C^inf solutions with these axis data. So, unlike the bottom data k in (a),
analytic axis data near G_* do not in general generate real-analytic local solutions. (c) A representation at the
source. Let g be a solution of (3) of 3.72 in the class of 3.73 with g_y > 0 on {y >= 0}, and let Y, Z and H be as in
3.74(a). Then, for a constant C', |h_xi(xi, y)| <= C' (1 + |xi| + y)^{gamma - 1} and |h(xi, y)| <= C'
((1 + |xi|)^gamma - 1) on {y >= 0}; H is C^1 on {sigma >= 0}; every backward trajectory of the vector field T = (c
xi + H) d_xi + sigma d_sigma in {sigma >= 0} tends to (0, 0); and
    Z(P) = exp( int_{-inf}^0 (D - H_xi)(P_tau) dtau ),   (2)
where tau -> P_tau is the trajectory of T with P_0 = P, H_xi is taken at fixed sigma (H_xi = h_xi - g_xi^2/g_y at
y = Y), and the integral converges absolutely. So Z is determined by H, and H is a fixed point of the map that takes H
to Z by (2), then to Y = int_0^sigma Z, then to int_sigma^inf d_xi Y(xi, s) ds; the dilations g -> l g(X/l) act by
H -> l H(xi/l, sigma/l). The domain of this map, its differentiability and any contraction property are not
established. (d) Formal statements. For (1) with coefficients frozen at a point where b != 0, perturbations
proportional to exp(lambda y + i eta xi) require
    b lambda^3 + (i a eta - 1) lambda^2 + i g_xi eta lambda + g_y eta^2 = 0,   a = c xi + h.   (3)
At a positive vertical-axis point (a = g_xi = 0, b = v, g_y = G', with v > 0 and G' > 0, as holds for solutions in the
class of 3.73) the roots, as |eta| -> inf, are (G'/v)^{1/3} |eta|^{2/3} omega + O(1) with omega^3 = -1, and the
largest real part is (1/2) (G'/v)^{1/3} |eta|^{2/3} + O(1); where a != 0 and g_y != 0 the roots are +-(i g_y
eta/a)^{1/2} + O(1) and -i a eta/b + O(1). This suggests, and does not prove, that the evolution of (1) in y can be
controlled in horizontal Gevrey classes of order at most 3/2 near the vertical axis and at most 2 away from it; it
concerns frozen coefficients at interior points, not the bottom, where b = 0. For the frozen linearization of the
evolution in xi at a positive axis point in 3.73(c), the roots instead have real parts of order |eta|^{3/2} at
vertical frequency eta. Counting one free function k by (a) against one functional condition h(xi, y) -> 0, then
adding c and quotienting the dilation, suggests expected local dimension zero: if a suitably differentiable fixed-c
defect map were Fredholm of index zero and the full map were transverse at a zero, a local slice for the dilation
would have an isolated zero in (k, c). Neither hypothesis is established, and this heuristic gives no global
discreteness or selection statement for c. (e) No sign of the cusp coefficient. For 0 < p < 1 put C_0 = 1/(p + 2) and,
on R^2 minus the origin,
    f = C_0 y r^{p - 3} (3 xi^2 + (p + 2) y^2),   V_1[f] = C_0 xi r^{p - 3} (xi^2 + p y^2),   V_2[f] = -C_0 y r^{p - 3} (p xi^2 + y^2).   (4)
The formulas (2) of 3.72 applied to f give exactly these functions on {y >= 0} minus the origin. The trace
Theta(th) = f(cos th, sin th) = C_0 sin th (3 cos^2 th + (p + 2) sin^2 th), a positive multiple of sin
th + ((1 - p)/(3 (p + 3))) sin 3th, is positive on (0, pi) and increasing on (0, pi/2) with Theta(pi/2) = 1; f_y > 0
on R^2 minus the origin, f_xi < 0 where xi > 0 and y > 0, and C_p(Theta) = 0 for the number C_p of 3.74(d). If
chi >= 0 is smooth, not identically zero and supported in (1, 2), then replacing F(s) = f(1, s) by F + eps chi for
s > 0 (and extending by homogeneity of degree p and the parities) gives, for |eps| small, a smooth trace with the same
jets at both axes and the same strict sign properties, and changes C_p by eps (p + 1)(p + 2) int_0^inf s chi(s) ds. So
positivity of the trace, its monotonicity on (0, pi/2) and these signs of f_y and f_xi do not determine the sign of
C_p: C_p = 0, C_p > 0 and C_p < 0 all occur. The function f is not a solution: (c X . grad - 1) f = 0, while V[f] .
grad f = -C_0^2 y r^{2p - 6} (3 xi^4 + 2p (p + 2) xi^2 y^2 + p (p + 2) y^4) < 0 on y > 0; and f is not C^1 at 0.
Scope: none of (a)-(e) establishes existence or nonexistence for (3) of 3.72 or selects c; (a)(ii) concerns the local
system near the bottom and imposes neither the bounds nor the condition at infinity; (b) concerns generic analytic
axis data; (d) is formal.

3.76 The second compatibility condition of the far field when 1 < c < 2 ((a), (b) and the statements about f_{3p-2}
defined by (1) proved; the expansion that leads to (1) formal as in 3.74(d); obtained by the checker; hand-checked in
the main analysis; independently proved by the checker with symbolic and high-precision checks; confirmed in an
external audit, whose local repairs are applied, and the repaired text confirmed by the checker). Let 1/2 < p < 1,
c = 1/p, D = c - 1 and d = d_2 = 2p - 1 (in the notation of 3.74(d)), so 0 < d < 1. For a function u on R^2 minus the
origin that is smooth there, even in xi, odd in y and homogeneous of degree q with 0 < q < 1, put F_u(s) = u(1, s),
q_u(s) = q (q - 1) F_u(s) - 2 (q - 1) s F_u'(s) + s^2 F_u''(s), let Q_u be defined by d_xi^2 u(0, y) = Q_u y^{q - 2}
for y > 0, and let C_q(u) = int_0^inf s (q_u(s) - Q_u s^{q - 2}) ds, which is finite; for q = p and u = f_p this is
the number C_p(Theta) of 3.74(d), and we write C_p(u) for it in general. Let f be such a function of degree p with
K = f(0, 1) > 0 and with V[f], given by (2) of 3.72 on {y >= 0} minus the origin and extended by parity, smooth on R^2
minus the origin (by 3.74(d) this requires C_p(f) = 0). Then f_d = (V[f] . grad f)/D, the term of degree d in (6) of
3.74, is smooth on R^2 minus the origin, even in xi, odd in y and homogeneous of degree d, its velocity V[f_d] is
given by the convergent formulas (2) of 3.72, and the terms of degree 3p - 2 in a termwise expansion
g = f + f_d + f_{3p-2} + (terms of lower degree) of (3) of 3.72, under the assumptions of 3.74(d), give
    -2 D f_{3p-2} + V[f] . grad f_d + V[f_d] . grad f = 0,   (1)
since c (3p - 2) - 1 = -2D. Define f_{3p-2} by (1). For every y > 0, (f_{3p-2}(xi, y) - f_{3p-2}(0, y))/|xi|^d -> p K
C_d(f_d) y^{p - 1}/(2D) as xi -> 0, so f_{3p-2} is C^1 in xi near the vertical axis only if C_d(f_d) = 0: a termwise
expansion of this kind with coefficients C^1 near the vertical axis requires C_p(f) = 0 and C_d(f_d) = 0. (a) For the
density f of 3.75(e) (K = 1),
    C_d(f_d) = -3 p^2 (4p^2 + 5p - 1) J_d/((p + 2)^2 (2p - 1)(2 - p)) < 0,   J_d = int_0^inf (1 + s^2)^{(d - 3)/2} ds,   (2)
so for 1 < c < 2 the termwise expansion that starts from this density has a third term that is not C^1 near the
vertical axis. (b) There are densities f as above with f(0, 1) = 1, trace positive on (0, pi) and increasing on (0,
pi/2), f_y > 0 on R^2 minus the origin and f_xi < 0 where xi > 0 and y > 0, with C_d(f_d) = 0, and others with all
these properties and C_d(f_d) > 0. So, for 1 < c < 2, neither of the first two compatibility conditions C_p(f) = 0,
C_d(f_d) = 0 implies a sign obstruction for positive monotone traces, and both hold together for some of them. Scope:
these are conditions on a termwise homogeneous expansion with smooth angular coefficients; no hydrostatic solution is
constructed, the conditions at higher degrees are not examined, expansions with angular layers (3.78 treats the
leading inner problem of such a layer formally) or other matching are not excluded, the densities are not C^1 at the
origin, and nothing is claimed for c >= 2: then d <= 0, and a nonzero axis curvature of f_d makes its unmatched lower
velocity integral diverge, so matching to a core must in general be included (3.74(d)); 3.77(c) and (d) give necessary
conditions for c > 2 and c = 2 under explicit far-field hypotheses.

3.77 The core constant of the vertical velocity is the same on every vertical line, and necessary far-field conditions
under explicit hypotheses (main analysis; the agreement of the moments in (a) and the statements (c) and (d) also
obtained in an external analysis; independently proved by the checker with symbolic and improper-integral checks;
confirmed in an external audit, whose two optional clarifications are applied, and the clarified text confirmed by the
checker). Let g solve (3) of 3.72 in the class of 3.73, with G, v, K and gamma as there, b = c y + V_2 and Delta(xi,
y) = V_2(xi, y) - V_2(0, y) for y >= 0. (a) There are y_0 >= 1 and C_3, independent of xi, such that for every xi and
every y >= y_0 the improper integral
    I(xi, y) = int_y^inf G(t) Delta(xi, t)/(b(xi, t) v(t)) dt   (1)
converges and |I(xi, y)| <= C_3 xi^2 y^{gamma - 2}. Consequently, for fixed xi, Delta(xi, y) = A y^alpha (1 + o(1)) as
y -> inf with A != 0 and alpha > gamma - 1 - p is impossible; in particular, if Delta(xi, y) has a limit as y -> inf,
this limit is 0. If the hypothesis of 3.74(d) holds on the axis with the constant Q, and int_0^inf t |g_xixi(xi_1,
t) - Q_1 t^{p - 2}| dt < inf for some xi_1 and a constant Q_1, then Q_1 = Q and m(xi_1) = int_0^inf t (g_xixi(xi_1,
t) - Q t^{p - 2}) dt equals m_0: the moment does not depend on the line. (b) Every c > 1. Let f = r^p Theta(th) be
smooth on R^2 minus the origin, even in xi and odd in y, with Theta(pi/2) = K, let chi be a smooth radial function
with chi = 0 for r <= 1/2 and chi = 1 for r >= 1, and put R = g - chi f. If for every |xi| >= 2 the limit v_R(xi) of
V_2[R](xi, y) - V_2[R](0, y) as y -> inf exists, and v_R(xi) = o(|xi|^p) as |xi| -> inf, then C_p(Theta) = 0 (C_p as
in 3.74(d)). (c) c > 2. With f, chi and R as in (b), suppose |d_xi^2 R| <= C' (1 + r)^{-2 - eps} for some eps > 0.
Then the hypothesis of 3.74(d) holds on every vertical line with Q = p K + Theta''(pi/2), C_p(Theta) = 0, m_0 = 0, and
    G(y) = K y^p + A_2 y^{2p - 1} + o(y^{p - 1}),   A_2 = K Q/((1 - p) D),   (2)
so the axis density has no term of degree p - 1. If moreover R = chi f_d + R_2, where f_d is smooth on R^2 minus the
origin, even in xi, odd in y and homogeneous of degree d = 2p - 1 (< 0), and |d_xi^2 R_2| <= C' (1 + r)^{e - 2} with
e < d, then also C_d^-(f_d) = int_0^inf s q_{f_d}(s) ds = 0, where q_u is defined as in 3.76 (with q = d) and the
integral converges because d < 0. (d) c = 2 (p = 1/2, D = 1). Suppose g = chi (f + f_0) + R_2 with f as in (b), f_0
smooth on R^2 minus the origin, even in xi, odd in y and homogeneous of degree 0, and |d_xi^2 R_2| <= C'
(1 + r)^{e - 2} with e < 0. Define B by d_xi^2 f_0(0, y) = B y^{-2} for y > 0 and C_0(f_0) = lim_{S -> inf} (int_0^S s
q_{f_0}(s) ds - B log S), with q_{f_0}(s) = 2 s F_0'(s) + s^2 F_0''(s), F_0(s) = f_0(1, s). Then C_p(Theta) = 0,
B = 0, the moment hypothesis of 3.74(d) holds on the axis with Q = p K + Theta''(pi/2) and m_0 = C_0(f_0), V_2(0,
y) = 4 Q y^{1/2} + C_0(f_0) + o(1) and
    G(y) = K y^{1/2} + 2 K Q + (K C_0(f_0)/4) y^{-1/2} + o(y^{-1/2}).   (3)
(e) Scope. The estimate and the exclusions in (a) hold for every solution in the class; they use neither g_y > 0 nor
any far-field hypothesis. The moment comparison in (a) uses the two stated moment hypotheses. By the bounds of 3.73,
g(xi, y) - G(y) = O(xi^2 y^{gamma - 2}) with gamma - 2 < p - 1, so g(xi, y) = G(y) + M(xi) y^{p - 1} + o(y^{p - 1})
with M(xi) != 0 is impossible in the class; (a) is the corresponding statement for the velocity: a constant part of
V_2 at large height cannot depend on the line. (b)-(d) are conditional: their far-field hypotheses are not proved for
solutions (3.74(b) gives uniform convergence of r^{-p} g without derivatives). They show that the conditions
C_p(Theta) = 0 of 3.74(d), and C_d^-(f_d) = 0, m_0 = 0 for c > 2 and B = 0 for c = 2, are necessary for solutions with
expansions of the stated kinds, not only for termwise formal expansions. Nothing here shows that such solutions exist,
and nonzero values of these numbers for a trial density, which is not a solution, do not exclude solutions; whether
expansions with angular layers of shrinking width occur is not decided (3.78 treats the leading inner problem of such
a layer formally).

3.78 A near-axis layer of the hydrostatic far field: the leading inner problem has exactly one solution for every
value of C_p(Theta) (formal; main analysis, with symbolic and multiprecision checks; the explicit inner inverse, the
value h(0) and the remarks on the next orders in (e) obtained in an external analysis; independently derived by the
checker, with symbolic and multiprecision checks; confirmed in an external audit after local repairs, which are
applied, and the repaired text confirmed by the checker). Let 0 < p < 1, c = 1/p, D = c - 1, and let f_p = r^p
Theta(th) with Theta smooth, K = Theta(pi/2) > 0, Q and C_p(Theta) be as in 3.74(d). Put mu = (p + 1)/2, z = xi/y^mu,
q = mu p + p - 1 = (p^2 + 3p - 2)/2, n = mu p = p (p + 1)/2 and s = p - 1/mu = (p + 2)(p - 1)/(p + 1). Then
p - 1 < q < 2p - 1 < n < p, s < 0, and the cusp p K C_p(Theta) |xi|^p y^{p - 1}/D of f_{2p-1} in 3.74(d) equals (p K
C_p(Theta)/D) y^q |z|^p. (a) Inner equations. Near the positive vertical axis write g = f_p + f_s + y^q h(z) and
V_2 = Q y^p/(p (1 - p)) + y^n w(z) + V_s, with h and w even, where f_s and V_s collect the other terms of the outer
expansion, which are smooth in xi near the axis (f_s contains f_{2p-1} - C_p(Theta) |xi|^p d_y f_p/D, which is smooth
near the axis; the part of C_p(Theta) |xi|^p d_y f_p/D beyond the cusp is of relative order y^{p - 1} at fixed z; and
V_s contains V_2[f_p] - Q y^p/(p (1 - p)) - C_p(Theta) |xi|^p = O(xi^2 y^{p - 2})); w includes the term C_p(Theta)
|z|^p of V_2[f_p]. The terms of order y^q in (3) of 3.72 and of order y^{n - 2} in V_{2,yy} = -g_xixi give
    (mu - c) h + c (1 - mu) z h' + p K w = 0,   h'' + (mu th - n)(mu th - n + 1) w = 0,   th = z d/dz.   (1)
Once the outer equations for f_p and f_s are used, the local interaction terms not kept are smaller by a factor
O(y^{p - 1}) at fixed z. This is not a complete remainder estimate: nonlocal contributions of the canonical inverse
from the outer region (for example a term of order |xi|^{2p - 1} in V_2 coming from f_{2p-1}) enter at the relative
order y^{mu (p - 1)}, and core constants and logarithms may also intervene. For even h, smooth at z = 0, with
h = O(z^p) and h'' = O(z^{p - 2}) as z -> inf, the canonical inverse in the inner variables is
    w = C_p(Theta) |z|^p + (1/mu) [|z|^p int_{|z|}^inf t^{-p-1} h''(t) dt + |z|^s int_0^{|z|} t^{-s-1} h''(t) dt];   (2)
(2) solves the second equation of (1), and every solution of it bounded at z = 0 whose coefficient of z^p at infinity
is C_p(Theta) equals (2). As z -> inf, w = C_p(Theta) z^p + A z^s + O(z^{p - 2}), where A = (1/mu) int_0^inf t^{-s-1}
h''(t) dt is determined by h; y^n A z^s = A y |xi|^s is the contribution of the layer to y int_y^inf g_xixi dt at
points below it on the same vertical line. A component of h growing like z^{p + 2} would be the degree-p term
|xi|^{p + 2} y^{-2}, which is not smooth at the axis, and is excluded because Theta is smooth (for a trace that is
only C^2 at the axis it is not excluded). (b) Solutions. Eliminating w, h solves a third-order equation which, in
t = z^{-2} with h = t^{-p/2} u(t), is the generalized hypergeometric equation for 2F2(a_1, a_2; b_1, b_2; X) with
a_1 = -p/2, a_2 = (1 - p)/2, b_1 = p/(p + 1), b_2 = 2 and X = -lambda/z^2, lambda = 4 p^2 K/((p + 1)^2 (1 - p)) > 0.
As z -> inf its solutions behave like z^p (h_1 = z^p 2F2(a_1, a_2; b_1, b_2; X)), z^s (h_2 = z^s 2F2(a_1 - b_1 + 1,
a_2 - b_1 + 1; 2 - b_1, 3 - b_1; X)) and z^{p + 2} (with a correction z^p log z); as z -> 0+ like an even power series
in z (asymptotic, divergent), an odd one beginning with z, and a recessive solution z^{5 + 2p + s} exp(-lambda/z^2)
(1 + O(z^2)), of which any multiple is allowed locally. The coefficient of z in h_1 is Gamma(b_1) Gamma(b_2)
Gamma(a_1 - a_2) lambda^{-a_2}/(Gamma(a_1) Gamma(b_1 - a_2) Gamma(b_2 - a_2)), which vanishes only when
b_1 - a_2 = (p^2 + 2p - 1)/(2 (p + 1)) = 0, that is p = sqrt(2) - 1 (where s = -1); the analogous coefficient of h_2
is negative for every p in (0, 1). (c) Count. The solutions whose even extension is C^1 at z = 0 form a plane, those
without the z^{p + 2} behaviour form another, and the two planes meet in a line on which the coefficient of z^p does
not vanish. Hence for every value of C_p(Theta) exactly one solution of (1) and (2) is even and smooth at z = 0 and
has no z^{p + 2} component; its recessive part is fixed by these conditions, h = (p K C_p(Theta)/D) z^p + O(z^s) as
z -> inf, and
    h(0) = (p K C_p(Theta)/D) Gamma((1 - p)(p + 2)/(2 (p + 1))) Gamma((1 + p)/2) lambda^{p/2}
           /(sqrt(pi) Gamma(2 + p/2) Gamma(1/(p + 1))),   (3)
so h(0), w(0) = (1 - n) h(0)/(p^2 K) and h''(0) = n (1 - n) w(0) are nonzero when C_p(Theta) != 0, and the solution is
zero when C_p(Theta) = 0. (d) Consistency. In the near-axis region r ~ y the layer is compatible with the bounds of
3.73 (its contribution to g_xixi is O(y^{n - 2}) uniformly in z, and n < p <= gamma; global bounds would require a
completed matching), with the tail condition of V_2 (n < 1) and with 3.77(a) (V_2(xi, y) - V_2(0, y) = O(xi^2 y^{n - 2
mu}) on each vertical line, with n - 2 mu = n - p - 1 < gamma - 1 - p, below the exponents excluded there). When
C_p(Theta) != 0 the moment hypothesis of 3.74(d) fails on every vertical line, because g_xixi(xi, y) - Q y^{p - 2}
contains h''(0) y^{n - 2} with n > 0 (for the displayed leading layer and f_p, the truncated moments int_0^y t
(g_xixi - Q t^{p - 2}) dt of two lines differ by o(1), while each contains (1 - n) w(0) y^n; this says nothing about
the outer and core terms not constructed here), and the axis density contains h(0) y^q between the terms of degrees
2p - 1 and p - 1. The matching allows in the outer region a velocity term (B xi |xi|^s, A y |xi|^s) of degree 1 + s,
with a constant B determined by h, A = -(s + 1) B and 2p - 1 < 1 + s < p (at p = sqrt(2) - 1, A = 0 and the horizontal
term B sgn(xi) remains), and density terms of degree p + s, with 3p - 2 < p + s < 2p - 1; neither degree is among the
d_n of 3.74(d). (e) Scope. (a)-(d) are formal and concern the leading inner problem only. At c = 2 the inner problems
at the relative orders y^{p - 1} (local interactions) and y^{n - 1} (quadratic terms) have, under the analogous
conditions at z = 0 and z = inf, no nonzero homogeneous solution; for some other c (p = sqrt(5) - 2 and
p = (sqrt(17) - 3)/4) the corresponding coefficient vanishes and the consequence is not determined. The nonlocal terms
of relative order y^{mu (p - 1)}, the matching of the outer terms allowed in (d), possible logarithms and the matching
with the core near the origin are not constructed. Thus the leading inner boundary problem has exactly one solution
for each value of C_p(Theta) and imposes no solvability condition requiring C_p(Theta) = 0; the hypotheses of
3.77(b)-(d) exclude the corresponding nonzero layers, of physical width y^{(p + 1)/2} (angular width y^{-(1 - p)/2}).
No complete matched expansion, and no global density satisfying the canonical inverse and the bounds of 3.73, is
constructed; higher inner orders, the nonlocal matching, nonlinear corrections and the matching with the core may
impose further conditions, and whether they, or the solutions, impose C_p(Theta) = 0 is not decided. All constants are
for fixed p and K; no uniformity as p -> 0 or p -> 1 is claimed. Nothing here shows that solutions have such layers,
nor existence, nor nonexistence.

3.79 The near-axis layer of the signed problem: the leading inner problem has no nonzero admissible solution (formal,
except the sign of K, the symmetry in (d) and the statement in (c) on the solutions of (1), which are proved; leading
order only; derived in the main analysis, with symbolic and multiprecision checks; independently derived by the
checker, with multiprecision checks; confirmed in external audits after local repairs, which are applied, and the
repaired text confirmed by the checker). Let 0 < p < 1, c = 1/p, D = c - 1, let f_p = r^p Theta(th) with Theta smooth
and K = Theta(pi/2) > 0, let Q and C_p(Theta) be as in 3.74(d), and let mu, z, q, n, s and lambda be as in 3.78.
Consider the signed problem of 3.72 (the limit a0 -> -inf), (c xi - V_1) g_xi + (c y - V_2) g_y = g, with V_1 and V_2
given by (2) of 3.72 applied to g. The sign of K is the one that occurs: for a C^2 solution of the signed problem,
even in xi and odd in y, with g_y(0) = 1 and the three bounds of 3.72(d), the argument of 3.73(a) applies with
v(y) = c y - V_2(0, y) and gives g(0, y) = K y^p (1 + O(y^{gamma - 1})) with 0 < K < inf. (a) Inner equations. In its
termwise far-field expansion (as in 3.74(d), with the velocity -V) f_{2p-1} = -(V[f_p] . grad f_p)/D, whose cusp near
the vertical axis is -(p K C_p(Theta)/D) |xi|^p y^{p - 1} = -(p K C_p(Theta)/D) y^q |z|^p; so, as in 3.74(d), an
expansion of this kind with coefficients C^1 in xi near the vertical axis requires C_p(Theta) = 0. Write
g = f_p + f_s + y^q h(z) as in 3.78(a), with f_s now the smooth outer terms of the signed problem, and let w be the
inner part of V_2 (so that the inverse (2) of 3.78 holds unchanged). The terms of order y^q in the transport equation
and of order y^{n - 2} in V_{2,yy} = -g_xixi give
    (mu - c) h + c (1 - mu) z h' - p K w = 0,   h'' + (mu th - n)(mu th - n + 1) w = 0,   th = z d/dz,   (1)
with the scope stated in 3.78(a) (the error orders count local interactions only). The coefficient of z^p in h at
infinity is -p K C_p(Theta)/D. Eliminating w gives (th - p)(th - s)(th - p - 2) h = -2 lambda h'', which in t = z^{-2}
with h = t^{-p/2} u is the equation of 2F2(a_1, a_2; b_1, b_2; X) with a_1, a_2, b_1, b_2 as in 3.78(b) but
X = +lambda/z^2. (b) Solutions. As z -> inf the solutions behave like z^p, z^s and z^{p + 2} (with a correction z^p
log z), as in 3.78(b), and those without the z^{p + 2} behaviour are span(h_1, h_2), with h_1 and h_2 as there and
X = lambda/z^2. As z -> 0+ (X -> +inf) every solution is a combination of an even algebraic solution (with an
asymptotic expansion in powers of z^2 beginning with a constant), an odd one (z times such an expansion) and a
dominant solution z^{5 + 2p + s} exp(lambda/z^2) (1 + O(z^2)), unbounded; h_1 contains the dominant solution, since
2F2(a_1, a_2; b_1, b_2; X) ~ Gamma(b_1) Gamma(b_2) e^X X^{a_1 + a_2 - b_1 - b_2}/(Gamma(a_1) Gamma(a_2)) as X -> +inf
with a nonzero constant. The Meijer function u_G(X) = G^{2,2}_{2,3}(X | 1 - a_1, 1 - a_2; 0, 1 - b_1 | 1 - b_2) solves
the same equation, has at X = 0 only the exponents 0 and 1 - b_1, so that h_G = z^p u_G(lambda/z^2) has no z^{p + 2}
component, and is purely algebraic as X -> +inf: u_G = c_E X^{-a_1} (1 + O(1/X)) + c_O X^{-a_2} (1 + O(1/X)), with
c_E = Gamma(a_1) Gamma(1 - b_1 + a_1) Gamma(a_2 - a_1)/Gamma(b_2 - a_1) and
    c_O = Gamma(a_2) Gamma(1 - b_1 + a_2) Gamma(a_1 - a_2)/Gamma(b_2 - a_2)
        = -2 sqrt(pi) Gamma((1 - p)/2) Gamma((3 - p^2)/(2 (p + 1)))/Gamma((3 + p)/2) < 0.   (2)
(c) Count. The solutions bounded near z = 0 form a plane, and span(h_1, h_2) is another plane, different from the
first because h_1 is unbounded at z = 0; they meet in the line spanned by h_G. Since c_O != 0 for every p in (0, 1),
h_G'(0+) = c_O lambda^{-a_2} != 0, so the even extension of h_G is not C^1 at z = 0. Hence the only solution of (1),
with w given by (2) of 3.78, that is bounded near z = 0, has an even extension of class C^1 at z = 0 and has no
z^{p + 2} component is h = 0; for C_p(Theta) != 0 the leading inner problem has no solution, because the required
coefficient -p K C_p(Theta)/D of z^p is then nonzero. On z > 0, solutions with all the other properties exist for
every C_p(Theta) if a corner h'(0+) != 0 at the axis is admitted (multiples of h_G, since u_G(0) != 0); in outer
variables it is a term y^{q - mu} |xi|, not C^1 in xi. This concerns the equations on the half-line z > 0: the even
extension of a solution with h'(0+) != 0 does not satisfy (1) across z = 0 in the sense of distributions, since its
h'' contains delta(z) with the factor 2 h'(0+), while (mu th - n)(mu th - n + 1) w, with w given by the first equation
of (1), contains no multiple of delta(z). (d) Comparison and scope. In 3.78 the third solution at z = 0 is recessive,
exp(-lambda/z^2), and flat there, which leaves exactly one solution for every value of C_p(Theta); for the signed
problem it is exponentially large, and a near-axis layer of width y^{(p + 1)/2}, even and C^1 at the axis, cannot
carry a nonzero cusp coefficient at leading order. Only the product of K with the sign of the velocity enters (1): for
a trace with K < 0, which does not occur for the solutions described above, the count of 3.78 would apply (with
|lambda|). Since V is linear in g, g solves the transport equation of the signed problem if and only if -g solves that
of (3) of 3.72, so the signed problem is (3) of 3.72 with the normalization g_y(0) = -1 in place of g_y(0) = 1. In a
termwise expansion of the signed problem as in 3.74(d), with f_p as above and 1/2 < p < 1, the term of degree 2p - 1
is -f_d with f_d = (V[f_p] . grad f_p)/D, as in (a), and, when C_p(Theta) = 0, the term of degree 3p - 2 is the
function f_{3p-2} defined by (1) of 3.76; so the first two compatibility conditions are again C_p(Theta) = 0 and
C_d(f_d) = 0 of 3.76, and some of the positive monotone traces of 3.76(b) satisfy both. The symmetry, the sign of K
and the statement in (c) on the solutions of (1) are exact; the derivation of (1) as the leading inner problem is
formal, and the count concerns the leading inner problem of this layer only: other layer widths, nonlinear inner
balances, the nonlocal outer terms, logarithms and the matching with the core are not considered. It does not show
that solutions of the signed problem have expansions of the form of 3.74(d), constructs no solution and proves no
nonexistence, and it concerns the hydrostatic limit of 3.72, not profiles at finite slope.

3.80 Finite polynomial axis data do not solve the axis equation of the hydrostatic problem, except possibly at
half-integer exponents P >= 27/2 (proved by the checker, (b) from derivations in the main analysis, the checker and
external answers, with exact supporting checks; hand-checked in the main analysis; audited externally). Let C > 0 and
P > 1 be real, and let H and k be real polynomials with H nonzero and H(0) = 0. For 0 < t < 1 put w = 1 - t^2 and
y = C t w^{-P}; since dy/dt = C Q w^{-P - 1} with Q = 1 + (2P - 1) t^2, the map t -> y is an increasing bijection of
(0, 1) onto (0, inf), and t and w are regarded as functions of y. Let G(y) = y H(w), and let V be a function with
V'(y) = k(w) (for instance V(y) = int_0^y k(w(s)) ds). Write H(w) = w^n h(w) with an integer n >= 1 and h(0) != 0, and
F(t) = C t h(1 - t^2), an odd polynomial of odd degree d. Suppose that for some real c the identity (c y + V) G' = G
holds on a nonempty open interval of y > 0. Then (a) P = n + d/2 and d >= 5; (b) d >= 25, so that P >= 27/2, F has at
least seven distinct complex roots, alpha^2 is real for at most two of the pairs +-alpha of nonzero roots of F, and
the nonzero roots of F do not all have the same multiplicity (in particular F has a repeated root); moreover, if all
nonzero roots of F except one pair +-alpha have the same multiplicity mu, then 0 is a simple root of F and the
multiplicity nu of alpha satisfies nu < mu - n. Consequently the identity holds on no nonempty open interval of y > 0
for any real c when 1 < P < 27/2, when P is not a half-integer, when all nonzero roots of F have the same multiplicity
(in particular when F has no repeated root), when F has at most five distinct complex roots, or when all roots of F
are real; the remaining cases are not decided here. This strengthens the form of the result in earlier versions of
this report (n = 1, that is H'(0) != 0, and 1 < P <= 2), which is contained in (a). The hypotheses H != 0 and H(0) = 0
cannot be dropped: H = 0 gives G = 0, and for a nonzero constant H the choices V = (1 - c) y and k = 1 - c satisfy the
identity for every P. Application to 4.10. On the vertical axis V_1 = 0 by evenness, so the hydrostatic equation (3)
