of 3.72 reads (c y + V_2(0, y)) G' = G there, with G(y) = g(0, y), and (2) of 3.72 gives d/dy V_2(0, y) = int_y^inf
g_xixi(0, s) ds (an integral of the horizontal curvature on the axis, not g_xixi itself). For the saved trial
densities of 4.10 the radial map r = L ((1 + t')/2)^{1/2}/(1 - t')^P of 4.7 and 4.10 (t' the compactified radial
variable there, L > 0) is, on the axis, the map of this result with w = (1 - t')/2, t = (1 - w)^{1/2} and C = 2^{-P}
L. For ten of them, the checker's exact reconstruction of the axis data from the saved coefficient vectors gives g(0,
y) = y H(w) and d/dy V_2(0, y) = k(w) with polynomials H and k of degree N + 1 (N the radial degree), where V_2 is the
velocity (2) of 3.72 of the trial density, obtained through an exact polynomial primitive of the axis integral and not
through the quadrature of 4.10; the checker verified in exact rational arithmetic that H(0) = k(0) = 0, H'(0) != 0 and
C > 0 for the stored map exponent P (P = 2 at c = 2, and at c = 3 the stored binary value 6755399441055743/2^52,
slightly below 3/2): the three states at c = 3 with the logarithmic-panel rule of 4.10 (64 x 16, 96 x 24, 128 x 32),
two states at c = 3 with the same rule and rows at 3M angles (64 x 16, 96 x 24), and five states at c = 2 with the
same rule (96 x 24; 128 x 32 at the iteration cap and continued past it; 160 x 40; 192 x 48), the two with rows at 3M
angles not otherwise reported here. As P < 27/2 for all ten, none of them satisfies the axis equation on a nonempty
open interval of y > 0. Scope. This concerns exact solutions within the stated class of polynomial axis data: it gives
no lower bound on the residual uniform in the degrees, does not exclude limits of such densities as the degrees tend
to infinity, densities of other forms or profiles at finite slope, and is not a nonexistence result for the
hydrostatic problem.

## 4. Numerical computations

No candidate meeting the standard of the primary class. This section records what was computed, including attempted
and withdrawn candidates, with residual tables. Apart from exact evaluations of saved states and the analytical
example in 4.7(c), which are stated as such, this section reports sampled evidence, not uniform residual bounds or
existence proofs; results of Section 3 are applied to computed states where they are cited. Unless an item is marked
"independently re-evaluated", it is a report of the main numerical computation that has not yet been repeated by the
checker.

4.1 Method. The main computation represents rho = y w(r) kappa(r, th), w(r) = (1 + r^2/L_g^2)^{(gamma - 1)/2} with
gamma = 1/c_l and a grid length L_g, kappa even in x and y and bounded on the compactified plane, kappa(0, .) = a0.
Radial coordinate t in [-1, 1) with r = L_g (1 + t)/(1 - t)^{1/(1 - gamma)} (Chebyshev-Radau nodes, linear in r at the
origin, so a discrete state is in general not smooth at 0); angular quadrant grid with exact parity transforms; the
canonical inverse is computed mode by mode from 3.1(iv); unknowns kappa and c_l (or mu in forced problems); rows: the
equation at the nodes, continuity at r = 0, the origin relation c_l + c = 1 (or its forced form), and one gauge row;
Newton with exact Jacobian. Off-grid evaluation of R, N_f, N_v uses the spectral representation. A second,
independent implementation (a basis that is C^inf at every finite point by its Cartesian form, a direct real-space
inverse, an eighth-order finite-difference evaluator) is used for re-evaluation. Resolutions are written N x M (labels
such as N16 M12 mean N x M = 16 x 12): radial polynomial degree N (N + 1 Chebyshev-Radau nodes in the collocation
solvers; in the smooth basis of 4.7(a) the radial factor of the angular mode k has degree N - k) and M angular modes
cos(2k th), k = 0, ..., M - 1. Numerical cubic defects are T1 := (a0 - 2A) b - 6e and T2 := (a0 - 4A) b - 3 a0
(q1 - q2) in the notation of 3.3 (so (T1), (T2) of 3.3 read T1 = T2 = 0), in the length unit of the state unless the
dilation-invariant forms T1 L^2/a0^2, T2 L^2/a0^2 (L a length scale of the state) are stated; the table of 4.7(c)
lists the normalized columns defined there.

4.2 Non-smooth discrete solutions of the unforced problem (attempted; not candidates). Discretizations of the full
problem of the type of 4.1 admit, at every tested c_l, numerical roots of the discrete system (Newton residual at
roundoff; these are not certified as exact discrete solutions) that are not smooth at the origin: the saved early
interpolants are not C^2, conditional on the recorded interval evaluation of their nodal data (3.8); later states of
the same type show
algebraic Chebyshev tails, and at c_l = 1.5 the truncated (T2) integral int_{r > eps} s^{-3} f_2 grows like eps^{-0.8}
over the sampled eps. If that growth is established asymptotically for a fixed encoded interpolant, it excludes C^3 of
that interpolant; it does not by itself exclude a C^3 limit of the changing sequence of states, which would need a
uniformity (order-of-limits) argument. Independently re-evaluated residuals of six such states (independent Cartesian
full-plane inverse at three resolutions and exterior splits, eighth-order differences at three step sizes, 62 off-grid
points with radii 1e-6 to 2e5; maxima over the 59 points off the x-axis; centre defect = c_l + c - 1):

The maximizer of |R|/N_v coincides with that of |R|/N_f except at (3.0, 192 x 48), where it is (13, 1.5708). These
are maxima over 59 sample points, not suprema.
(The large absolute residuals at c_l = 1.5 occur at large radius, where N_f is large.) At c_l = 3 the residual does not
improve monotonically and a0 moves by 18 percent between the first two resolutions. In a manufactured problem with a
planted smooth solution (4.4) the same kind of non-smooth discrete solutions coexists with the planted one, so their
existence is evidence neither for nor against a smooth profile. Their identification with exact finite-regularity
solutions is open (4.5).
Smoothness imposed by constraint rows (attempted; inconclusive; not independently re-evaluated). Rows forcing the
Taylor coefficients at r = 0 of the angular mode k of kappa to vanish for orders j < 2k and for odd j <= J (k <= 3)
were added to the unforced system with c_l free (partial Taylor compatibility conditions at the origin on the angular
modes k <= 3, not a smoothness condition on the whole expansion), and the overdetermined system was solved by
Gauss-Newton with unit-norm constraint rows, from a non-smooth state at c_l = 1.5 and from a forced state at c_l = 2:

    start     N x M    J   |F|_2     max PDE row   max constraint row   c_l          a0      between-node |R|/N_f
    c_l 1.5   48 x 24  3   1.05e-4   7.6e-6        3.5e-6               1.49989756   3.4914  <= 1.5e-6
    c_l 1.5   64 x 32  3   3.36e-4   4.1e-5        1.7e-6               1.49989764   3.4926  <= 4.6e-6
    c_l 1.5   96 x 32  3   3.98e-4   4.2e-5        1.2e-6               1.49989752   3.4912  <= 2.2e-6
    c_l 2     48 x 24  3   2.05e-3   2.0e-4        5.9e-7               2.00458      9.378   <= 1.4e-5
    c_l 2     64 x 32  3   9.63e-4   7.3e-5        9.4e-8               2.01332      9.097   <= 3.7e-6
    c_l 2     96 x 32  3   1.18e-4   6.2e-6        5.7e-8               1.99933      8.324   <= 1.1e-5

(J = 5 gives the same picture.) Here |F|_2 is the Euclidean norm of the stacked residual vector (the rows of 4.1, with
the equation divided by y w(r), and the constraint rows normalized to unit Euclidean norm and then given weight 1),
and the two maxima are the largest absolute entries of these two parts. Every run stopped at the iteration cap with
very short steps. The between-node maxima of |R|/N_f do not decrease monotonically under refinement at either start;
|F|_2 and the maximum PDE row decrease at the c_l = 2 start and increase at the c_l = 1.5 start. At the c_l = 1.5
start c_l stays at 1.49990 to six digits; at the c_l = 2 start c_l lies in [1.99933, 2.01332] (a spread of about 0.7
percent) while a0 decreases from 9.378 to 8.324 (about 11 percent). This is a Gauss-Newton stall with an arbitrary row
weighting, not a certified least-squares minimum, so it is evidence neither for nor against a smooth profile near
these states.

4.3 Forced formulation. W . grad rho - rho = mu y phi(|X|/eps), phi(t) = (1 + t^2)^{-2}, c_l a prescribed parameter
(scanned, never normalized), mu unknown, gauge: far-field angular mean of kappa equal to beta (this gauge reaches only
profiles with nonzero far-field angular mean of kappa; for states of one fixed growth exponent gamma, a gauge valid for
all of them is Q_s = int rho^2 |X|^{-s} dX for one fixed s with 2 + 2 gamma < s < 4, which scales as l^{4 - s}; it was
not used).
(a) Sheet 1 (the branch continued from small amplitude). mu agrees to 8-9 digits between 48 x 16 and 96 x 48 at the
tested points. mu > 0 at all 40 converged sheet-1 entries of a table with c_l in [1.1, 8], beta in [0.25, 16] (a 41st
converged entry of that table, (c_l, beta) = (1.35, 16), mu = -0.848, Delta = -0.239, lies on a different, nearly
singular sheet), and at 277 (beta = 1) and 274 (beta = 4) converged points of scans in c_l with step 0.025 on
[1.05, 8], where mu is increasing in c_l. The small-amplitude law derived from 3.19(iii) for the weight
w = (1 + r^2/L_g^2)^{(gamma - 1)/2} with gamma = p = 1/c_l is beta = (mu/c_l) (eps/L_g)^{1 - p} J(p) + O(beta^2),
J(q) = Gamma((1 - q)/2) Gamma((3 + q)/2)/2; at eps = L_g it reads mu = (c_l / J(1/c_l)) beta + O(beta^2). The
remainder O(beta^2) is formal (the nonlinear small-amplitude branch is not proved to exist). The law is consistent
with the data. These are finitely many floating-point samples without enclosures of mu; they show that no sampled
state passes the unforced test (an exact solution of the forced equation with mu != 0 does not solve the unforced
equation, 3.19).
(b) Sheet-1 state (c_l, beta, eps) = (3, 1, 1), with an independent reproduction of its parameters: the main
computation (96 x 48) gives
mu = 1.9806606230, a0 = 1.1384875215, c = -0.2602702396; the independent C^inf-basis solver (16 x 12, own inverse) gives
mu = 1.98066062305477, a0 = 1.13848752152384, c = -0.260270239585424. Forced residual of the primary state, evaluated
by the main computation's evaluator (the checker's evaluations concern the parameters above, the coarser independent
state below and the state (1.5, 4, 1)), on between-node points (midpoints in t and th plus four angles near the axes):

    region r        points  max|R_f|   max|R_f|/N_f  max|R_f|/N_v  min N_f   max|mu y phi|
    [0, 1e-2)        357    9.9e-17    4.0e-15       6.7e-15       1.6e-6    1.6e-2
    [1e-2, 1e-1)     714    1.3e-15    8.9e-15       1.5e-14       1.9e-4    1.8e-1
    [1e-1, 1)       1377    1.8e-14    1.2e-14       2.7e-14       1.8e-3    6.4e-1
    [1, 10)         1224    5.0e-14    1.6e-14       3.0e-14       1.8e-2    4.9e-1

    [1e4, 1e8)       102    3.7e-14    4.9e-16       1.3e-15       6.9e-1    3.1e-13

The independent evaluation of the coarser independent state (12 x 8, mu = 1.9806606369) at 56 points gives
max |R_f| = 1.4e-8, max |R_f|/N_f = 1.6e-8, max |R_f|/N_v = 5.8e-8. As an unforced candidate this state fails by
construction: max |R| differs from max |mu y phi| by at most max |R_f| on the same samples, so it is O(1) (the
independent evaluation gives max |R|/N_f = 0.47). The checker's independent evaluation of the saved sheet-1 state
(c_l, beta, eps) = (1.5, 4, 1) at 96 x 48 (own real-space inverse, three quadrature levels) gives at the finest level
max |R_f| = 6.1e-9, max |R_f|/N_f = 3.9e-9 and max |R_f|/N_v = 3.6e-9, limited by its quadrature and by floating-point
cancellation, and, as an unforced
candidate, max |R|/N_f = 0.075.
(c) Negative amplitude (a0 < 0). Sheet 1 continued from small |beta| to beta < 0 (c_l = 1.5, 2, 3; 48 x 24 and 64 x 32)
and scans at beta = -1 (c_l = 2 .. 8) and beta = -4 (c_l = 4 .. 8) converge with Delta between +0.59 and +23 (mu < 0) and
positive strain c at every converged entry; the sheet stops converging (Jacobian singular values to 6e-8) near
beta = -0.6 at c_l = 1.5 and jumps to unrelated states beyond beta = -1 at c_l = 2. Refinement invariance was checked at
(c_l, beta) = (3, -1), (5, -4), (8, -1) (mu = -3.39280410, -45.297165, -9.5390501, to 9 digits from 48 x 24 to 96 x 48).
No zero of mu was found. For an exact profile with a0 < 0 the strain identity requires
int rho_3 r^{-2} dr = 1 - c_l + a0/4 < 0.
Consistency with 3.19(iii): the linearized forced problem gives a0 = mu/(c_l - 1), so Delta -> c_l - 1 on both sides
of beta = 0 is expected if the computed branch has this small-amplitude limit (the nonlinear small-amplitude branch is
not proved to exist); the data approach this value (Delta = 0.593, 1.08, 2.08 at beta = -0.25 for c_l = 1.5, 2, 3).
Along sheet 1, Delta decreases from c_l - 1 as a0 increases (beta > 0) and increases as a0 decreases (beta < 0).
Sample points (a0, Delta) on sheet 1 at c_l = 2: (-1.984, 1.69), (-0.696, 1.19), (-0.320, 1.08), (0, 1), (0.285,
0.932), (1.011, 0.782), (3.071, 0.476), (4.869, 0.293), (6.858, 0.140), (8.220, 0.0517); at c_l = 3: (-3.754, 3.29),
(-1.415, 2.40), (0, 2), (1.138, 1.740), (3.886, 1.264), (8.189, 0.776), (15.61, 0.294), (21.83, 0.047). The entries
(0, 1) and (0, 2) are zero-amplitude limits (Delta = mu/a0 is undefined at a0 = 0). Delta > 0 at every converged
point, on both sides of a0 = 0.
(d) Other forced solutions. Multistarts (up to 540 initial guesses per parameter point: anisotropic cores, second
scales, angular modes of both signs) find many further converged forced solutions at each (c_l, beta), mostly with
mu < 0 and larger a0, often near a0 = 4A. None of them passes the refinement test: under 48 x 16 -> 96 x 48 they drift,
stop converging, or have singular values of the Jacobian decreasing to 1e-13 .. 1e-15.

4.4 Methodology validation (planted solution). Planted smooth solution rho_m = 3 y (1 + r^2)^{(p_m - 1)/2}
(1 - x^2/(2 (1 + r^2))), p_m = 1/c_lm, with the source S_m = (c_lm X + U_m) . grad rho_m - rho_m added, and
c_lm = 1 - psi_m,xy(0) = 2.394008418478. Newton with c_l free, started from a 5 percent perturbation, returns
(rho_m, c_lm) with |c_l - c_lm| = 1.3e-11 (a single recovery; this does not prove that c_l is determined). The forced
problem at c_lm returns mu = 0 and a0 = 3 at four resolutions, while a second zero of mu on the same well-conditioned
branch (a non-smooth discrete solution), located anew at each resolution, moves monotonically in a0 under refinement. Residual of the planted
state, R_m = (c_lm X + U).grad rho - rho - S_m, max |R_m|/N_f by the regions of 4.3(b): 2.7e-12, 9.0e-12, 1.0e-11,
5.3e-12, 1.6e-12, 6.5e-12, 7.8e-12 at 48 x 16 and 1.3e-13, 2.3e-13, 2.4e-13, 1.2e-13, 5.0e-14, 4.9e-14, 1.0e-13 at
96 x 48 (max |S_m| up to 2.1). Adopted criterion: a zero of mu is evidence of a smooth profile only if mu, a0 and the
location of the zero are invariant under refinement and the zero passes the scaling test of Section 5 (iii). The
smallest singular value of the Jacobian in coefficient norms is 1.6e-5 even for the planted smooth solution, so small
values of it are not by themselves evidence against smoothness.

4.5 Finite-regularity variant: the concentrated-forcing limit (separately labelled; not evidence for P_inf).
By 3.19, rescaling maps the forced solutions at large beta with eps = 1 one to one onto the forced solutions at the
gauge value 1 with forcing width eps = beta^{-1/sigma_sc} -> 0 (onto those at a gauge value beta_0 with
eps = (beta/beta_0)^{-1/sigma_sc}), where sigma_sc = 1 - p is the scaling exponent of the gauge of 3.19 (not the
strain supremum sigma) (a correspondence of solution sets, not a uniqueness statement); the sheet-1 states at large
beta correspond in this way to states with small width. Continuation in eps at the fixed gauge value beta = 4 of 4.3
(grid length L_g = 1; N x M = 96 x 32; selected rows; b_cub is the coefficient b of x^2 y in rho, from the r^2
coefficients of cubic least-squares fits in r^2 of rho_1/r and rho_3/r (the sin th and sin 3th modes of rho) at 30
log-spaced radii with 10^{-3.5} <= r/min(1, eps) <= 10^{-1.5}; a re-extraction of the 63 saved converged states with
this window reproduces the logged values of b_cub and b_cub L_K^2 within 5e-6 relative and agrees with the table to
its displayed precision, and b_cub L_K^2 is the scale-free cubic coefficient):

    c_l = 2 (4A = 12):

residual 2e-7 vs 7e-6); the quartic datum H_4 is not resolution-stable and is not reported. Residual table of the
eps = 0.0156 state at c_l = 2 (96 x 32), forced equation:

    region r        points  max|R_f|   max|R_f|/N_f  max|R_f|/N_v  min N_f   max|R|

The last column is the unforced residual R = R_f + mu y phi(|X|/eps) of this state. The forcing itself satisfies
|mu y phi| <= mu eps^4 r^{-3} <= 2.52e-8 r^{-3} for r >= 1 (mu = 0.4253, eps = 0.0156; confirmed by the checker), so for r >= 1 that column
coincides with max |R_f| to the digits shown. (In the table of 4.3(b) the last column is the forcing max |mu y phi|;
on the same samples |max |R| - max |mu y phi|| <= max |R_f|, at most 6.6e-14 there.)

Reading (heuristic). At c_l = 1.5 and 2, Delta decreases nearly linearly in a0 and extrapolates to 0 at a0 about 3.9
and 9.0 (below 4A); the scale-free cubic coefficient grows in magnitude over the computed range of eps, and successive rescaled outer profiles on
1/4 < |X| < 4 differ by amounts decreasing roughly like eps^0.4. This is consistent with convergence, away from the
origin, to an exact solution that is not C^3 at the origin, with a0 near that of the non-smooth discrete solutions of
4.2 at the same c_l (3.44 at c_l = 1.5). At c_l = 3 the branch crosses the forced degree-3 resonance
a0 - 4A + 2 Delta = 0 near eps = 0.03 and enters the region of the withdrawn branch of 4.6. Fitted local exponents of
Delta(eps) drift with eps (0.35, 0.53, 0.72 at c_l = 2), so no singular exponent is identified at c_l = 2. At c_l = 1.5 a
continuation to smaller widths with a grid scale resolving the forcing core (a0 and Delta are invariant under scaling, so
rescaled states lie on the same curve in the (a0, Delta) plane, and a change of grid scale changes only the
discretization) gives Delta = 0.021807, 0.016201, 0.011657 at eps = 0.0039, 0.002, 0.001 (grid length L_g = 0.1 with
gauge value beta = 8.6177 in the grid units, which keeps the physical far-field amplitude of the table, since beta
L_g^{1 - gamma} = 4.0000 to the displayed precision, with gamma = 2/3; eps is the physical forcing width; the
continuation starts from the state of the table at eps = 0.0156 and reproduces its a0 and Delta to the printed
digits), local exponents log(Delta_i/Delta_{i+1})/log(eps_i/eps_{i+1}) = 0.445 and 0.475, with a0 rising to about 3.8
(extrapolated limit near 3.9); the exponent is in the range 0.43-0.52 of the algebraic Chebyshev tails of the
non-smooth discrete solutions of 4.2 at the same c_l. A single-inner-scale matching argument (heuristic; it assumes
that the outer limit has a leading term C r^{1+s} Theta(th) and that the inner expansions converge) predicts that
Delta, a0 - lim a0 and mu scale like eps^s and the cubic coefficient like eps^{s-2}, so that eps^2 b/Delta and
(a0 - lim a0)/Delta have finite limits. At c_l = 1.5 the data are consistent with this for s about 0.4: d a0/d Delta
settles near -12.5 and eps^2 b/Delta moves from -1.48 to -3.19 with increments per halving of eps falling from 0.25 to
0.14. At c_l = 2, d a0/d Delta settles near -15.6 but eps^2 b/Delta (from -1.48 to -6.57) is still growing, so these
data are not yet in that regime. An unforced solve with an explicit term C r^{d-1} in kappa (d and C unknown) did not
converge (residual 1e-3, Jacobian singular values 1e-11 to 1e-13, c_l drifting when free). Status of the
finite-regularity variant: UNRESOLVED; no exact P_{1,alpha} profile has been constructed or certified, and the data
above do not bear on P_inf.

4.6 Withdrawn branch. A second forced branch had a sign change of mu near c_l ~ 3.0-3.1 at beta = 4, eps = 1. Root
location by secant in c_l:

    N x M     c_l*       a0        a0/4A   K        between-node |R|/N_f (max)
    48 x 12   2.972064   19.5494   0.988   2.9517   7.6e-4
    48 x 24   3.075975   21.9196   1.064   2.9275   3.2e-5
    48 x 32   3.066482   18.9471   0.923   2.9908   2.6e-6

Its Jacobian is nearly singular at every resolution above the coarsest, a0 at the sign change moves by about 15 percent
between angular resolutions, regridding to finer grids jumps to other sheets, and the rescaled root state does not
re-converge (failed scaling test of Section 5 (iii)). Residual of the 48 x 24 root state (mu = -2.1e-6, so R and R_f
coincide to 2e-6 |y phi|): max |R|/N_f by the regions of 4.3(b) = 4.9e-7, 5.0e-6, 2.9e-5, 3.2e-5, 2.0e-5, 4.6e-6, 2.4e-7
(max |R| up to 2.7e-4). On this branch at fixed c_l = 2.8 and 3.3, refinement from 48 x 24 to 128 x 64 leaves the
between-node maxima of the forced residual |R_f|/N_f near 8e-6 and 2.5e-5 while mu and a0 fluctuate (the maxima of the
table above decrease with M at N = 48). These are forced, not unforced, residuals (mu = -0.83 at c_l = 2.8 and 1.08 at
c_l = 3.3 in the 128 x 64 solves), and only the first solve of each chain, at 48 x 24, converges at the nodes (to
below 1e-12): the solves with N = 64, 96 and 128 stop at the cap of 120 iterations with node residuals about 1e-4.
Independently re-evaluated: by the criterion of 3.8 (a nonzero first radial derivative at r = 0 of the angular mean of
kappa excludes C^2 at the origin), a 256-bit ball-arithmetic evaluation by the checker of the exact interpolants of
the 48 x 12, 48 x 24 and 48 x 32 root states encloses this derivative in intervals of radius below 1e-69 whose
midpoints round to 0.014753, 0.0094964 and 0.0097183 (the four states of 3.8 are other states), so these interpolants
are not C^2 if that evaluation is accepted, although their sampled between-node residuals are small (max
|R|/N_f = 2.6e-6 for the 48 x 32 state in the table and 2.5e-6 on the 59 off-axis sample points of the checker). The
withdrawal is confirmed. The concentrated-forcing continuation of 4.5 at c_l = 3 reaches the same region of (c_l, a0).
A third root of mu, met while regridding (c_l = 3.805, a0 = 28.79 at 64 x 32, a0/4A = 1.09), was refined at fixed c_l and
beta = 4: mu = 4e-6, 0.173, 0.195 at 64 x 32, 96 x 48, 128 x 64 (the last two Newton solves not converged, |F| ~ 1e-4),
a0 = 28.79, 28.59, 28.41, smallest singular value 1e-11 to 2e-14. It drifts and degenerates like the second branch and is
withdrawn (attempted; not independently re-evaluated). Every root of mu found off sheet 1 so far lies within 10 percent
of the degree-3 resonance a0 = 4A and has failed refinement.

4.7 Unforced solves in smooth-by-construction representations (attempted; no candidate). These representations contain
only functions that are C^inf at the origin, so the non-smooth discrete solutions of 4.2 cannot occur.
(a) Basis with radial map analytic in r^2 at 0 and angular mode k of kappa carrying the factor sigma^k, sigma =
(1 + t)/2 with t the compactified radial variable (every basis function is C^inf in Cartesian coordinates), each mode
collocated on its own nodes, far-field gauge on the y-axis, c_l an unknown. Calibration: the forced problem reproduces
the sheet-1 state (c_l, beta) = (3, 1) of 4.3 to 10 digits (mu = 1.9806606230, a0 = 1.1384875215) at 48 x 12 and
64 x 16. Unforced, c_l free, 24 starts (constant starts and releases of c_l from converged forced states, 48 x 12 to
128 x 8): every run either collapsed to a spurious state with a0 = 0 (which satisfies the centre row of that system
trivially; between-node |R|/N_f = 1) or stalled (|F| 1e-3 to 1e-1; the best stalled state, at c_l = 1.99969,
a0 = 11.43, has centre defect -2e-12 but PDE residual 1e-3 and between-node |R|/N_f 3e-4 to 7e-3). A least-squares
variant (every mode collocated at every node, centre row replaced by (c_l - 1 + c) K_g = 0 with K_g the gauge value,
which removes the automatic vanishing of the old centre row at a0 = 0 but does not by itself impose
a0 != 0: the finite basis contains smooth non-profiles with a0 = 0 satisfying both replacement rows; the stalls below
have a0 != 0) solves forced problems robustly (mu and a0 agree to 10 digits between 64 x 16 and
96 x 24 for forcing widths 1 to 1/8 at c_l = 1.5 and 3); its unforced releases (Gauss-Newton with SVD steps and
backtracking, from forced states of widths 1/4 and 1/8; the two widths give nearby but unequal stalls, with relative
differences up to 2.6e-4 in c_l and 1.7e-3 in a0 over the six pairs, for example c_l = 3.19033 and 3.19068 at 128 x 32
from c_l = 3; the table lists the releases from width 1/4) stall:

    start c_l   size     c_l at stall   a0       |F|max    between-node |R|/N_f   Chebyshev tail (mode 0 / 1)

    3           96x24    3.36370        15.100   5.3e-2    3e-2 .. 5e-2           6e-4 / 1.5e-2
    3           128x32   3.19033        16.371   3.1e-2    2.3e-2 .. 3.0e-2       3.1e-4 / 2.4e-3
    1.5         64x16    1.56283        5.322    1.2e-4    8e-3 .. 1.5e-2         1.5e-3 / 5e-2

Restriction of these releases (checker's representation identity, confirmed on the saved metadata): the radial map
was built once at the starting c_l and kept fixed while c_l was released in the transport rows. The finite basis
consists of rho = r sin(th) ((1 - t)/2) sum_j sigma^j B_j(t) cos(2 j th), sigma = (1 + t)/2, with polynomials B_j, on
the map r = L sqrt((1 + t)/2)/(1 - t)^k with k = 1/(1 - 1/c_l(start)); the gauge value is K_g = sum_j (-1)^j B_j(1).
As t -> 1, 1 - t = (L/r)^{1/k} + O(r^{-2/k}), so every function of this basis is rho = r^{g0} Theta0 + O(r^{2 g0 - 1})
with Theta0 = (L^{1/k}/2) sin(th) sum_j B_j(1) cos(2 j th), axis amplitude Theta0(pi/2) = L^{1/k} K_g/2, and the
fixed exponent g0 = 1 - 1/k = 1/c_l(start), whatever the released value of c_l. With a nonzero gauge value an exact
solution of this finite form therefore requires c_l g0 = 1, that is c_l = c_l(start), and for any other c_l the
residual has a nonzero floor on the positive y-axis, |R|/N_f -> |c_l g0 - 1|/(c_l g0 + 1). For the five rows above the
floor is 0.1059, 0.0572, 0.0307, 0.0205 and 0.0147 (confirmed by the checker on the saved states with 80-digit
arithmetic and an eighth-order difference stencil; three stencil steps agree to 1e-16), of the same order as the between-node residuals in the table (each
limit exceeds the corresponding sampled maximum, so the samples do not reach the asymptotic floor). The drift of
c_l away from its starting value thus builds in a residual floor, and these releases do not test smooth existence with
an unrestricted far-field exponent. They neither show that a rebuilt map would converge nor bear on existence.
Rebuilt-map releases (solver trajectories of the main computation; apart from the four iterates checked below they
are not independently re-evaluated; not a claim). With the map rebuilt from c_l at every step the releases of this
paragraph do not stall (rebuilt-map runs that stall are reported in 4.7(d)). From c_l = 1.5 at 64 x 16 the iterates
drift down toward c_l = 1 while the interior residual keeps decreasing (after 150 steps c_l = 1.0623, a0 = 0.953,
between-node |R|/N_f about 1e-6 for r < 100 but 4e-3 for r > 100); other starts reach the solver bound c_l = 1.02 with
different slopes (a0 = 0.242 at 64 x 16; a0 between 0.04 and 0.2 for four releases at 96 x 24), and a start at c_l = 3
drifts the same way. With the bound lowered to 1.005 a 64 x 16 release reached c_l = 1.0078 after 300 steps, still
moving, with a0 near 0.19, so that a0/D grows roughly like 1/D (12.5, 13.1, 17.7, 24.9 at steps 128, 192, 256, 300),
and between-node |R|/N_f about 1.45e-5 spread over all radii sampled up to 1e115; at that c_l the map exponent is
about 130, so the representation itself degenerates. A larger outer length or a finer radial grid changes the path (a
faster drift to the bound), not the outcome, and a partial survey of starts (9 of 42 done) found no start settling at
c_l > 1.05. Tentative reading, not established: the iterates approach the degenerate endpoint c_l = 1, where rho = a y
with U = 0 solves the equations but violates the growth class; the data do not exclude other behaviour (a zero,
non-affine or non-convergent limit; compare 3.37(iv)), and no limit is claimed. A decreasing interior residual is not
evidence of a profile: the compactly supported non-profiles of 3.37(iii) have transport residual identically zero on
arbitrarily large disks at any fixed c_l > 1. Independent checks of four iterates (checker; states identified by the
first eight hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 hash of the saved state). (1) The 150-step iterate (e861227a;

inverse, multiprecision at 75 and 110 digits; sampled maxima, not bounds); for N44 a coarser complementary chart gives
9.88e-8 and misses the off-axis peak. Over N36, N40, N44 the selected maximum of |R|/N_f falls by 35 percent and then
rises by 2.9 percent, the cubic coefficients b = rho_xxy(0)/2 = -2.141, -2.152, -2.130 and e = rho_yyy(0)/6 = -5.280,
-5.212, -4.998 move, and the Frobenius norm of the degree-11 derivative tensor of R at the centre grows (5.5e9,
1.7e10, 5.5e10, against 1.4e9, 2.5e9, 5.4e9 for rho). The slopes 12.936, 14.851, 17.260, 19.204, 20.473 at N12, N16,
N20, N24, N28 (and 21.870, 22.793, 22.532, 22.078 at N32, N36, N40, N44 in the common-budget sequence) have not
stabilized. The selected canonical ratios reach 1.97e-7, 1.28e-7 and 1.32e-7 at N36, N40 and N44 while the slope still
drifts, the inverse implementation changes at N36 and the centre derivatives of R are not controlled; this shows only
that smooth functions can make these sampled ratios small. By 3.26(iii)-(iv), in the C^{1,d-1} norms of its quasimode
examples and in the far-field weighted Holder norm stated there, a small linearized residual does not control the
distance to a solution (in Sobolev norms below both thresholds 3.26(ii) gives a lower bound instead); 3.26 concerns
linear operators in those norms and says nothing about the sampled pointwise ratios of the nonlinear residuals
reported here. No larger free-c_l search was completed.

(c) Fixed-c_l chains in the smooth basis of (a) (main computation: Gauss-Newton on collocated residuals with c_l
and the far-field gauge value fixed; checker: exact rational Taylor jets of the saved coefficients, its own canonical

is the exact centre defect, b, e are the cubic coefficients of rho in physical units, the (T1) column is
[6e - (a0 - 2A) b]/(6e), and the (T2) column is (q1 - q2) - (a0 - 4A) b/(3 a0) in the notation of 3.3.

The last column is the sampled maximum over the checker's dense set (multiprecision at the maximizing point). At
c_l = 3 the sampled residual decreases with the size up to 160 x 40 and increases from 1.13e-6 to 1.54e-6 at 192 x 48
(there the sampled maximum is at (x, y) = (0.1110, 1.39e-5), near the x-axis, where |R| = 1.21e-9), while a0 increases
by 0.95, 1.11, 0.11 and 0.25 per step and the cubic coefficients grow in magnitude; both cubic defects are smallest at
128 x 32 and larger at 160 x 40 and 192 x 48, so the residual does not control them (they involve derivatives of the
residual at the centre). Precisely, for any smooth density with the parities and any stream psi = c x y + q1 x^3
y + q2 x y^3 + O(r^6) with q1 + q2 = -b/3, write R = r_01 y + r_21 x^2 y + r_03 y^3 + O(r^5); direct expansion gives
r_01 = a0 Delta, r_21 = (2A - Delta) b + 3 a0 q1 and r_03 = (2 + 3 Delta) e + a0 q2, hence 6e - (a0 - 2A) b = r_21 + 3
r_03 - Delta (9e - b) and (q1 - q2) - (a0 - 4A) b/(3 a0) = (2/(3 a0)) (r_21 + Delta b) (external analysis; confirmed
by the checker by an independent derivation with 1026 exact checks). Both cubic defects are therefore combinations of
the cubic Taylor coefficients of R and of the centre defect, which a sampled maximum of |R| does not bound. This is
not only a sampling effect (checker; confirmed in an external audit): for a0 = 4D, rho_0 = a0 y exp(-r^2), a
nonnegative smooth radial cutoff chi(r^2) equal to 1 for r <= 1/2 and to 0 for r >= 1, zeta = y r^2 chi(r^2),
1 < m < 3 and rho_eps = rho_0 + eps^m zeta(X/eps), every rho_eps has the slope a0 and the exact centre normalization
(zeta = O(r^3), and its stream is O(r^4) at 0), and sup over y != 0 of |R_eps - R_0|/N_f[rho_eps] is at most C
(eps^{m-1} + eps^{2m-2}), which tends to 0 as eps -> 0 (on r <= eps, N_f[rho_eps] >= |rho_0| >= c |y| and, by parity
and scaling, |R_eps - R_0| <= C |y| (eps^{m-1} + eps^{2m-2}); for r >= eps only delta U . grad rho_0 remains, the
stream of the perturbation there is -I eps^{m+3} x y r^{-4} with I = int_0^1 s^5 chi(s^2) ds, so |delta U| <= C
eps^{m+3} r^{-3} and |delta U_2/y| <= C eps^{m+3} r^{-4}, while rho_{0,x}/rho_0 = -2x and rho_{0,y}/rho_0 = 1/y - 2y),
while r_21 changes by 2 c_l eps^{m-3}, which tends to infinity; the example concerns residual differences, and rho_eps
is not an approximate profile. The first three sizes are not fitted by the model a0(N) = a_inf - C N^{-t} with C,
t > 0: for it the ratio of the increments 96 -> 128 and 64 -> 96 is below log(4/3)/log(3/2) = 0.7095 (the function is
concave in log N), while it is 1.166; this excludes only that model on these three sizes, not eventual convergence by
a power law with corrections or by another law. At c_l = 2.5 the sampled residual
decreases at the first refinement and increases at the last. Every centre defect is a nonzero exact rational, so no
saved state is a profile. These data neither support
convergence to a smooth profile nor identify a non-smooth limit; samples are lower estimates of suprema.

On the main computation's own sample sets (4608 to 38400 points per state) the checker's canonical evaluation gives
1.63e-5, 3.44e-6, 1.47e-6, 1.12e-6, 1.53e-6 for the five c_l = 3 sizes, close to the last column, while the main
computation's evaluator printed 1.6e-5, 3.38e-6, 8.67e-7, 6.8e-7, 5.88e-7 for the same states and points; the
difference at the three finer sizes (up to a factor 2.6) is therefore not due to the choice of points; at the six
tested maximizing points described below it arises through the stream and the velocity, while its mechanism, its
extent elsewhere and its relation to the centre Poisson defect remain undetermined. A possible source (checker): the
main computation's evaluator uses an interpolated stream,
and the stream exported at 192 x 48 does not solve the Poisson equation at low order at the centre (a defect of about
0.0099 r^2 sin 6 theta, which gives about 0.055 r^3 sin 5 theta in the transport residual, terms that the canonical
stream of a smooth density does not have); whether this defect accounts for the difference has not been determined. At
the six points where the checker's canonical evaluation attains its maxima of |R|/N_f and of |R|/N_v on the main
computation's sample sets at 128 x 32, 160 x 40 and 192 x 48, the checker evaluated the exported stream with its own
interpolation of the saved binary data (80 and 120 digits) and compared it with the canonical stream of the same
density: the velocities differ there (|delta U_2| from 1.68e-9 to 5.04e-9, |delta U_1| from 5.9e-10 to 3.24e-9), the
difference of the two residuals equals delta U_1 rho_x + delta U_2 rho_y (from 3.57e-8 to 1.02e-7 in absolute value;
the horizontal term has the opposite sign and is at most 0.06 percent of it), the interpolated stream has nonzero
Poisson defects from 2.2e-7 to 7.2e-7 at these points, and the canonical value of |R|/N_f is 3.41 to 11.50 times the
interpolated one. At these six points the two evaluations therefore differ through the velocity, that is through the
stream; this says nothing about other points or the other tables, and the mechanism (in particular the role of the
defect at the centre) is not established. For the 64 x 16 and 96 x 24 states of this chain the two evaluations agree
to within 2 percent; that agreement is not a check of the residual values reported below for other states. The
checker's whole-plane derivative ratios eta_k = ||D^k R||_2/||D^k rho||_2 (D^k collects all ordered Cartesian
derivatives of order k, and eta_3 is the quantity of 3.40) for the same five states are, for k = 2, ..., 5, smallest
at 128 x 32 among the five sizes (eta_6 is smallest at 64 x 16), and each of the five ratios increases from 128 x 32
to 160 x 40 and again to 192 x 48 (at 192 x 48: 0.0044, 0.324, 10.4, 134, 192; Gaussian quadrature at two sizes with
selected integrands recomputed at 80 and 120 digits, not an enclosure); the residual is not small relative to the
density in these derivative norms, and nothing about the regularity of a limit follows.

Decision: the runs of this subsection are stopped as a stall, with no sustained improvement of the sampled residual
over the last three sizes (1.44e-6, 1.13e-6, 1.54e-6) while a0 keeps increasing and both cubic defects grow from
128 x 32 on; this ends these runs and is not evidence that every fixed-c_l approach stalls. Restarts at 64 x 16 and
c_l = 3 (main computation; of these, only the lineage of the end point a0 = 29.56 was re-evaluated by the checker, see
below) from the constant starts rho = a0 y w(r) with a0 = 16, 18, 20 (the chain above), 22, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40 end at
a0 = 17.34, 17.74, 19.74, 29.56, 23.96, 19.30, 29.17, 31.90, 26.63, with sampled between-node maxima of |R|/N_f (the
largest of four radial-bin maxima) from 2.5e-6 to 3.8e-5. These nine runs end at substantially different slopes
depending on their starts, not monotonically in the start, and comparable sampled residuals occur at values of a0 that
differ by a factor up to 1.8; this shows a sensitivity of the algorithm, not distinct solution branches or distinct
local minima. The lowest maximum, 2.5e-6 (bin maxima 2.0e-6, 2.5e-6, 9.3e-7, 9.9e-7), belongs to the end point
a0 = 29.56, whose cubic coefficients are small (b = 0.774, e = 2.096, against -36.9, -58.1 for the chain at the same
size; this lineage has the far-field gauge value K = 11 and the chain K = 10, and the scaling from the gauge K = 11 to
the gauge K = 10 multiplies b and e by (11/10)^3, about 1.33; the reverse scaling multiplies them by (10/11)^3).
Refined at 96 x 24 and at 128 x 32 this state ends at a0 = 30.015 and 30.117, with Delta = +1.1e-7 at both sizes and
sampled maxima 3.0e-6, 3.9e-6, 9.2e-7, 8.6e-7 and 3.0e-6, 3.8e-6, 9.3e-7, 9.2e-7, not lower than at 64 x 16. The
checker re-evaluated the three states of this lineage (exact jets, canonical inverse, dense samples and multiprecision
at the sampled maxima): the sampled maxima of |R|/N_f are 2.55e-6, 3.87e-6, 3.94e-6 and (b, e) = (0.774, 2.096),
(-3.49, -12.06), (-5.56, -19.05) at 64 x 16, 96 x 24 and 128 x 32, so the small cubic coefficients at 64 x 16 do not
persist under refinement. The 96 x 24 state is not a stationary point of the truncated least-squares problem (the
projection of the collocated residual vector, in the Euclidean inner product, on the span of the left singular vectors
of the Jacobian with singular values at least 1e-13 times the largest carries 97 percent of its squared norm); this
concerns the discrete objective, not the distance to a solution of the equation. The value 30 = 6A is the number e_3
of 3.51(c) for n = 7; at A = 5 the numbers e_j of 3.51(c), over all odd n >= 3 and 1 <= j <= (n - 1)/2, are exactly
the even integers >= 10, so the closeness of a0 to one of them carries no information by itself. Whether the other end
points are local minima of the discrete problem has not been determined (the checker showed by explicit polynomial
examples that small projected residuals and barriers along straight segments do not establish it). Conditional
reading: by 3.27, 3.28 and 3.52, an exact profile of the primary class with (H-dyn) that satisfies the kernel
hypothesis of 3.27 is isolated modulo the scaling, with c_l and a0 locally determined, so a fixed-c_l chain converging
to it would have a0 settling at its value. The drift and the spread are consistent both with the absence of such a
profile at c_l = 3 and with a profile at c_l = 3 that these runs do not approach; they are not evidence for or against
a profile at c_l = 3 or at another c_l.

In the normalization of 3.72(a) (the representative with K = a0, reached from the gauge K = 10 of the chain by the
dilation rho -> l rho(X/l) of 3.5 with l = (a0/10)^{3/2}, which multiplies K by l^{2/3}), the cubic coefficients are
B = b/l^2 and E = e/(a0 l^2): B = -4.80, -12.33, -15.68, -17.69, -19.14 and E = -0.382, -1.056, -1.416, -1.607, -1.755
for the five sizes (main computation, re-gauged states; recomputed from the table in the main analysis and in an
external audit); |B| grows by a factor 4.0 while a0 grows by 12 percent, so the growth of the cubic coefficients along
the chain is not an effect of the slope normalization. In the same normalization the first x at which rho_y(x, 0)/a0
is 1/2, divided by sqrt(a0), is 1.1415, 1.1412, 1.1516, 1.1533, 1.1560 for the five sizes and the first y at which

search of the checker; these are numerically located first crossings on a fine geometric scan, refined by bisection,
and no proof excludes an earlier crossing between scan points), and the maximum of |g - g_192| over a 61 x 60 grid of

first four sizes (main computation, confirmed by an independent evaluation of the checker; maxima over the grid
points, not over the box): the normalized densities change less and less on this box while their cubic Taylor
coefficients at 0 have not stabilized at these five sizes. Here 2 A eps = 10/a0 lies between 0.451 and 0.507, so the
correction in the exact cubic identity 6E = (1 - 2A eps) B of 3.72(a) is not small: the states have 6E/B = 0.478,
0.514, 0.542, 0.545, 0.550 (the values 1 - 2A eps up to the (T1) defects of the table), against the value 1 of the
hydrostatic problem of 3.72(e).

The change from 32 to 48 angular modes at radial degree 128 raises a0 by 0.93 percent, about half of the change of the
chain from 128 x 32 to 192 x 48 (1.7 percent), and 64 modes change it by a further -0.07 percent; at 32 modes a0 is
not monotone in the radial size (22.204, 21.804, 21.957 at 96, 128, 192); the cubic coefficients change by 9 to 11
percent from 32 to 48 modes and by 6 to 7 percent from radial degree 128 to 192. Every centre defect is a nonzero exact
rational, and four of the five sampled maxima are above 1e-6. None of the five end points is converged or shown to be
stationary (the runs stopped after 10 to 52 steps, by a failed line search or a very small step). These are
observations about the attained iterates, consistent with a sensitivity to the angular truncation; they do not
separate the drift into angular and radial parts and say nothing about a limit.

Change of the compactification scale at fixed physical gauge value K = 10 (main computation; checker: canonical
inverse, dense samples and multiprecision at the sampled maxima): the 128 x 32 end point of the chain was re-expressed
on the maps with scale L = 1/2 and L = 2 (the chain uses L = 1) and the iteration was continued with at most 80 steps.
The L = 1/2 run used all 80 steps and ended at a0 = 22.067 (+1.2 percent), b = -160.80, e = -323.47, with a sampled
maximum of |R|/N_f of 1.46e-6; the L = 2 run stopped on its sixth iteration by a failed line search, after five
accepted updates, at a0 = 21.759 (-0.2 percent), b = -150.02, e = -292.96, with a sampled maximum of 1.25e-5. Neither
run recovered the collocation residual of the L = 1 end point (Euclidean norm 1.9e-3 for both, against 5.0e-4), and
both end states stay close to their re-expressed starts, so this test does not measure the dependence of a converged
state on the map; it shows only that these two changes of map did not give better end points within this budget, and
it is not the test on three domains required of a candidate.

(d) Low-slope starts (main computation; the checker evaluated two end states and computed exactly the quadratic centre
terms of q for all 24 saved states, as stated below; otherwise not independently re-evaluated; not candidates). By
3.48(a) an exact profile with 0 < a0 <= 2D needs int (rho_3)_- r^{-2} dr >= D/2. Constant starts rho = a0 y w(r) with
a0/D = 0.5, 1, 1.5 at c_l = 3 and at c_l = 1.5 were run at 64 x 16 (at most 150 steps) and continued from the end
state at 96 x 24 (at most 100 steps), with c_l fixed and with c_l released on the rebuilt map (bound c_l >= 1.02); 24
runs. With c_l fixed, the starts a0/D = 0.5 and 1 stop after 2 to 7 steps at a0 between 5.6e-4 and 1.1e-2, with
sampled bin maxima of |R|/N_f between 0.93 and 1; the starts a0/D = 1.5 leave the regime (a0/D from 6.9 to 13.6) and
stall with sampled bin maxima of |R|/N_f from 1.5e-3 to 5.8e-3. Each of the six releases at 64 x 16 leaves the regime
a0 < 2D on its first accepted step (the six continuations at 96 x 24 start outside it, and one of them, from c_l = 1.5
and a0/D = 0.5, has no accepted step, its first line search failing): from c_l = 3 the end states have c_l = 1.0277,
1.0889, 1.1569 at 64 x 16 and c_l = 1.0252, 1.0799, 1.1517 after the continuation at 96 x 24 (still moving toward the
bound), from c_l = 1.5 they reach the bound 1.02 at 64 x 16 (after 17, 46 and 75 accepted steps), with a0/D from 10.3
to 29.0 and the largest of the four bin maxima of |R|/N_f from 9.2e-6 to 2.4e-4. The checker evaluated two end states,
both from a0 = 1 at c_l = 3, with its own canonical inverse (dense samples, multiprecision at 75 and 110 digits at the
selected maxima). The fixed-c_l state at 64 x 16 has a0 = 0.00277898, centre defect Delta = 1.98180 and selected
maxima |R|/N_f = 1, |R|/N_v = 2.99942. The released state at 96 x 24 has c_l = 1.025236316, a0 = 0.622112555
(a0/D = 24.65), Delta = -1.289e-5 and selected maxima |R|/N_f = 9.0107e-6, |R|/N_v = 9.0876e-6. The main computation's
sampled bound q <= 0.9990 for the released state (radii 1e-4 to 1e6) is not a global bound: on the positive y-axis q
is a polynomial in the compactified radial variable with exact rational coefficients, and its exact value at the
radius where that variable equals 1/2048 (y about 1.33e-14) is 1 + 4.3127e-7; moreover both states have a0 > 0 and a
positive cubic coefficient e in rho(0, y) = a0 y + e y^3 + O(y^5), so q(0, y) = 1 + (e/a0) y^2 + O(y^4) > 1 for all
small y != 0 (checker, exact rational evaluation of the saved coefficients). Both centre defects are nonzero, so
neither state is an exact profile. For all 24 saved states the checker computed exactly the quadratic terms of q at
the centre, q = 1 + (b_c x^2 + e_c y^2)/(a0 ell_c^2) + O(r^4) (ell_c a length fixed by the radial map, b_c and e_c
rational combinations of the saved coefficients): e_c/a0 > 0, so that q(0, y) > 1 for all small y != 0, in 21 states,
including all 12 releases; in the other three (c_l fixed, from a0/D = 1.5: c_l = 3 at 64 x 16 and at 96 x 24,
c_l = 1.5 at 96 x 24) both b_c/a0 and e_c/a0 are negative, so q < 1 near the centre, and whether q <= 1 everywhere has
not been determined. These runs show that this solver does not stay in the regime a0 <= 2D with a small residual; they
are not evidence for or against profiles with a0 <= 2D.

4.8 Reproducibility. The accompanying artifacts contain, for each table above, the solver and evaluator sources, the
saved states and the command lines (with the recorded software versions), and, for the independent re-evaluations,
the separate implementation and its smaller result records; the run logs and the larger raw point arrays of the
checker are not included. Still missing for a candidate-level table: three
domain extents or exterior-closure tests (the compactified grid covers the whole plane, but region samples of one
compactified computation do not replace them) and three resolutions for every attempted state. Parameters and
resolution do not identify a saved state uniquely; the accompanying artifacts include a manifest of the saved states
of Section 4 with their SHA-256 hashes; in the text the four rebuilt-map iterates of 4.7(a) (e861227a, 4fa3641d,
06f24d76, 709d48d4) and six further states of 4.7(a) (c3f17dc2, 31bcc7b5, 1083cfed, 548d12fe, 777ccdba, 48d5cecb) are
identified by hash prefix, and the other states (in 4.2, 4.3, 4.5, 4.6 and the other parts of 4.7) only by their
parameters and resolution, so not every table row is tied to a saved state in the text. The tables of the attempted
states (4.2, 4.3(c)-(d), 4.5, 4.6, 4.7(a)-(d)) are also incomplete in other respects: for most rows the regional
absolute maxima of |R| with their locations, the maxima of |R|/N_v, bounds in neighbourhoods of the zeros of the
denominators and three physical domain extents are missing (for example, the absolute maximum given for the N36 state
of 4.7(b) is over a local grid, and its absolute residual is unbounded at very large radii); these tables record
attempts and are not candidate-level tables. The checker's manifest lists 20 frozen states of 4.7 (among them the 14
smooth-basis states audited exactly, the drift archives and the fixed c_l = 2.5 states) with full SHA-256 hashes, the
recorded command lines, the package versions and, for each smooth-basis state, an exact replay command for its
evaluation; an integrity check recomputed the hashes of 290 files and compared four raw-to-saved conversions exactly.
Hashes of the source code at each historical run were not recorded, so bitwise replay of the historical optimizer runs
is not available. This report does not itself contain the saved coefficients or the solver sources: the numerical
statements of Section 4 can be reproduced from the accompanying artifacts, not from the text alone. The trial states
of 4.10 have the same limitations: the text gives sampled maxima of |R_h|/N_f but no regional absolute maxima of |R_h|
with their locations. So no attempted state of Section 4 has a residual table of the completeness required for a
candidate, and the missing entries are not supplied here.

4.9 Dynamic rescaling in pseudo-time (main computation, with the parts attributed to the checker re-evaluated
independently; finite pseudo-time windows and discrete states; not evidence about existence). The time-dependent
problem rho_tau = c_w rho - (c_x X + U[rho]) . grad rho of Section 7, item 1, was integrated in the smooth basis of
4.7 with the canonical inverse at every stage, the slope normalization c_w = c_x + psi_xy(0), which keeps rho_y(0)
fixed, and a prescribed exponent, c_x = C c_w, so that a steady state with c_w > 0 gives a profile rho/c_w with
c_l = C exactly. With p = 1/C, for data rho = K r^p F(th) + o(r^p) as r -> inf whose remainder has gradient
o(r^{p-1}), and with U = o(r), these asymptotics and differentiated bounds being uniform on compact pseudo-time
intervals, the coefficient K F(th) of r^p and hence the ratio K/a0 are conserved along this flow (since c_w - p
c_x = 0), so the flow stays on one slice of the dilations of 3.5 (every profile with K/a0 > 0 has a representative on
it), and a start whose trace is proportional to sin th cannot converge to a profile with another trace in a topology
preserving the trace, although compact convergence alone is not excluded. Tests: for the manufactured pair psi = -x
y/(4 (1 + r^2)), rho = y (r^2 + 2)/(2 (1 + r^2)^2) of the checker the discrete right-hand side agrees with the exact
rho_tau to 2.6e-15 at 48 points off the grid and its cubic Taylor coefficients to 1e-11 at 64 x 16 (a test of the
unprojected generator on a field with a single angular mode), and the strain identity psi_xy(0) = -a0/4 + int_0^inf
rho_3 r^{-2} dr holds along the runs to between 1e-8 and 1e-15. Two implementation defects (a leakage of weakly
resolved coefficient directions through product-rule differentiation, and a duplicated moment routine) were found
during the computation and repaired; the numbers below are from the repaired code. (a) Constant start. From rho = y
w(r) with a0 = 1 at C = 3, the scalars c = psi_xy(0) and c_w agree across the sizes 64 x 16, 96 x 24 and 128 x 32,
three cutoffs (relative singular-value cutoffs between 1e-8 and 1e-13 in the mode-by-mode least-squares fit of the
time derivative), two bases (Chebyshev polynomials in t, and for the mode k Chebyshev polynomials of the affine image
of a subinterval [t_k, 1] onto [-1, 1]; both span the same space) and three time steps at exact output times to 7e-5
(relative) at tau = 15 and 2e-3 at tau = 20; between the 96 x 24 state at tau = 20.0470 and the 128 x 32 state at
tau = 20.0359, the ratio ||f_96 - f_128||_S / ||f_96||_S on the finite sample set S in 0.1 <= r < 1 is about 9e-5 for
the density and 5e-4 for the vertical velocity U_2 (||f||_S is the maximum of |f| over S; this comparison is from runs
made before the repair above, which left the logged scalars of this trajectory unchanged to about three digits). The
checker's evaluation of the saved states at tau = 20, with its own reconstruction of the density derivatives and its
own full-plane inverse, gives a0* = 1/c_w between 60.093 and 60.149 at 64 x 16 and between 60.107 and 60.137 at
96 x 24 over the cutoffs and bases. The annulus 1 <= r < 100 is not resolved: for the saved states at tau about 20.04
the ratios of the sampled norms of the projection defect (the part of the right-hand side not represented by the
fitted time derivative) and of the right-hand side there are 32, 11 and 3.5 percent at the nodes at the three sizes
(about 37.5, 12.2 and 4.05 percent between the nodes, by the checker), and the checker's values of the x-derivative of
rho/c_w at (6, 8) at tau = 20 are +0.223, -1.002 and -0.489 at the three sizes, so not even its sign is determined
there. c_w falls from 0.125 to 0.0166 (a0* from 8 to 60) while at tau = 20 the reported regional sampled maxima of
|R|/N_f for rho/c_w range from about 0.018 to 0.62 (checker at tau = 20: maximum in the core of |R*|, with R* the
transport residual of rho/c_w as a profile with c_l = C (equal to -rho_tau/c_w^2 for the exact time derivative), about
12.2, maximum of |R|/N_f about 0.28): no approach to a steady state is observed for tau <= 20, and the later phase is
not resolved. The coefficient b3 of the r^{2p - 1} sin 3th term of the far field agrees with the integrated law d b3/d
tau = (C - 1) c_w b3 + A1^2 (1 - p)/(4 (p + 3)) (A1 the coefficient of r^p sin th; derived by the checker for a
far-field trace proportional to sin th) to about 1.6e-4 relative or better at the reported times tau = 5, 10, 15 and
20, and the density in r > 1 contributes 62 percent of c + a0/4 at tau = 20. For C in {1.2, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6}
the tested starts, constructed from the same coefficient prescription with the physical map changing with C, show
decreasing c_w (centred logarithmic rates d(log c_w)/d tau between -0.11 and -0.14 at tau = 5 and between -0.07 and
-0.095 at tau = 10), with no arrest or reversal at the reported times. If profiles exist only at isolated values of
c_l, this flow has no steady state at a generic C, so this observed drift alone does not decide existence. (b) Starts
at the stalled states. Started at the fixed-c_l states of 4.7(c) (a0 from 19.7 to 21.9 at C = 3; c_w approximately 1,
c_x approximately 3), the flow leaves them: in an early window the core time derivative (the maximum over r <= 1 of
the absolute value of the fitted rho_tau) grows at a rate (the difference of its logarithms at the output times
nearest tau = 0.1 and tau = 0.5, divided by the actual difference of these times, some of which lie outside
[0.1, 0.5]) of 15.2 to 15.8 per unit tau at the sizes 64 x 16 to 160 x 40 (0.69 a0 to 0.78 a0; for the c_l = 2.5
states, 9.8 to 10.8, that is 0.73 a0 to 0.77 a0), stable under a change of the time step at 64 x 16 (15.49, 15.52 and
15.52 for three time steps) and dependent on the cutoff at 128 x 32 (15.5 to 18.5 for cutoffs 1e-8 to 1e-13, alike for
both bases at matched cutoff); the runs ended as follows. Of the runs at C = 3 with final time tau = 1.5, the 64 x 16
and 96 x 24 local-basis runs at cutoff 1e-8 stopped at the first nonpositive c_w step, recorded at tau = 1.1679 and
1.3705, and the 128 x 32 Chebyshev run at cutoff 1e-13 at its first nonpositive c_w step at tau = 1.4612; the 128 x 32
and 160 x 40 local-basis runs at cutoff 1e-8 were stopped by the integrator after repeated detection of a numerical
blow-up with halving of the time step, at tau = 1.3848 and 1.4215 (their last periodic outputs are at tau = 1.3501 and
1.4000), with c_w positive. The three time-step runs at 64 x 16 and the runs at 128 x 32 for the other cutoffs
(Chebyshev basis at 1e-8 and 1e-10, local basis at 1e-13), with final time tau = 1.0, and the runs from the c_l = 2.5
states, with final time 1.5, reached their final times with c_w positive at every step. In modified flows, which also
change the slope normalization: with the velocity, the strain and the rates frozen at the start (a linear transport
flow) the core derivative grows by 0.7 to 1.0 per unit tau; with the velocity evolving and the rates frozen the
departure is comparable to the full one (13.6 to 15.8); with the velocity frozen and the rates evolving it is much
weaker (0.5 to 3.8). The Jacobian compressed to the resolved coefficient directions has positive spectral abscissae
0.73 a0 to 0.78 a0 at the stalled states (one stalled background at 64 x 16 transferred to the larger grids, not three
separately refined stalled states), increasing with N at three sizes with no limit established (0.19 to 0.30 per unit
tau without the velocity of the perturbation), and 0.47 a0 to 0.53 a0 at the constant start; an independent
compression of the checker agrees to about 0.3 to 2 percent in the tested cases. The relative residuals
|J v - lambda v|/(|Re lambda| |v|) of the lifted eigenpairs (J the full discrete Jacobian, v the lift of an
eigenvector of the compressed Jacobian; norms of the kappa- and density fields) are 0.4 to 9; finite amplification is
seen in direct linear integration (12.7 to 14.7 per unit tau for lifted and random vectors), and the nonlinear
response to two prescribed perturbations is within about 0.1 to 1.1 percent of the prediction of the frozen
linearization (the Jacobian of the discrete right-hand side at the initial state) over tau about 0.3 for perturbation
sizes 1e-3 to 1e-7 (1.6 and 2.6 percent at size 1e-2), with small-perturbation plateaus of about 1.054 and 0.1042
percent over the tested perturbation sizes (a comparison with the frozen linearization over a short window, not with
the variational equation along the moving background). No converged eigenmode of the full discrete or of the continuum
linearization is demonstrated, and no instability of the continuum problem is certified.
(c) Interpretation (not a proof). The ablations are consistent with a contribution to the departure from the velocity
feedback -U[h] . grad rho on the core, where rho_y > 0; for a constant gradient a0 > 0 the local symbol of this term
in pseudo-time is a0 k_1^2/|k|^2 >= 0. If exact profiles with a0* much larger than 1 had such an instability (a
hypothesis; the stalled states are not shown to be near profiles), forward integration would reach them only from
their stable set. This concerns the tested forward integrations and starts; it does not show that every use of the
flow to find candidates fails. The saved states and the sources are in the accompanying artifacts (the run logs are
not).

4.10 Least-squares trial states for the hydrostatic problem (main computation; the independent evaluations of the
checker and its consistency checks are distinguished in the Scope paragraph of this item; finite discrete trial
states; not evidence about existence). Computed. In the frame of 3.72 (x = sqrt(a0) xi, rho = a0 g, psi = sqrt(a0)
Phi) the hydrostatic problem (c xi + V_1) g_xi + (c y + V_2) g_y = g, with V_1 = -int_y^inf g_xi dt, V_2 = int_0^y t
g_xixi dt + y int_y^inf g_xixi dt, g_y(0) = 1 and the y-axis tail g(0, y) ~ K y^{1/c} (K = 1), was discretized in the
smooth radial-angular basis of 4.7 with radial map exponent P = c/(c - 1), which fixes the axis tail exponent
1 - 1/P = 1/c. The inverse was evaluated by Gauss quadrature with g_xixi by central differences (validated on the
manufactured field g = exp(-xi^2) y exp(-y^2): V_1 to 3e-15, V_2 to 2e-10; a fixed step of 1e-5 is round-off dominated
where g is large, so the c = 1.5 runs are not used; a radius-scaled step was added), and the collocation rows at the
radial nodes times the quadrant angles plus the normalization rows g_y(0) = 1 and K = 1 were solved by Gauss-Newton
least squares (SVD steps keeping singular values above 1e-13 of the largest) at c = 3 (48 x 12 to 128 x 32) and c = 2
(64 x 16 to 224 x 56), from the simple start g = y (1 + r^2)^{(1/c - 1)/2} and from the re-gauged stalled states of
4.7, with c fixed or free (the map stays fixed, so exact axis transport forces c = c_start: a fixed-tail-exponent
experiment, not a test of selection), with collocated or angularly oversampled rows, and with the centre condition
c + int_0^inf g_xixi(0, t) dt = 1 of 3.72(e) dropped or imposed as a row (a finite-difference row, or an exact
polynomial primitive of the inverse on the axis derived by the checker and implemented independently in the main
computation: on the two centre-kept states at c = 3 and on the free-c kept state the two implementations differ by
8.5e-13, 7.0e-13 and 7.5e-13, on the oversampled kept state by 9.5e-10, and for the four collocated states at c = 3
the comparison was made with values rounded to four digits and agrees within that rounding). Below, R_h := (c
xi + V_1) g_xi + (c y + V_2) g_y - g and N_f := |(c xi + V_1) g_xi| + |(c y + V_2) g_y| + |g| are the analogues of R
and N_f of Section 2. Measured. The reported c = 2, 3 trials end in Gauss-Newton stalls (the line search fails),
except three runs at c = 2, stated below, that end at iteration caps (two at 128 x 32 and one at 96 x 24 with the
refined rule defined below) and two runs at c = 2 with that rule, also stated below, without a saved endpoint (one
interrupted and one stopped during setup by the memory of the device). At c = 3 the node residuals (the largest
absolute entry of the unweighted residual vector: R_h at the collocation points and the normalization rows, with the
centre row when it is imposed; not divided by N_f) are 1.7e-4, 5.9e-7, 1.1e-7, 7.7e-7 (48 .. 128; not monotone); the
between-node maxima of |R_h|/N_f, including vertical-axis sample angles, are 9.5e-3, 8.6e-3, 1.9e-3, 3.1e-3 in
1 <= r < 100 and 6.3e-3, 1.3e-2, 1.1e-3, 4.5e-3 for 100 <= r <= r_max with r_max = 7.5e3, 1.7e4, 5.9e4, 1.4e5 (the

unprojected dilation is a null direction of the PDE residual at an exact solution; this does not make its finite

at c = 3, with normalized gradient |J_h^T F|/(s_max |F|) = 8e-4 to 3.5e-3: the predicted fractional decrease of |F|^2
for the undamped linearized step restricted to the kept singular directions is the square of the kept fraction, 5e-6,
5e-5 and 7e-5; the states are approximately stationary in this sense only, not declared stationary points or minima,
and whether the dropped part could be removed by order-one changes of the field was not measured. Scope. All saved

reproduced these exported arrays bit for bit for the 21 earlier states; derived arrays involve rounding); the checker
confirmed every number of this item against the sources and run logs, and evaluated the residual maxima and centre
values of the earlier states independently as stated above, while the linearization data (singular values, dilation
